verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Devoted Dedication</vt>
सर्ववेदान्तसिद्धान्तगोचरं तमगोचरम् ।
गोविन्दं परमानन्दं सद्गुरुं प्रणतोऽस्म्यहम् ॥१॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Devoted Dedication</vt>
sarvavedāntasiddhāntagocaraṃ tamagocaram |
govindaṃ paramānandaṃ sadguruṃ praṇato'smyaham || 1 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Devoted Dedication</vt>
sarva vedaanta siddhaanta gocaram tam agocaram |
govindam param aanandam sadgurum pranato smi aham || 1 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I bow to Govinda, the Satguru, whose very nature is Supreme Bliss, who is beyond the reach of speech and mind, and who can be known only through the meaning of all Vedanta.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Glory of Spiritual Life</vt>
जन्तूनां नरजन्म दुर्लभमतः पुंस्त्वं ततो विप्रता तस्माद्वैदिकधर्ममार्गपरता विद्वत्त्वमस्मात्परम् ।
आत्मानात्मविवेचनं स्वनुभवो ब्रह्मात्मना संस्थितिः मुक्तिर्नो शतजन्मकोटिसुकृतैः पुण्यैर्विना लभ्यते ॥२॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Glory of Spiritual Life</vt>
jantūnāṃ narajanma durlabhamataḥ puṃstvaṃ tato vipratā tasmādvaidikadharmamārgaparatā vidvattvamasmātparam |
ātmānātmavivecanaṃ svanubhavo brahmātmanā saṃsthitiḥ muktirno śatajanmakoṭisukṛtaiḥ puṇyairvinā labhyate || 2 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Glory of Spiritual Life</vt>
jantuunaam nara janma durlabham atah pumstvam tato viprataa tasmaat vaidika dharma maarga parataa vidvattvam asmaat param |
aatmaa anaatma vivecanam sva anubhavo brahma aatmanaa samsthitih muktir no shata janma koti sukritaih punyair vinaa labhyate || 2 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For any being, a human birth is hard to gain, a male body harder still. Brahminhood is rarer than that, and rarer again is commitment to the path of Vedic religion. Beyond this comes scholarship in the scriptures. After it, in order, come discrimination between the Self and the not-Self, Realisation, and remaining in identity with Brahman. Mukti (Liberation) of this kind cannot be reached without the hard-earned merit of a hundred crore of births.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Unique Graces in Life</vt>
दुर्लभं त्रयमेवैतद्देवानुग्रहहेतुकम् ।
मनुष्यत्वं मुमुक्षुत्वं महापुरुषसंश्रयः ॥ ३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Unique Graces in Life</vt>
durlabhaṃ trayamevaitaddevānugrahahetukam |
manuṣyatvaṃ mumukṣutvaṃ mahāpuruṣasaṃśrayaḥ || 3 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Unique Graces in Life</vt>
durlabham trayam eva etat deva anugraha hetukam |
manushyatvam mumukshutvam mahaa purusha samshrayah || 3 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Three things are truly rare and come only by the grace of God: a human birth, the longing for Liberation, and the protective care of a perfected sage.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Miseries of The Unspiritual Man</vt>
लब्ध्वा कथंचिन्नरजन्म दुर्लभं तत्रापि पुंस्त्वं श्रुतिपारदर्शनम् ।
यस्त्वात्ममुक्तौ न यतेत मूढधीः स ह्यात्महा स्वं विनिहन्त्यसद्ग्रहात् ॥ ४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Miseries of The Unspiritual Man</vt>
labdhvā kathaṃcinnarajanma durlabhaṃ tatrāpi puṃstvaṃ śrutipāradarśanam |
yastvātmamuktau na yateta mūḍhadhīḥ sa hyātmahā svaṃ vinihantyasadgrahāt || 4 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Miseries of The Unspiritual Man</vt>
labdhvaa kathamchin nara janma durlabham tatraapi pumstvam shruti paara darshanam |
yah tu aatma muktau na yateta muudha dhiih sah hi aatma haa svam vinihanti asad grahaat || 4 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Suppose someone has somehow gained a human birth, a male body, and mastery of the Vedas as well, and is still foolish enough to make no effort toward self-liberation. That person is committing suicide, destroying himself by clinging to what is unreal.

verses.sanskrit:
इतः को न्वस्ति मूढात्मा यस्तु स्वार्थे प्रमाद्यति ।
दुर्लभं मानुषं देहं प्राप्य तत्रापि पौरुषम् ॥ ५ ॥
verses.roman:
itaḥ ko nvasti mūḍhātmā yastu svārthe pramādyati |
durlabhaṃ mānuṣaṃ dehaṃ prāpya tatrāpi pauruṣam || 5 ||
verses.colloquial:
itah kah nu asti muudha aatmaa yah tu sva arthe pramaadyati |
durlabham maanusham deham praapya tatraapi paurusham || 5 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Who could be a greater fool than one who gains a rare human body, a masculine one at that, and then fails to pursue the true purpose of this life?

verses.sanskrit:
वदन्तु शास्त्राणि यजन्तु देवान् कुर्वन्तु कर्माणि भजन्तु देवताः ।
आत्मैक्यबोधेन विनापि मुक्तिः न सिध्यति ब्रह्मशतान्तरेऽपि ॥ ६ ॥
verses.roman:
vadantu śāstrāṇi yajantu devān kurvantu karmāṇi bhajantu devatāḥ |
ātmaikyabodhena vināpi muktiḥ na sidhyati brahmaśatāntare'pi || 6 ||
verses.colloquial:
vadantu shaastraani yajantu devaan kurvantu karmaani bhajantu devataah |
aatma aikya bodhena vinaa api muktih na sidhyati brahma shata antare api || 6 ||
verses.translation_reworded: People may cite the Scriptures and sacrifice to the gods; they may carry out rituals and worship the deities. Yet without realising one's identity with the Ātman there is no Liberation, not even in a span equal to the lifetimes of a hundred Brahmas combined.

verses.sanskrit:
अमृतत्वस्य नाशास्ति वित्तेनेत्येव हि श्रुतिः ।
ब्रवीति कर्मणो मुक्तेरहेतुत्वं स्फुटं यतः ॥ ७ ॥
verses.roman:
amṛtatvasya nāśāsti vittenetyeva hi śrutiḥ |
bravīti karmaṇo mukterahetutvaṃ sphuṭaṃ yataḥ || 7 ||
verses.colloquial:
amritatvasya na aashaa asti vittena iti eva hi shrutih |
braviiti karmanah mukteh ahetutvam sphutam yatah || 7 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Vedas plainly state that wealth offers no hope of immortality. It follows clearly that works cannot bring about Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Means of Wisdom</vt>
अतो विमुक्त्यै प्रयतेत्विद्वान् संन्यस्तबाह्यार्थसुखस्पृहः सन् ।
सन्तं महान्तं समुपेत्य देशिकं तेनोपदिष्टार्थसमाहितात्मा ॥ ८ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Means of Wisdom</vt>
ato vimuktyai prayatetvidvān saṃnyastabāhyārthasukhaspṛhaḥ san |
santaṃ mahāntaṃ samupetya deśikaṃ tenopadiṣṭārthasamāhitātmā || 8 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Means of Wisdom</vt>
atah vimuktyai prayateta vidvaan samnyasta baahya artha sukha spriha san |
santam mahaantam samupetya deshikam tena upadishta artha samaahita aatmaa || 8 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The learned person should therefore give up the wish for pleasure from outer objects, properly approach a good and generous teacher, fix the mind on the truth that teacher imparts, and strive with all his strength for Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
उद्धरेदात्मनात्मानं मग्नं संसारवारिधौ ।
योगारूढत्वमासाद्य सम्यग्दर्शननिष्ठया ॥ ९ ॥
verses.roman:
uddharedātmanātmānaṃ magnaṃ saṃsāravāridhau |
yogārūḍhatvamāsādya samyagdarśananiṣṭhayā || 9 ||
verses.colloquial:
uddharet aatmanaa aatmaanam magnam samsaara vaaridhaau |
yoga aaruudhatvam aasaadya samyag darshana nishthayaa || 9 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Having reached the Yogārūḍha state, one should rescue oneself, sunk as one is in the sea of birth and death, through devotion to right discrimination.

verses.sanskrit:
संन्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि भवबन्धविमुक्तये ।
यत्यतां पण्डितैर्धीरैरात्माभ्यास उपस्थितैः ॥ १0 ॥
verses.roman:
saṃnyasya sarvakarmāṇi bhavabandhavimuktaye |
yatyatāṃ paṇḍitairdhīrairātmābhyāsa upasthitaiḥ || 10 ||
verses.colloquial:
samnyasya sarva karmaani bhava bandha vimuktaye |
yatyataam panditaih dhiiraih aatma abhyaase upasthitaih || 10 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Once the wise and learned person has begun the practice of realising the Ātman, he should give up all works and work to sever the bonds of birth and death.

verses.sanskrit:
चित्तस्य शुद्धये कर्म न तु वस्तूपलब्धये ।
वस्तुसिद्धिर्विचारेण न किंचित्कर्मकोटिभिः ॥ ११ ॥
verses.roman:
cittasya śuddhaye karma na tu vastūpalabdhaye |
vastusiddhirvicāreṇa na kiṃcitkarmakoṭibhiḥ || 11 ||
verses.colloquial:
chittasya shuddhaye karma na tu vastu upalabdhaye |
vastu siddhir vicaarena na kimchit karma kotibhih || 11 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Work purifies the mind but does not reveal Reality. Truth is realised through discrimination, and ten million acts will not accomplish it in the least.

verses.sanskrit:
सम्यग्विचारतः सिद्धा रज्जुतत्त्वावधारणा ।
भ्रान्तोदितमहासर्पभयदुःखविनाशिनी ॥ १२ ॥
verses.roman:
samyagvicārataḥ siddhā rajjutattvāvadhāraṇā |
bhrāntoditamahāsarpabhayaduḥkhavināśinī || 12 ||
verses.colloquial:
samyag vicaaratah siddhaa rajju tattva avadhaaranaa |
bhraanta udita mahaa sarpa bhaya duhkha vinaashinii || 12 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Sound reasoning produces certainty about what the rope really is, and this ends the great fear and misery caused by the snake conjured up in the deluded mind.

verses.sanskrit:
अर्थस्य निश्चयो दृष्टो विचारेण हितोक्तितः ।
न स्नानेन न दानेन प्राणायमशतेन वा ॥ १३ ॥
verses.roman:
arthasya niścayo dṛṣṭo vicāreṇa hitoktitaḥ |
na snānena na dānena prāṇāyamaśatena vā || 13 ||
verses.colloquial:
arthasya nishchayo drishto vicaarena hita uktitah |
na snaanena na daanena praanaayaama shatena vaa || 13 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Certainty about the Truth is seen to arise from reflecting on the beneficial advice of the wise. It does not come from bathing in sacred waters, from giving gifts, or from hundreds of Prāṇāyāmas (exercises controlling the vital force).

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Fit Student</vt>
अधिकारिणमाशास्ते फलसिद्धिर्विशेषतः ।
उपाया देशकालाद्याः सन्त्यस्मिन्सहकारिणः ॥ १४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Fit Student</vt>
adhikāriṇamāśāste phalasiddhirviśeṣataḥ |
upāyā deśakālādyāḥ santyasminsahakāriṇaḥ || 14 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Fit Student</vt>
adhikaarinaam aashaaste phala siddhir visheshatah |
upaayaa desha kaala aadyaah santi asmin sahaakaarinah || 14 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Success depends above all on the aspirant being qualified. Time, place, and similar means only assist in this.

verses.sanskrit:
अतो विचारः कर्तव्यो जिज्ञासोरात्मवस्तुनः ।
समासाद्य दयासिन्धुं गुरुं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमम् ॥ १५ ॥
verses.roman:
ato vicāraḥ kartavyo jijñāsorātmavastunaḥ |
samāsādya dayāsindhuṃ guruṃ brahmaviduttamam || 15 ||
verses.colloquial:
atah vicaarah kartavyo jijnaasoh aatma vastunah |
samaasaadya dayaa sindhum gurum brahma vid uttamam || 15 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So the one who seeks the Reality of the Ātman should properly approach a Guru, the finest among the knowers of Brahman and an ocean of mercy, and then take up reasoning.

verses.sanskrit:
मेधावी पुरुषो विद्वानुहापोहविचक्षणः ।
अधिकार्यात्मविद्यायामुक्तलक्षणलक्षितः ॥ १६ ॥
verses.roman:
medhāvī puruṣo vidvānuhāpohavicakṣaṇaḥ |
adhikāryātmavidyāyāmuktalakṣaṇalakṣitaḥ || 16 ||
verses.colloquial:
medhaavii purushoh vidvaan uhaa apoha vicakshanah |
adhikaaree aatma vidyaayaam ukta lakshana lakshitah || 16 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A person who is intelligent and learned, skilled at arguing for the Scriptures and at refuting arguments against them, and who has the qualities described above, is a fit recipient of the knowledge of the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
विवेकिनो विरक्तस्य शमादिगुणशालिनः ।
मुमुक्षोरेव हि ब्रह्मजिज्ञासायोग्यता मता ॥ १७ ॥
verses.roman:
vivekino viraktasya śamādiguṇaśālinaḥ |
mumukṣoreva hi brahmajijñāsāyogyatā matā || 17 ||
verses.colloquial:
vivekinah viraktasya shama aadi guna shaalinah |
mumukshoh eva hi brahma jijnaasaa yogyataa mataa || 17 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only someone who distinguishes the Real from the unreal, whose mind has turned away from the unreal, who has calmness and the virtues that go with it, and who longs for Liberation, is regarded as qualified to inquire into Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Four Qualifications</vt>
साधनान्यत्र चत्वारि कथितानि मनीषिभिः ।
येषु सत्स्वेव सन्निष्ठा यदभावे न सिध्यति ॥ १८ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Four Qualifications</vt>
sādhanānyatra catvāri kathitāni manīṣibhiḥ |
yeṣu satsveva sanniṣṭhā yadabhāve na sidhyati || 18 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Four Qualifications</vt>
saadhanaan yatra chatvaari kathitaani maniishibhih |
yeshu satsu eva san nishthaa yad abhaave na sidhyati || 18 ||
verses.translation_reworded: On this subject, sages speak of four means of attainment. When they are present, devotion to Brahman succeeds; when they are absent, it fails.

verses.sanskrit:
आदौ नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः परिगम्यते ।
इहामुत्रफलभोगविरागस्तदनन्तरम् शमादिषट्कसम्पत्तिर्मुमुक्षुत्वमिति स्फुटम् ॥ १९ ॥
verses.roman:
ādau nityānityavastuvivekaḥ parigamyate |
ihāmutraphalabhogavirāgastadanantaram śamādiṣaṭkasampattirmumukṣutvamiti sphuṭam || 19 ||
verses.colloquial:
aadau nitya anitya vastu vivekah parigamyate |
iha amutra phala bhoga viraagah tad anantaram shama aadi shatka sampattih mumukshutvam iti sphutam || 19 ||
verses.translation_reworded: First on the list is discrimination between the Real and the unreal. Next is aversion to enjoying the fruits of one's actions, both in this life and the next. Then comes the group of six attributes, calmness and the rest. Last, plainly, is the yearning for Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्म सत्यं जगन्मिथ्येत्येवंरूपो विनिश्चयः ।
सोऽयं नित्यानित्यवस्तुविवेकः समुदाहृतः ॥ २0 ॥
verses.roman:
brahma satyaṃ jaganmithyetyevaṃrūpo viniścayaḥ |
so'yaṃ nityānityavastuvivekaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ || 20 ||
verses.colloquial:
brahma satyam jagat mithyaa iti evam ruupah vinishchayah |
sah ayam nitya anitya vastu vivekah samudaahritah || 20 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The mind's firm conviction that Brahman is real and the universe unreal is what is called discrimination (Viveka) between the Real and the unreal.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वैराग्यं जिहासा या दर्शनश्रवणादिभिः ।
देहादिब्रह्मपर्यन्ते ह्यनित्ये भोगवस्तुनि ॥ २१ ॥
verses.roman:
tadvairāgyaṃ jihāsā yā darśanaśravaṇādibhiḥ |
dehādibrahmaparyante hyanitye bhogavastuni || 21 ||
verses.colloquial:
tat vairaagyam jihaasaa yaa darshana shravaana aadibhih |
deha aadi brahma paryante hi anitye bhoga vastuni || 21 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Vairāgya, or renunciation, is the wish to give up every passing enjoyment, from those of an animate body up to those of Brahmāhood, their defects having already been learned through observation, instruction, and the like.

verses.sanskrit:
विरज्य विषयव्राताद्दोषदृष्ट्या मुहुर्मुहुः ।
स्वलक्ष्ये नियतावस्था मनसः शम उच्यते ॥ २२ ॥
verses.roman:
virajya viṣayavrātāddoṣadṛṣṭyā muhurmuhuḥ |
svalakṣye niyatāvasthā manasaḥ śama ucyate || 22 ||
verses.colloquial:
virajya vishaya vraataat dosha drishtayaa muhur muhuh |
sva lakshye niyata avasthaa manasah shama uchyate || 22 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Śama, or calmness, is the mind resting firmly on its Goal (Brahman) after it has pulled away from the many sense objects by repeatedly noticing their defects.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयेभ्यः परावर्त्य स्थापनं स्वस्वगोलके ।
उभयेषामिन्द्रियाणां स दमः परिकीर्तितः बाह्यानालम्बनं वृत्तेरेषोपरतिरुत्तमा ॥ २३ ॥
verses.roman:
viṣayebhyaḥ parāvartya sthāpanaṃ svasvagolake |
ubhayeṣāmindriyāṇāṃ sa damaḥ parikīrtitaḥ bāhyānālambanaṃ vṛttereṣoparatiruttamā || 23 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishayebhyah paraavartya sthaapanam svasva golake |
ubhayesham indriyaanaam sah damah parikirtitah baahya anaalambanam vrittih esha uparatih uttamaa || 23 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Dama, or self-control, is turning both kinds of sense organs away from sense objects and settling them in their own centres. The best Uparati, or self-withdrawal, is when the mind's activity no longer operates through external objects.

verses.sanskrit:
सहनं सर्वदुःखानामप्रतीकारपूर्वकम् ।
चिन्ताविलापरहितं सा तितिक्षा निगद्यते ॥ २४ ॥
verses.roman:
sahanaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāmapratīkārapūrvakam |
cintāvilāparahitaṃ sā titikṣā nigadyate || 24 ||
verses.colloquial:
sahanam sarva duhkhaanaam apratiikaara puurvakam |
chintaa vilaapa rahitam saa titikshaa nigadyate || 24 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Titikṣā, or forbearance, is enduring all afflictions without seeking to remedy them, while staying free of anxiety or lament about them.

verses.sanskrit:
शास्त्रस्य गुरुवाक्यस्य सत्यबुद्ध्यवधारणम् ।
सा श्रद्धा कथिता सद्भिर्यया वस्तूपलभ्यते ॥ २५ ॥
verses.roman:
śāstrasya guruvākyasya satyabuddhyavadhāraṇam |
sā śraddhā kathitā sadbhiryayā vastūpalabhyate || 25 ||
verses.colloquial:
shaastrasya guru vaakyasya satya buddhyaa avadhaaranam |
saa shraddhaa kathitaa sadbhih yayaa vastu upalabhyate || 25 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Sages use the word Śraddhā, or faith, for firmly judging to be true what the Scriptures and the Guru teach. Through it Reality is perceived.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वदा स्थापनं बुद्धेः शुद्धे ब्रह्मणि सर्वदा ।
तत्समाधानमित्युक्तं न तु चित्तस्य लालनम् ॥ २६ ॥
verses.roman:
sarvadā sthāpanaṃ buddheḥ śuddhe brahmaṇi sarvadā |
tatsamādhānamityuktaṃ na tu cittasya lālanam || 26 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarvadaa sthaapanam buddheh shuddhe brahmani sarvadaa |
tat samaadhaanam iti uktam na tu chittasya laalanam || 26 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Samādhāna, or self-settledness, is the constant focusing of the intellect (the affirming faculty) on the ever-pure Brahman. It is not merely letting thought indulge its curiosity.

verses.sanskrit:
अहंकारादिदेहान्तान् बन्धानज्ञानकल्पितान् ।
स्वस्वरूपावबोधेन मोक्तुमिच्छा मुमुक्षुता ॥ २७ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃkārādidehāntān bandhānajñānakalpitān |
svasvarūpāvabodhena moktumicchā mumukṣutā || 27 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahankkaara aadi deha antaan bandhaan ajnaana kalpitaan |
sva svaruupa avabodena moktum ichchhaa mumukshutaa || 27 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Mumukṣutā, or yearning for Freedom, is the wish to be released, by realising one's true nature, from every bondage imposed by Ignorance, from egoism down to the body.

verses.sanskrit:
मन्दमध्यमरूपापि वैराग्येण शमादिना ।
प्रसादेन गुरोः सेयं प्रवृद्धा सूयते फलम् ॥ २८ ॥
verses.roman:
mandamadhyamarūpāpi vairāgyeṇa śamādinā |
prasādena guroḥ seyaṃ pravṛddhā sūyate phalam || 28 ||
verses.colloquial:
manda madhyama ruupaa api vairaagyena shama adinaa |
prasaadena guroh saa iyam pravriddhaa suuyate phalam || 28 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Even when dull or only moderate, this yearning for Freedom can bear fruit by the Guru's grace, as it is developed through Vairāgya (renunciation), Śama (calmness), and the rest.

verses.sanskrit:
वैराग्यं च मुमुक्षुत्वं तीव्रं यस्य तु विद्यते ।
तस्मिन्नेवार्थवन्तः स्युः फलवन्तः शमादयः ॥ २९ ॥
verses.roman:
vairāgyaṃ ca mumukṣutvaṃ tīvraṃ yasya tu vidyate |
tasminnevārthavantaḥ syuḥ phalavantaḥ śamādayaḥ || 29 ||
verses.colloquial:
vairaagyam cha mumukshutvam tiivram yasya tu vidyate |
tasmin eva artha vantah syuh phala vantah shama aadayah || 29 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is only in the person whose renunciation and yearning for Freedom are intense that calmness and the other practices have real meaning and bear fruit.

verses.sanskrit:
एतयोर्मन्दता यत्र विरक्तत्वमुमुक्षयोः ।
मरौ सलीलवत्तत्र शमादेर्भानमात्रता ॥ ३0 ॥
verses.roman:
etayormandatā yatra viraktatvamumukṣayoḥ |
marau salīlavattatra śamāderbhānamātratā || 30 ||
verses.colloquial:
etayoh mandataa yatra viraktatva mumukshayoh |
marau salila vat tatra shama aadeh bhaana maatrataa || 30 ||
verses.translation_reworded: But where renunciation and yearning for Freedom are dull, calmness and the other practices are mere appearances, like water seen in a desert.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Bhakti - Firm and Deep</vt>
मोक्षकारणसामग्र्यां भक्तिरेव गरीयसी ।
स्वस्वरूपानुसन्धानं भक्तिरित्यभिधीयते ॥ ३१ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Bhakti - Firm and Deep</vt>
mokṣakāraṇasāmagryāṃ bhaktireva garīyasī |
svasvarūpānusandhānaṃ bhaktirityabhidhīyate || 31 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Bhakti - Firm and Deep</vt>
moksha kaarana saamagryaam bhaktir eva gariiasii |
sva svaruupa anu sandhanam bhaktir iti abhidhiiyate || 31 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Of all that helps toward Liberation, devotion (Bhakti) stands highest. Seeking one's real nature is what is called devotion.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Courtesy of Approach and Questioning</vt>
स्वात्मतत्त्वानुसन्धानं भक्तिरित्यपरे जगुः ।
उक्तसाधनसंपन्नस्तत्त्वजिज्ञासुरात्मनः उपसीदेद्गुरुं प्राज्ञ्यं यस्माद्बन्धविमोक्षणम् ॥ ३२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Courtesy of Approach and Questioning</vt>
svātmatattvānusandhānaṃ bhaktirityapare jaguḥ |
uktasādhanasaṃpannastattvajijñāsurātmanaḥ upasīdedguruṃ prājñyaṃ yasmādbandhavimokṣaṇam || 32 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Courtesy of Approach and Questioning</vt>
sva aatma tattva anusandhanam bhaktir iti apare jaguh |
ukta saadhana sampannah tattva jijnaasuh aatmanah upasiidet gurum praajnam yasmaat bandha vimokshanam || 32 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Others hold that inquiry into the truth of one's own self is devotion. One who inquires into the truth of the Ātman and has the means of attainment described above should go to a wise teacher who grants release from bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रोत्रियोऽवृजिनोऽकामहतो यो ब्रह्मवित्तमः ।
ब्रह्मण्युपरतः शान्तो निरिन्धन इवानलः अहेतुकदयासिन्धुर्बन्धुरानमतां सताम् ॥ ३३ ॥
verses.roman:
śrotriyo'vṛjino'kāmahato yo brahmavittamaḥ |
brahmaṇyuparataḥ śānto nirindhana ivānalaḥ ahetukadayāsindhurbandhurānamatāṃ satām || 33 ||
verses.colloquial:
shrotriyah avrijinah akaama hatah yo brahma vittamah |
brahmani uparatah shaantah nir indhana iva analah ahetuka dayaa sindhuh bandhuh aanamantaam sataam || 33 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Such a teacher is versed in the Vedas, sinless, untouched by desire, and a supreme knower of Brahman. He has withdrawn into Brahman and is calm, like a fire that has burned up its fuel. He is a limitless reservoir of causeless mercy and a friend to all good people who bow before him.

verses.sanskrit:
तमाराध्य गुरुं भक्त्या प्रह्वप्रश्रयसेवनैः ।
प्रसन्नं तमनुप्राप्य पृच्छेज्ज्ञातव्यमात्मनः ॥ ३४ ॥
verses.roman:
tamārādhya guruṃ bhaktyā prahvapraśrayasevanaiḥ |
prasannaṃ tamanuprāpya pṛcchejjñātavyamātmanaḥ || 34 ||
verses.colloquial:
tam aaraadhy a gurum bhaktyaa prahva prashhraya sevanaih |
prasannam tam anu praapya prichchhej jnaatavyam aatmanah || 34 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Worshipping that Guru with devotion and approaching him, once he has been pleased by prostration, humility, and service, the seeker should ask him what he needs to know:

verses.sanskrit:
स्वामिन्नमस्ते नतलोकबन्धो कारुण्यसिन्धो पतितं भवाब्धौ ।
मामुद्धरात्मीयकटाक्षदृष्ट्या ऋज्व्यातिकारुण्यसुधाभिवृष्ट्या ॥ ३५ ॥
verses.roman:
svāminnamaste natalokabandho kāruṇyasindho patitaṃ bhavābdhau |
māmuddharātmīyakaṭākṣadṛṣṭyā ṛjvyātikāruṇyasudhābhivṛṣṭyā || 35 ||
verses.colloquial:
svaaamin namaste nata loka bandho kaarunya sindho patitam bhava abdhau |
maam uddhar aatmiiya kataaksha drishtayaa rijvyaa ati kaarunya sudhaa abhivrishtayaa || 35 ||
verses.translation_reworded: O Master, friend of those who bow to you, ocean of mercy, I bow to you. I have fallen into this sea of birth and death. Rescue me with a direct glance of your eye, which pours out supreme, nectar-like grace.

verses.sanskrit:
दुर्वारसंसारदवाग्नितप्तं दोधूयमानं दुरदृष्टवातैः ।
भीतं प्रपन्नं परिपाहि मृत्योः शरण्यमन्यद्यदहं न जाने ॥ ३६ ॥
verses.roman:
durvārasaṃsāradavāgnitaptaṃ dodhūyamānaṃ duradṛṣṭavātaiḥ |
bhītaṃ prapannaṃ paripāhi mṛtyoḥ śaraṇyamanyadyadahaṃ na jāne || 36 ||
verses.colloquial:
dur vaara samsaara dava agni taptam dodhuu yamaanm dur adrishta vaataih |
bhiitam prapannam paripaahi mrityoh sharanyam anyad yad aham na jaane || 36 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Save me from death. I am scorched by the unquenchable fire of this world-forest and violently shaken by the winds of an adverse fate. Terrified, I seek refuge in you, for I know of no one else who can shelter me.

verses.sanskrit:
शान्ता महान्तो निवसन्ति सन्तो वसन्तवल्लोकहितं चरन्तः ।
तीर्णाः स्वयं भीमभवार्णवं जनान् अहेतुनान् यानपि तारयन्तः ॥ ३७ ॥
verses.roman:
śāntā mahānto nivasanti santo vasantavallokahitaṃ carantaḥ |
tīrṇāḥ svayaṃ bhīmabhavārṇavaṃ janān ahetunān yānapi tārayantaḥ || 37 ||
verses.colloquial:
shaantaa mahaanto nivasanti santo vasanta val loka hitam charantah |
tiirnah svayam bhiima bhava arnavaam janaan ahetunaa yaan api taarayantah || 37 ||
verses.translation_reworded: There are good souls, calm and generous, who benefit others as the spring season does. Having crossed this terrible ocean of birth and death themselves, they help others cross it too, with no motive at all.

verses.sanskrit:
अयं स्वभावः स्वत एव यत्पर श्रमापनोदप्रवणं महात्मनाम् ।
सुधांशुरेष स्वयमर्ककर्कश प्रभाभितप्तामवति क्षितिं किल ॥ ३८ ॥
verses.roman:
ayaṃ svabhāvaḥ svata eva yatpara śramāpanodapravaṇaṃ mahātmanām |
sudhāṃśureṣa svayamarkakarkaśa prabhābhitaptāmavati kṣitiṃ kila || 38 ||
verses.colloquial:
ayam svabhaavah svata eva yat para shrama apanoda pravanam mahaatmanaam |
sudhaa amshu esha svayam arka karkasha prabhaa abhitaptaam avati kshitim kila || 38 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is the very nature of the generous to set about relieving the troubles of others of their own accord. Take the moon: as everyone knows, it freely rescues the earth when it is parched by the sun's blazing rays.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मानन्दरसानुभूतिकलितैः पूर्तैः सुशीतैर्युतैः युष्मद्वाक्कलशोज्झितैः श्रुतिसुखैर्वाक्यामृतैः सेचय ।
संतप्तं भवतापदावदहनज्वालाभिरेनं प्रभो धन्यास्ते भवदीक्षणक्षणगतेः पात्रीकृताः स्वीकृताः ॥ ३९ ॥
verses.roman:
brahmānandarasānubhūtikalitaiḥ pūrtaiḥ suśītairyutaiḥ yuṣmadvākkalaśojjhitaiḥ śrutisukhairvākyāmṛtaiḥ secaya |
saṃtaptaṃ bhavatāpadāvadahanajvālābhirenaṃ prabho dhanyāste bhavadīkṣaṇakṣaṇagateḥ pātrīkṛtāḥ svīkṛtāḥ || 39 ||
verses.colloquial:
brahma aananda rasa anubhuuti kalitaih puurtaih sushiitaih yutaih yushmad vaak kalasha ujjhitaih shruti sukhair vaakya amritaih sechaya |
samtaptam bhavat taapa daava dahana jvaalabhir enam prabho dhanyaah te bhavad iikshana kshana gateh paatri kritaah sviikritaah || 39 ||
verses.translation_reworded: O Lord, I am tormented by worldly afflictions as if by the tongues of a forest fire. Sprinkle me with your nectar-like speech, sweetened by tasting the elixir of Brahman's bliss, pure, deeply cooling, flowing from your lips as from a pitcher, and delightful to the ear. Blessed are those on whom even a passing glance of yours falls, accepting them as your own.

verses.sanskrit:
कथं तरेयं भवसिन्धुमेतं का वा गतिर्मे कतमोऽस्त्युपायः ।
जाने न किञ्ज्चित्कृपयाव मां प्रभो संसारदुःखक्षतिमातनुष्व ॥ ४0 ॥
verses.roman:
kathaṃ tareyaṃ bhavasindhumetaṃ kā vā gatirme katamo'styupāyaḥ |
jāne na kiñjcitkṛpayāva māṃ prabho saṃsāraduḥkhakṣatimātanuṣva || 40 ||
verses.colloquial:
katham tareyam bhava sindhum etam kaa vaa gatir me katamah asti upaayah |
jaane na kinchit kripayaa ava maam prabho samsaara duhkha kshatiim aatanushva || 40 ||
verses.translation_reworded: How to cross this ocean of phenomenal existence, what will become of me, and which means I should take up: of these I know nothing. Please be gracious enough to save me, O Lord, and explain in full how to end the misery of this relative existence.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Loving Advice of the Guru</vt>
तथा वदन्तं शरणागतं स्वं संसारदावानलतापतप्तम् ।
निरीक्ष्य कारुण्यरसार्द्रदृष्ट्या दद्यादभीतिं सहसा महात्मा ॥ ४१ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Loving Advice of the Guru</vt>
tathā vadantaṃ śaraṇāgataṃ svaṃ saṃsāradāvānalatāpataptam |
nirīkṣya kāruṇyarasārdradṛṣṭyā dadyādabhītiṃ sahasā mahātmā || 41 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Loving Advice of the Guru</vt>
tathaa vadantam sharana aagatam svam samsaara daava anala taapa taptam |
niiriikshya kaarunya rasa aardra drishtayaa dadyaat abhiitim sahasaa mahaatmaa || 41 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As the seeker says this, tormented by the afflictions of the world, which is like a forest on fire, and asking for protection, the saint looks at him with eyes softened by pity and at once tells him to give up all fear.

verses.sanskrit:
विद्वान् स तस्मा उपसत्तिमीयुषे मुमुक्षवे साधु यथोक्तकारिणे ।
प्रशान्तचित्ताय शमान्विताय तत्त्वोपदेशं कृपयैव कुर्यात् ॥ ४२ ॥
verses.roman:
vidvān sa tasmā upasattimīyuṣe mumukṣave sādhu yathoktakāriṇe |
praśāntacittāya śamānvitāya tattvopadeśaṃ kṛpayaiva kuryāt || 42 ||
verses.colloquial:
vidvaan sah tasmai upasattim iiyushe mumukshave saadhu yathoktakaarinne |
prashaanta chittaaya shama anvitaaya tattva upadesham kripayaa eva kuryaat || 42 ||
verses.translation_reworded: To the one who has come for protection, who thirsts for Liberation, who properly follows the injunctions of the Scriptures, and whose mind is serene and calm, the sage begins to teach the truth out of pure grace.

verses.sanskrit:
मा भैष्ट विद्वंस्तव नास्त्यपायः संसारसिन्धोस्तरणेऽस्त्युपायः ।
येनैव याता यतयोऽस्य पारं तमेव मार्गं तव निर्दिशामि ॥ ४३ ॥
verses.roman:
mā bhaiṣṭa vidvaṃstava nāstyapāyaḥ saṃsārasindhostaraṇe'styupāyaḥ |
yenaiva yātā yatayo'sya pāraṃ tameva mārgaṃ tava nirdiśāmi || 43 ||
verses.colloquial:
maa bhaishta vidvaan tava na asti apaayah samsaara sindhos tarane asti upaayah |
yena eva yaataa yatayo asya paaram tam eva maargam tava nirdishaami || 43 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Have no fear, learned one. There is no death for you. There is a way to cross this sea of relative existence, and I will teach you the very path by which sages have passed beyond it.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्त्युपायो महान् कश्चित्संसारभयनाशनः ।
तेन तीर्त्वा भवाम्भोधिं परमानन्दमाप्स्यसि ॥ ४४ ॥
verses.roman:
astyupāyo mahān kaścitsaṃsārabhayanāśanaḥ |
tena tīrtvā bhavāmbhodhiṃ paramānandamāpsyasi || 44 ||
verses.colloquial:
asti upaayah mahaan kashchit samsaara bhaya naashanah |
tena tiirtvaa bhava ambhodhim param aanandam aapsyasi || 44 ||
verses.translation_reworded: There is a sovereign means that ends the fear of relative existence. Through it you will cross the sea of Samsāra and reach supreme bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
वेदान्तार्थविचारेण जायते ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ।
तेनात्यन्तिकसंसारदुःखनाशो भवत्यनु ॥ ४५ ॥
verses.roman:
vedāntārthavicāreṇa jāyate jñānamuttamam |
tenātyantikasaṃsāraduḥkhanāśo bhavatyanu || 45 ||
verses.colloquial:
vedaanta artha vicaarena jaayate jnaanam uttamam |
tena atyantika samsaara duhkha naasho bhavati anu || 45 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Reasoning on the meaning of Vedanta produces effective knowledge, and this is followed at once by the complete destruction of the misery born of relative existence.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रद्धाभक्तिध्यानयोगाम्मुमुक्षोः मुक्तेर्हेतून्वक्ति साक्षाच्छ्रुतेर्गीः ।
यो वा एतेष्वेव तिष्ठत्यमुष्य मोक्षोऽविद्याकल्पिताद्देहबन्धात् ॥ ४६ ॥
verses.roman:
śraddhābhaktidhyānayogāmmumukṣoḥ mukterhetūnvakti sākṣācchrutergīḥ |
yo vā eteṣveva tiṣṭhatyamuṣya mokṣo'vidyākalpitāddehabandhāt || 46 ||
verses.colloquial:
shraddhaa bhakti dhyaana yogaan mumukshoh mukteh hetuun vakti saakshaat shruteh giih |
yo vaa eteshu eva tishthati amushy a mokshah avidyaa kalpitaat deha bandhaat || 46 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Faith (Śraddhā), devotion, and the Yoga of meditation are named by the Śruti as the direct means of Liberation for a seeker. Whoever remains in these is released from the bondage of the body, which Ignorance has conjured up.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानयोगात्परमात्मनस्तव ह्यनात्मबन्धस्तत एव संसृतिः ।
तयोर्विवेकोदितबोधवन्हिः अज्ञानकार्यं प्रदहेत्समूलम् ॥ ४७ ॥
verses.roman:
ajñānayogātparamātmanastava hyanātmabandhastata eva saṃsṛtiḥ |
tayorvivekoditabodhavanhiḥ ajñānakāryaṃ pradahetsamūlam || 47 ||
verses.colloquial:
ajnaana yogaat param aatmanah tava hi anaatma bandhah tatah eva samsritih |
tayoh viveka udita bodha vahnih ajnaana kaaryam pradahet samuulam || 47 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is indeed by contact with Ignorance that you, the Supreme Self, find yourself bound by the non-Self, and from this alone comes the round of births and deaths. The fire of knowledge, lit by discriminating between the two, burns up the effects of Ignorance along with their root.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Questions of the Disciple</vt>
शिष्य उवाच कृपया श्रूयतां स्वामिन् प्रश्नोऽयं क्रियते मया ।
यदुत्तरमहं श्रुत्वा कृतार्थः स्यां भवन्मुखात् ॥ ४८ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Questions of the Disciple</vt>
śiṣya uvāca kṛpayā śrūyatāṃ svāmin praśno'yaṃ kriyate mayā |
yaduttaramahaṃ śrutvā kṛtārthaḥ syāṃ bhavanmukhāt || 48 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Questions of the Disciple</vt>
shishya uvaacha kripayaa shruuyataam svaaamin prashnoh ayam kriyate mayaa |
yad uttaram aham shrutvaa kritaarthah syaam bhavan mukhaat || 48 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Disciple said: Please be gracious enough to listen, O Master, to the question I am putting to you. I will be glad to hear the answer from your own lips.

verses.sanskrit:
को नाम बन्धः कथमेष आगतः कथं प्रतिष्ठास्य कथं विमोक्षः ।
कोऽसावनात्मा परमः क आत्मा तयोर्विवेकः कथमेतदुच्यताम् ॥ ४९ ॥
verses.roman:
ko nāma bandhaḥ kathameṣa āgataḥ kathaṃ pratiṣṭhāsya kathaṃ vimokṣaḥ |
ko'sāvanātmā paramaḥ ka ātmā tayorvivekaḥ kathametaducyatām || 49 ||
verses.colloquial:
kah naama bandhah katham esha aagatah katham pratishthaa asya katham vimokshah |
kah asau anaatmaa paramah kah aatmaa tayoh vivekah katham etad uchyataam || 49 ||
verses.translation_reworded: What exactly is bondage? How did it come upon the Self? How does it continue? How does one become free of it? What is this non-Self? Who is the Supreme Self? And how can one tell them apart? Please tell me about all of this.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Intelligent Disciple - Appreciated</vt>
श्रीगुरुवाच धन्योऽसि कृतकृत्योऽसि पावित ते कुलं त्वया ।
यदविद्याबन्धमुक्त्या ब्रह्मीभवितुमिच्छसि ॥ ५0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Intelligent Disciple - Appreciated</vt>
śrīguruvāca dhanyo'si kṛtakṛtyo'si pāvita te kulaṃ tvayā |
yadavidyābandhamuktyā brahmībhavitumicchasi || 50 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Intelligent Disciple - Appreciated</vt>
shrii guruh uvaacha dhanyah asi krita krityah asi paavita te kulam tvayaa |
yad avidyaa bandha muktyaa brahmii bhavitum ichchhasi || 50 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Guru replied: You are blessed! You have achieved the purpose of your life and made your family holy, since you wish to reach Brahmanhood by getting free of the bondage of Ignorance!

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Glory of Self-Effort</vt>
ऋणमोचनकर्तारः पितुः सन्ति सुतादयः ।
बन्धमोचनकर्ता तु स्वस्मादन्यो न कश्चन ॥ ५१ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Glory of Self-Effort</vt>
ṛṇamocanakartāraḥ pituḥ santi sutādayaḥ |
bandhamocanakartā tu svasmādanyo na kaścana || 51 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Glory of Self-Effort</vt>
rina mocana kartaarah pituh santi suta aadayah |
bandha mocana kartaa tu svasmaat anyah na kashchana || 51 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A father has sons and others to clear him of his debts, but no one except himself can remove his bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
मस्तकन्यस्तभारादेर्दुःखमन्यैर्निवार्यते ।
क्षुधादिकृतदुःखं तु विना स्वेन न केनचित् ॥ ५२ ॥
verses.roman:
mastakanyastabhārāderduḥkhamanyairnivāryate |
kṣudhādikṛtaduḥkhaṃ tu vinā svena na kenacit || 52 ||
verses.colloquial:
mastaka nyasta bhaara ader duhkham anyaih nivaaryate |
kshudha aadi krita duhkham tu vinaa svena na kenachit || 52 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Others can relieve a burden such as a load carried on the head, but only one's own self can stop the pain of hunger and the like.

verses.sanskrit:
पथ्यमौषधसेवा च क्रियते येन रोगिणा ।
आरोग्यसिद्धिर्दृष्टास्य नान्यानुष्ठितकर्मणा ॥ ५३ ॥
verses.roman:
pathyamauṣadhasevā ca kriyate yena rogiṇā |
ārogyasiddhirdṛṣṭāsya nānyānuṣṭhitakarmaṇā || 53 ||
verses.colloquial:
pathyam aushadha sevaa cha kriyate yena roginaa |
aarogya siddhir drishta asya na anya anushtita karmanaa || 53 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is only the patient who takes the proper diet and medicine who is seen to recover fully; others doing the work on his behalf will not cure him.

verses.sanskrit:
वस्तुस्वरूपं स्फुटबोधचक्षुषा स्वेनैव वेद्यं न तु पण्डितेन ।
चन्द्रस्वरूपं निजचक्षुषैव ज्ञातव्यमन्यैरवगम्यते किम् ॥ ५४ ॥
verses.roman:
vastusvarūpaṃ sphuṭabodhacakṣuṣā svenaiva vedyaṃ na tu paṇḍitena |
candrasvarūpaṃ nijacakṣuṣaiva jñātavyamanyairavagamyate kim || 54 ||
verses.colloquial:
vastu svaruupam sphuta bodha chakshushaa svena eva vedyam na tu panditena |
chandra svaruupam nija chakshushaa eva jnaatavyam anyaih avagamyate kim || 54 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The true nature of things must be known personally, through the eye of clear illumination, and not through a sage. What the moon is exactly must be seen with one's own eyes. Can others know it for you?

verses.sanskrit:
अविद्याकामकर्मादिपाशबन्धं विमोचितुम् ।
कः शक्नुयाद्विनात्मानं कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ॥ ५५ ॥
verses.roman:
avidyākāmakarmādipāśabandhaṃ vimocitum |
kaḥ śaknuyādvinātmānaṃ kalpakoṭiśatairapi || 55 ||
verses.colloquial:
avidyaa kaama karma aadi paasha bandham vimochitum |
kah shaknuyaat vinaa aatmaanam kalpa koti shataih api || 55 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Who but oneself can be rid of the bondage forged by the fetters of Ignorance, desire, action, and the like, even over a hundred crore of cycles?

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Knowledge of the Self-Its Beauty</vt>
न योगेन न सांख्येन कर्मणा नो न विद्यया ।
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्वबोधेन मोक्षः सिध्यति नान्यथा ॥ ५६ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Knowledge of the Self-Its Beauty</vt>
na yogena na sāṃkhyena karmaṇā no na vidyayā |
brahmātmaikatvabodhena mokṣaḥ sidhyati nānyathā || 56 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Knowledge of the Self-Its Beauty</vt>
na yogena na saamkhyena karmanaa no na vidyayaa |
brahma aatma aikatva bodhena mokshah sidhyati na anyathaa || 56 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Liberation is not possible through Yoga, through Sānkhya, through work, or through learning. It comes through realising one's identity with Brahman, and by no other means.

verses.sanskrit:
वीणाया रूपसौन्दर्यं तन्त्रीवादनसौष्ठवम् ।
प्रजारञ्ज्जनमात्रं तन्न साम्राज्याय कल्पते ॥ ५७ ॥
verses.roman:
vīṇāyā rūpasaundaryaṃ tantrīvādanasauṣṭhavam |
prajārañjjanamātraṃ tanna sāmrājyāya kalpate || 57 ||
verses.colloquial:
viinayaa ruupa saundaryam tantrii vaadana saushtavam |
prajaa ranjana maatram tat na saamraajyaaya kalpate || 57 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The beauty of a guitar's form and skill in playing its strings serve only to please a few people. They are not enough to confer sovereignty.

verses.sanskrit:
वाग्वैखरी शब्दझरी शास्त्रव्याख्यानकौशलम् ।
वैदुष्यं विदुषां तद्वद्भुक्तये न तु मुक्तये ॥ ५८ ॥
verses.roman:
vāgvaikharī śabdajharī śāstravyākhyānakauśalam |
vaiduṣyaṃ viduṣāṃ tadvadbhuktaye na tu muktaye || 58 ||
verses.colloquial:
vaak vaikharee shabda jharii shastra vyaakhyaana kaushalam |
vaidushyam vidushaam tadvad bhuktaye na tu muktaye || 58 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Loud speech pouring out in a torrent of words, skill in expounding the Scriptures, and erudition as well bring the scholar a little personal enjoyment, but they do nothing for Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
अविज्ञाते परे तत्त्वे शास्त्राधीतिस्तु निष्फला ।
विज्ञातेऽपि परे तत्त्वे शास्त्राधीतिस्तु निष्फला ॥ ५९ ॥
verses.roman:
avijñāte pare tattve śāstrādhītistu niṣphalā |
vijñāte'pi pare tattve śāstrādhītistu niṣphalā || 59 ||
verses.colloquial:
avijnaate pare tattve shastra adhiitih tu nishphalaa |
vijnaate api pare tattve shastra adhiitih tu nishphalaa || 59 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Studying the Scriptures is useless as long as the highest Truth is unknown, and it is just as useless once the highest Truth has been known.

verses.sanskrit:
शब्दजालं महारण्यं चित्तभ्रमणकारणम् ।
अतः प्रयत्नाज्ज्ञातव्यं तत्त्वज्ञैस्तत्त्वमात्मनः ॥ ६0 ॥
verses.roman:
śabdajālaṃ mahāraṇyaṃ cittabhramaṇakāraṇam |
ataḥ prayatnājjñātavyaṃ tattvajñaistattvamātmanaḥ || 60 ||
verses.colloquial:
shabda jaalam mahaa aranyam chitta bhramana kaaranam |
atah prayatnaat jnaatavyam tattva jnaih tattvam aatmanah || 60 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Scriptures, with their many words, are a dense forest that only sets the mind wandering. Wise people should therefore apply themselves earnestly to knowing the true nature of the Self.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानसर्पदष्टस्य ब्रह्मज्ञानौषधं विना ।
किमु वेदैश्च शास्त्रैश्च किमु मन्त्रैः किमौषधैः ॥ ६१ ॥
verses.roman:
ajñānasarpadaṣṭasya brahmajñānauṣadhaṃ vinā |
kimu vedaiśca śāstraiśca kimu mantraiḥ kimauṣadhaiḥ || 61 ||
verses.colloquial:
ajnaana sarpa dashtasya brahma jnaana aushadham vinaa |
kim u vedaih cha shaastraih cha kim u mantraih kim aushadhaih || 61 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Knowledge of Brahman is the one cure for someone bitten by the serpent of Ignorance. What use to that person are the Vedas and Scriptures, Mantras and medicines?

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Direct Experience - Liberation</vt>
न गच्छति विना पानं व्याधिरौषधशब्दतः ।
विनापरोक्षानुभवं ब्रह्मशब्दैर्न मुच्यते ॥ ६२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Direct Experience - Liberation</vt>
na gacchati vinā pānaṃ vyādhirauṣadhaśabdataḥ |
vināparokṣānubhavaṃ brahmaśabdairna mucyate || 62 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Direct Experience - Liberation</vt>
na gachchhati vinaa paanam vyaadhir aushadha shabdatah |
vinaa aparoksha anubhavam brahma shabdaih na muchyate || 62 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Saying the name of a medicine without swallowing it will not rid anyone of a disease. In the same way, no one is liberated just by pronouncing the word Brahman, without direct realization.

verses.sanskrit:
अकृत्वा दृश्यविलयमज्ञात्वा तत्त्वमात्मनः ।
ब्रह्मशब्दैः कुतो मुक्तिरुक्तिमात्रफलैर्नृणाम् ॥ ६३ ॥
verses.roman:
akṛtvā dṛśyavilayamajñātvā tattvamātmanaḥ |
brahmaśabdaiḥ kuto muktiruktimātraphalairnṛṇām || 63 ||
verses.colloquial:
akritvaaa drishya vilayam ajnaatvaaa tattvam aatmanah |
brahma shabdaih kutah muktih ukti maatra phalaih nrinaam || 63 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If the objective universe has not been made to vanish and the truth of the Self has not been known, how could saying the word Brahman bring Liberation? It would be nothing but an exercise of the voice.

verses.sanskrit:
अकृत्वा शत्रुसंहारमगत्वाखिलभूश्रियम् ।
राजाहमिति शब्दान्नो राजा भवितुमर्हति ॥ ६४ ॥
verses.roman:
akṛtvā śatrusaṃhāramagatvākhilabhūśriyam |
rājāhamiti śabdānno rājā bhavitumarhati || 64 ||
verses.colloquial:
akritvaaa shatru samhaaram agatvaaa akhila bhuu shriyam |
raajaa aham iti shabdaat no raajaa bhavitum arhati || 64 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Nobody becomes an emperor by announcing, 'I am an emperor,' without first slaying his enemies and taking possession of the splendor of the whole surrounding region.

verses.sanskrit:
आप्तोक्तिं खननं तथोपरिशिलाद्युत्कर्षणं स्वीकृतिं निक्षेपः समपेक्षते नहि बहिः शब्दैस्तु निर्गच्छति ।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदोपदेशमननध्यानादिभिर्लभ्यते मायाकार्यतिरोहितं स्वममलं तत्त्वं न दुर्युक्तिभिः ॥ ६५ ॥
verses.roman:
āptoktiṃ khananaṃ tathopariśilādyutkarṣaṇaṃ svīkṛtiṃ nikṣepaḥ samapekṣate nahi bahiḥ śabdaistu nirgacchati |
tadvadbrahmavidopadeśamananadhyānādibhirlabhyate māyākāryatirohitaṃ svamamalaṃ tattvaṃ na duryuktibhiḥ || 65 ||
verses.colloquial:
aapta uktim khananam tathaa upari shilaa aadi utkarshnam svikritim nikshepah sam apekshate na hi bahih shabdaih tu nirgachchhati |
tadvat brahma vid upadesh manana dhyaana aadibhih labhyate maayaa kaarya tirohitam sva amalam tattvam na dur yuktibhih || 65 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A treasure buried underground never comes up when called by name. Getting it requires reliable directions, digging, clearing away the stones and whatever else lies on top, and finally taking hold of it. Likewise, the clear Truth of the Self, hidden by Maya and its effects, is reached through the teaching of a knower of Brahman, followed by reflection, meditation, and the like, and not through twisted arguments.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन भवबन्धविमुक्तये ।
स्वैरेव यत्नः कर्तव्यो रोगादाविव पण्डितैः ॥ ६६ ॥
verses.roman:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena bhavabandhavimuktaye |
svaireva yatnaḥ kartavyo rogādāviva paṇḍitaiḥ || 66 ||
verses.colloquial:
tasmaat sarva prayatnena bhava bandha vimuktaye |
svaih eva yatnah kartavyo roga aadaau iva panditaih || 66 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So the wise should work personally, with every means at their disposal, to free themselves from the bondage of repeated birth and death, just as they would with a disease and similar troubles.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Discussion on Questions Raised</vt>
यस्त्वयाद्य कृतः प्रश्नो वरीयाञ्ज्छास्त्रविन्मतः ।
सूत्रप्रायो निगूढार्थो ज्ञातव्यश्च मुमुक्षुभिः ॥ ६७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Discussion on Questions Raised</vt>
yastvayādya kṛtaḥ praśno varīyāñjchāstravinmataḥ |
sūtraprāyo nigūḍhārtho jñātavyaśca mumukṣubhiḥ || 67 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Discussion on Questions Raised</vt>
yah tvayaa adya kritah prashnoh variiyaan shastra vin matah |
suutra praayah niguudha arthah jnaatavyah cha mumukshibhih || 67 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The question you have asked today is excellent. Those who know the Śastras approve of it; it is concise, rich in meaning, and worth knowing for all who seek Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
शृणुष्वावहितो विद्वन्यन्मया समुदीर्यते ।
तदेतच्छ्रवणात्सद्यो भवबन्धाद्विमोक्ष्यसे ॥ ६८ ॥
verses.roman:
śṛṇuṣvāvahito vidvanyanmayā samudīryate |
tadetacchravaṇātsadyo bhavabandhādvimokṣyase || 68 ||
verses.colloquial:
shrinushvaa avahitoh vidvan yan mayaa samudiryate |
tad etat shravanaat sadyo bhava bandhaat vimokshyase || 68 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Learned one, pay close attention to what I am about to say. Hearing it, you will at once be released from the bondage of Samsāra.

verses.sanskrit:
मोक्षस्य हेतुः प्रथमो निगद्यते वैराग्यमत्यन्तमनित्यवस्तुषु ।
ततः शमश्चापि दमस्तितिक्षा न्यासः प्रसक्ताखिलकर्मणां भृशम् ॥ ६९ ॥
verses.roman:
mokṣasya hetuḥ prathamo nigadyate vairāgyamatyantamanityavastuṣu |
tataḥ śamaścāpi damastitikṣā nyāsaḥ prasaktākhilakarmaṇāṃ bhṛśam || 69 ||
verses.colloquial:
mokhasya hetuh prathamo nigadyate vairaagyam atyantam anitya vastushu |
tatah shamah cha api dama titikshaa nyaasah prasakte akhila karmanaam bhrisham || 69 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The first step toward Liberation is a deep aversion to everything perishable. After it come calmness, self-control, forbearance, and the complete giving up of all work prescribed in the Scriptures.

verses.sanskrit:
ततः श्रुतिस्तन्मननं सतत्त्व ध्यानं चिरं नित्यनिरन्तरं मुनेः ।
ततोऽविकल्पं परमेत्य विद्वान् इहैव निर्वाणसुखं समृच्छति ॥ ७0 ॥
verses.roman:
tataḥ śrutistanmananaṃ satattva dhyānaṃ ciraṃ nityanirantaraṃ muneḥ |
tato'vikalpaṃ parametya vidvān ihaiva nirvāṇasukhaṃ samṛcchati || 70 ||
verses.colloquial:
tatah shrutih tan mananam sa tattva dhyaanam chiram nitya nirantaram muneh |
tatah avikalpam param etya vidvaan iha eva nirvaana sukham samrichchhati || 70 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Next, for the Muni, come hearing, reflection on what was heard, and long, constant, uninterrupted meditation on the Truth. The learned seeker then reaches the supreme Nirvikalpa state and experiences the bliss of Nirvana in this very life.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्बोद्धव्यं तवेदानीमात्मानात्मविवेचनम् ।
तदुच्यते मया सम्यक्श्रुत्वात्मन्यवधारय ॥ ७१ ॥
verses.roman:
yadboddhavyaṃ tavedānīmātmānātmavivecanam |
taducyate mayā samyakśrutvātmanyavadhāraya || 71 ||
verses.colloquial:
yad boddhavyam tava idaaniim aatmaa anaatma vivecanam |
tad uchyate mayaa samyak shrutvaa aatmani avadhaaraya || 71 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I will now explain in full what you need to know: the discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. Listen, and settle it in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Gross Body</vt>
मज्जास्थिमेदःपलरक्तचर्म त्वगाह्वयैर्धातुभिरेभिरन्वितम् ।
पादोरुवक्षोभुजपृष्ठमस्तकैः अङ्गैरुपाङ्गैरुपयुक्तमेतत् ॥ ७२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Gross Body</vt>
majjāsthimedaḥpalaraktacarma tvagāhvayairdhātubhirebhiranvitam |
pādoruvakṣobhujapṛṣṭhamastakaiḥ aṅgairupāṅgairupayuktametat || 72 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Gross Body</vt>
majjaa asthi medah pala rakta charma tvag aahvayaih dhaatubhih ebhih anvitam |
paada uru vaksha bhuja prishtha mastakaiah angaih upaangaih upayuktam etat || 72 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Made of seven components, namely marrow, bones, fat, flesh, blood, skin, and cuticle, and having these limbs and their parts: legs, thighs, chest, arms, back, and head:

verses.sanskrit:
अहंममेतिप्रथितं शरीरं मोहास्पदं स्थूलमितीर्यते बुधैः ।
नभोनभस्वद्दहनाम्बुभूमयः सूक्ष्माणि भूतानि भवन्ति तानि ॥ ७३ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃmametiprathitaṃ śarīraṃ mohāspadaṃ sthūlamitīryate budhaiḥ |
nabhonabhasvaddahanāmbubhūmayaḥ sūkṣmāṇi bhūtāni bhavanti tāni || 73 ||
verses.colloquial:
aham mama iti prathitam shariram moha aaspadam sthulam iti iiryate budhaih |
nabho nabhasvat dahana ambu bhuumayah suukshmani bhuutaani bhavanti taani || 73 ||
verses.translation_reworded: this body, known as the home of the delusion of 'I and mine,' is what the sages call the gross body. Sky, air, fire, water, and earth are the subtle elements. They:

verses.sanskrit:
परस्परांशैर्मिलितानि भूत्वा स्थूलानि च स्थूलशरीरहेतवः ।
मात्रास्तदीया विषया भवन्ति शब्दादयः पञ्च सुखाय भोक्तुः ॥ ७४ ॥
verses.roman:
parasparāṃśairmilitāni bhūtvā sthūlāni ca sthūlaśarīrahetavaḥ |
mātrāstadīyā viṣayā bhavanti śabdādayaḥ pañca sukhāya bhoktuḥ || 74 ||
verses.colloquial:
paraspara amshaih militaani bhuutvaa sthoolaani cha sthuula shariira hetavah |
maatraas tadiiyaah vishayaah bhavanti shabda aadayah pancha sukhaaya bhoktuh || 74 ||
verses.translation_reworded: by combining with portions of one another and turning gross, make up the gross body. Their subtle essences make up the sense objects, the group of five beginning with sound, which serve the happiness of the experiencer, the individual soul.

verses.sanskrit:
य एषु मूढा विषयेषु बद्धा रागोरुपाशेन सुदुर्दमेन ।
आयान्ति निर्यान्त्यध ऊर्ध्वमुच्चैः स्वकर्मदूतेन जवेन नीताः ॥ ७५ ॥
verses.roman:
ya eṣu mūḍhā viṣayeṣu baddhā rāgorupāśena sudurdamena |
āyānti niryāntyadha ūrdhvamuccaiḥ svakarmadūtena javena nītāḥ || 75 ||
verses.colloquial:
ye eshu muudhaah vishayeshu baddhaa raaga uru paashena su dur damena |
aayaanti niryaanti adha uurdhvam uchchaih sva karma duutena javena niitaah || 75 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Fools bound to these sense objects by the thick rope of attachment, which is so hard to cut, come and go, rising and falling, swept along at full speed by the mighty messenger of their past actions.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Sense Objects a Trap - Man Bound</vt>
शब्दादिभिः पञ्चभिरेव पञ्च पञ्चत्वमापुः स्वगुणेन बद्धाः ।
कुरङ्गमातङ्गपतङ्गमीन भृङ्गा नरः पञ्चभिरञ्चितः किम् ॥ ७६ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Sense Objects a Trap - Man Bound</vt>
śabdādibhiḥ pañcabhireva pañca pañcatvamāpuḥ svaguṇena baddhāḥ |
kuraṅgamātaṅgapataṅgamīna bhṛṅgā naraḥ pañcabhirañcitaḥ kim || 76 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Sense Objects a Trap - Man Bound</vt>
shabda aadibhih panchabhih eva pancha panchatvam aapuh sva gunena baddhah |
kurangah maatangah patangah miinah bhringaah narah panchabhih anchitah kim || 76 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The deer, the elephant, the moth, the fish, and the black bee have each perished, bound by their own attachment to just one of the five senses, sound and the rest. What then awaits a human being attached to all five?

verses.sanskrit:
दोषेण तीव्रो विषयः कृष्णसर्पविषादपि ।
विषं निहन्ति भोक्तारं द्रष्टारं चक्षुषाप्ययम् ॥ ७७ ॥
verses.roman:
doṣeṇa tīvro viṣayaḥ kṛṣṇasarpaviṣādapi |
viṣaṃ nihanti bhoktāraṃ draṣṭāraṃ cakṣuṣāpyayam || 77 ||
verses.colloquial:
doshen a tiivro vishayah krishna sarpa vishaat api |
visham nihanti bhoktaaram drashtaaram chakshushaa api ayam || 77 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Sense objects are even deadlier than cobra venom. Poison kills the one who swallows it, but sense objects kill a person who merely looks at them with the eyes.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयाशामहापाशाद्यो विमुक्तः सुदुस्त्यजात् ।
स एव कल्पते मुक्त्यै नान्यः षट्शास्त्रवेद्यपि ॥ ७८ ॥
verses.roman:
viṣayāśāmahāpāśādyo vimuktaḥ sudustyajāt |
sa eva kalpate muktyai nānyaḥ ṣaṭśāstravedyapi || 78 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishaya aashaa mahaa paashaat yo vimuktah su dustyajaat |
sah eva kalpate muktyai na anyah shat shastra vedyah api || 78 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only the person free of the terrible shackles of craving for sense objects, so very hard to shake off, is fit for Liberation. No one else is, even someone who has mastered all six Śastras.

verses.sanskrit:
आपातवैराग्यवतो मुमुक्षून् भवाब्धिपारं प्रतियातुमुद्यतान् ।
आशाग्रहो मज्जयतेऽन्तराले निगृह्य कण्ठे विनिवर्त्य वेगात् ॥ ७९ ॥
verses.roman:
āpātavairāgyavato mumukṣūn bhavābdhipāraṃ pratiyātumudyatān |
āśāgraho majjayate'ntarāle nigṛhya kaṇṭhe vinivartya vegāt || 79 ||
verses.colloquial:
aapaata vairaagya vatah mumukshun bhava abdhi paaram prati yaatum udyataan |
aashaa graho majjayate antaraale nigrahya kanthhe vinivartya vegaat || 79 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Some seekers of liberation have only the appearance of dispassion (Vairāgya) as they try to cross the ocean of Samsāra (relative existence). The shark of craving seizes them by the throat, drags them violently away, and drowns them midway.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयाख्यग्रहो येन सुविरक्त्यसिना हतः ।
स गच्छति भवाम्भोधेः पारं प्रत्यूहवर्जितः ॥ ८0 ॥
verses.roman:
viṣayākhyagraho yena suviraktyasinā hataḥ |
sa gacchati bhavāmbhodheḥ pāraṃ pratyūhavarjitaḥ || 80 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishaya aakhya graho yena su virakti asinaa hatah |
sah gachchhati bhava ambhodhehu paaram pratyuuha varjitah || 80 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whoever has slain the shark called sense object with the sword of mature dispassion crosses the ocean of Samsara with nothing to block the way.

verses.sanskrit:
विषमविषयमार्गैर्गच्छतोऽनच्छबुद्धेः प्रतिपदमभियातो मृत्युरप्येष विद्धि ।
हितसुजनगुरुक्त्या गच्छतः स्वस्य युक्त्या प्रभवति फलसिद्धिः सत्यमित्येव विद्धि ॥ ८१ ॥
verses.roman:
viṣamaviṣayamārgairgacchato'nacchabuddheḥ pratipadamabhiyāto mṛtyurapyeṣa viddhi |
hitasujanaguruktyā gacchataḥ svasya yuktyā prabhavati phalasiddhiḥ satyamityeva viddhi || 81 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishama vishaya maargaih gachchhato anachchha buddheh prati padam abhiyaato mrityuh api esha viddhi |
hita su jana guru uktyaa gachchhatah svasya yuktyaa prabhavati phala siddhih satyam iti eva viddhi || 81 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Understand that death soon catches the foolish person who travels the dreadful roads of sense pleasure. But one who follows the guidance of a benevolent and worthy Guru, along with his own reasoning, reaches his goal. Know this to be true.

verses.sanskrit:
मोक्षस्य कांक्षा यदि वै तवास्ति त्यजातिदूराद्विषयान्विषं यथा ।
पीयूषवत्तोषदयाक्षमार्जव प्रशान्तिदान्तीर्भज नित्यमादरात् ॥ ८२ ॥
verses.roman:
mokṣasya kāṃkṣā yadi vai tavāsti tyajātidūrādviṣayānviṣaṃ yathā |
pīyūṣavattoṣadayākṣamārjava praśāntidāntīrbhaja nityamādarāt || 82 ||
verses.colloquial:
mokhasya kaankshaa yadi vai tava asti tyaja ati duuraat vishayaan visham yathaa |
piiyuusha vat tosha dayaa kshamaa arjava prashhaanti daantiih bhaja nityam aadaaraat || 82 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If you truly long for Liberation, keep well away from sense objects as you would from poison, and always carefully cultivate the nectar-like virtues of contentment, compassion, forgiveness, honesty, calmness, and self-control.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Fascination for Body Criticised</vt>
अनुक्षणं यत्परिहृत्य कृत्यं अनाद्यविद्याकृतबन्धमोक्षणम् ।
देहः परार्थोऽयममुष्य पोषणे यः सज्जते स स्वमनेन हन्ति ॥ ८३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Fascination for Body Criticised</vt>
anukṣaṇaṃ yatparihṛtya kṛtyaṃ anādyavidyākṛtabandhamokṣaṇam |
dehaḥ parārtho'yamamuṣya poṣaṇe yaḥ sajjate sa svamanena hanti || 83 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Fascination for Body Criticised</vt>
anukshanam yat parihritya krityam anaadi avidyaa krita bandha mokshanam |
deha para arthah ayam amushy a poshanye yah sajjate sah svam anena hanti || 83 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Liberation from the bondage of beginningless Ignorance is what should always be striven for. Whoever sets it aside and eagerly tends this body, which is only an object for others to enjoy, is destroying himself.

verses.sanskrit:
शरीरपोषणार्थी सन् य आत्मानं दिदृक्षति ।
ग्राहं दारुधिया धृत्वा नदि तर्तुं स गच्छति ॥ ८४ ॥
verses.roman:
śarīrapoṣaṇārthī san ya ātmānaṃ didṛkṣati |
grāhaṃ dārudhiyā dhṛtvā nadi tartuṃ sa gacchati || 84 ||
verses.colloquial:
shariira poshanaa arthii san yah aatmaanam didrikshati |
graaham daaru dhiyaa dhritvaa nadi tartum sah gachchhati || 84 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Someone who tries to realize the Self while devoting himself to feeding the body is setting out to cross a river by clinging to a crocodile he has mistaken for a log.

verses.sanskrit:
मोह एव महामृत्युर्मुमुक्षोर्वपुरादिषु ।
मोहो विनिर्जितो येन स मुक्तिपदमर्हति ॥ ८५ ॥
verses.roman:
moha eva mahāmṛtyurmumukṣorvapurādiṣu |
moho vinirjito yena sa muktipadamarhati || 85 ||
verses.colloquial:
mohah eva mahaa mrityur mumukshoh vapur aadishu |
mohah vinirjitah yena sah mukti padam arhati || 85 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For a seeker of Liberation, then, infatuation with things such as the body is a terrible death. Whoever has fully overcome it is worthy of the state of Freedom.

verses.sanskrit:
मोहं जहि महामृत्युं देहदारसुतादिषु ।
यं जित्वा मुनयो यान्ति तद्विष्णोः परमं पदम् ॥ ८६ ॥
verses.roman:
mohaṃ jahi mahāmṛtyuṃ dehadārasutādiṣu |
yaṃ jitvā munayo yānti tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam || 86 ||
verses.colloquial:
moham jahi mahaa mrityum deha daara suta aadishu |
yam jitvaa munayo yaanti tad vishnoh paramam padam || 86 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Overcome the terrible death of infatuation with your body, wife, children, and the like. By overcoming it the sages reach that Supreme State of Vishnu.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Gross Body Condemned</vt>
त्वङ्मांसरुधिरस्नायुमेदोमज्जास्थिसंकुलम् ।
पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषाभ्यां स्थूलं निन्द्यमिदं वपुः ॥ ८७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Gross Body Condemned</vt>
tvaṅmāṃsarudhirasnāyumedomajjāsthisaṃkulam |
pūrṇaṃ mūtrapurīṣābhyāṃ sthūlaṃ nindyamidaṃ vapuḥ || 87 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Gross Body Condemned</vt>
tvang maamsah rudhira snaayuh medo majjaa asthi samkulam |
puurnam muutra puriishaabhyaam sthulam nindyam idam vapuh || 87 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This gross body deserves contempt, for it is made of skin, flesh, blood, arteries and veins, fat, marrow, and bones, and it is filled with other foul things.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चीकृतेभ्यो भूतेभ्यः स्थूलेभ्यः पूर्वकर्मणा ।
समुत्पन्नमिदं स्थूलं भोगायतनमात्मनः अवस्था जागरस्तस्य स्थूलार्थानुभवो यतः ॥ ८८ ॥
verses.roman:
pañcīkṛtebhyo bhūtebhyaḥ sthūlebhyaḥ pūrvakarmaṇā |
samutpannamidaṃ sthūlaṃ bhogāyatanamātmanaḥ avasthā jāgarastasya sthūlārthānubhavo yataḥ || 88 ||
verses.colloquial:
panchii kritebhyo bhuutebhyah sthuulbhyah puurva karmanaa |
samutpannam idam sthoolam bhoga aayatanam aatmanah avasthaa jaagara tasya sthuula artha anubhavo yatah || 88 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One's past actions produce the gross body from the gross elements, which are formed when the subtle elements unite with one another. It serves as the soul's medium of experience. Its waking state is the one in which it perceives gross objects.

verses.sanskrit:
बाह्येन्द्रियैः स्थूलपदार्थसेवां स्रक्चन्दनस्त्र्यादिविचित्ररूपाम् ।
करोति जीवः स्वयमेतदात्मना तस्मात्प्रशस्तिर्वपुषोऽस्य जागरे ॥ ८९ ॥
verses.roman:
bāhyendriyaiḥ sthūlapadārthasevāṃ srakcandanastryādivicitrarūpām |
karoti jīvaḥ svayametadātmanā tasmātpraśastirvapuṣo'sya jāgare || 89 ||
verses.colloquial:
baahya indriyaih sthuula padaartha sevaam srak chandana strii aadi vichitra ruupaam |
karoti jiivah svayam etad aatmanaa tasmaat prashastih vapushoh asya jaagareh || 89 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Identifying with this form, the individual soul, though distinct from it, enjoys gross objects such as garlands and sandal paste through the outer organs. That is why this body is most fully active in the waking state.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वापि बाह्यसंसारः पुरुषस्य यदाश्रयः ।
विद्धि देहमिदं स्थूलं गृहवद्गृहमेधिनः ॥ ९0 ॥
verses.roman:
sarvāpi bāhyasaṃsāraḥ puruṣasya yadāśrayaḥ |
viddhi dehamidaṃ sthūlaṃ gṛhavadgṛhamedhinaḥ || 90 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarvaapi baahya samsaarah purushasya yad aashrayah |
viddhi deham idam sthoolam grihavad grihamedhino || 90 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Understand this gross body as being like a house to its householder. All of a person's dealings with the outer world depend on it.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थूलस्य संभवजरामरणानि धर्माः स्थौल्यादयो बहुविधाः शिशुताद्यवस्थाः ।
वर्णाश्रमादिनियमा बहुधामयाः स्युः पूजावमानबहुमानमुखा विशेषाः ॥ ९१ ॥
verses.roman:
sthūlasya saṃbhavajarāmaraṇāni dharmāḥ sthaulyādayo bahuvidhāḥ śiśutādyavasthāḥ |
varṇāśramādiniyamā bahudhāmayāḥ syuḥ pūjāvamānabahumānamukhā viśeṣāḥ || 91 ||
verses.colloquial:
sthoolasya sambhava jaraa maranani dharmaah sthaula aadayah bahu vidhaah shishu aadya avasthaa |
varna aashrama aadi niyamaa bahudhaa mayaah syuh puujaa avamaana bahu maana mukhaa visheshaah || 91 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Birth, decay, and death are the various properties of the gross body, and stoutness and the like, childhood and the like, are its different conditions. It has various rules according to caste and order of life. It is prone to many diseases and receives different kinds of treatment, such as worship, insult, and high honors.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Organs of Perception and Action</vt>
बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि श्रवणं त्वगक्षि घ्राणं च जिव्हा विषयावबोधनात् ।
वाक्पाणिपादा गुदमप्युपस्थः कर्मेन्द्रियाणि प्रवणेन कर्मसु ॥ ९२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Organs of Perception and Action</vt>
buddhīndriyāṇi śravaṇaṃ tvagakṣi ghrāṇaṃ ca jivhā viṣayāvabodhanāt |
vākpāṇipādā gudamapyupasthaḥ karmendriyāṇi pravaṇena karmasu || 92 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Organs of Perception and Action</vt>
buddhi indriyaani shravanaam tvag akshi ghraanama cha jivhaa vishaya avabodhanaaat |
vaak paani paadaa gudam api upasthah karma indriyaani pravanenea karmasu || 92 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The ears, skin, eyes, nose, and tongue are organs of knowledge, since they enable us to perceive objects. The vocal organs, hands, legs, and so on are organs of action, because of their inclination to work.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Inner Instruments</vt>
निगद्यतेऽन्तःकरणं मनोधीः अहंकृतिश्चित्तमिति स्ववृत्तिभिः ।
मनस्तु संकल्पविकल्पनादिभिः बुद्धिः पदार्थाध्यवसायधर्मतः ॥ ९३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Inner Instruments</vt>
nigadyate'ntaḥkaraṇaṃ manodhīḥ ahaṃkṛtiścittamiti svavṛttibhiḥ |
manastu saṃkalpavikalpanādibhiḥ buddhiḥ padārthādhyavasāyadharmataḥ || 93 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Inner Instruments</vt>
nigadyate antahkaranam mano dhiih ahankritih chittam iti sva vrittibhih |
manah tu samkalpa vikalpana aadibhih buddhih padaartha adhyavaasaaya dharmatah || 93 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The inner organ (Antahkaraṇa) goes by the names Manas, Buddhi, ego, or Chitta, depending on what it is doing. It is Manas when it weighs the pros and cons of something; Buddhi when it determines the truth of objects; ego when it identifies with this body as one's own self; and Chitta when it goes in search of pleasurable objects.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्राभिमानादहमित्यहंकृतिः ।
स्वार्थानुसन्धानगुणेन चित्तम् ॥ ९४ ॥
verses.roman:
atrābhimānādahamityahaṃkṛtiḥ |
svārthānusandhānaguṇena cittam || 94 ||
verses.colloquial:
atra abhimaanaat aham iti ahankritih |
sva artha anusandhaana gunena chittam || 94 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The inner organ (Antahkaraṇa) goes by the names Manas, Buddhi, ego, or Chitta, depending on what it is doing. It is Manas when it weighs the pros and cons of something; Buddhi when it determines the truth of objects; ego when it identifies with this body as one's own self; and Chitta when it goes in search of pleasurable objects.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Five Pranas</vt>
प्राणापानव्यानोदानसमाना भवत्यसौ प्राणः ।
स्वयमेव वृत्तिभेदाद्विकृतिभेदात्सुवर्णसलिलादिवत् ॥ ९५ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Five Pranas</vt>
prāṇāpānavyānodānasamānā bhavatyasau prāṇaḥ |
svayameva vṛttibhedādvikṛtibhedātsuvarṇasalilādivat || 95 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Five Pranas</vt>
praana apaana vyaana udaana samaanaa bhavati asau praanah |
svayam eva vritti bhedaat vikrit bhedaat suvarna salila aadivat || 95 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One single Prāṇa (vital force) becomes Prāṇa, Apāna, Vyāna, Udāna, and Samāna according to differences of function and modification, as happens with gold, water, and so on.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Subtle Body - Effects</vt>
वागादि पञ्च श्रवणादि पञ्च प्राणादि पञ्चाभ्रमुखानि पञ्च ।
बुद्ध्याद्यविद्यापि च कामकर्मणी पुर्यष्टकं सूक्ष्मशरीरमाहुः ॥ ९६ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Subtle Body - Effects</vt>
vāgādi pañca śravaṇādi pañca prāṇādi pañcābhramukhāni pañca |
buddhyādyavidyāpi ca kāmakarmaṇī puryaṣṭakaṃ sūkṣmaśarīramāhuḥ || 96 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Subtle Body - Effects</vt>
vaak aadi pancha shravana aadi pancha praana aadi pancha abhra mukhaani pancha |
buddhi aadya avidyaa api cha kaama karmani pury ashtakam suukshma shariram aahuh || 96 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The five organs of action beginning with speech, the five organs of knowledge beginning with the ear, the group of five Prāṇas, Buddhi and the rest, together with Nescience, desire, and action: these eight 'cities' make up what is called the subtle body.

verses.sanskrit:
इदं शरीरं शृणु सूक्ष्मसंज्ञितं लिङ्गं त्वपञ्चीकृतसंभवम् ।
सवासनं कर्मफलानुभावकं स्वाज्ञानतोऽनादिरुपाधिरात्मनः ॥ ९७ ॥
verses.roman:
idaṃ śarīraṃ śṛṇu sūkṣmasaṃjñitaṃ liṅgaṃ tvapañcīkṛtasaṃbhavam |
savāsanaṃ karmaphalānubhāvakaṃ svājñānato'nādirupādhirātmanaḥ || 97 ||
verses.colloquial:
idam shariram shrinu suukshma samjnitam lingam tu apanchii krita sambhavam |
sa vaasanam karma phala anubhaavakam sva ajnaanato anaadi upaadhi aatmanah || 97 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Listen. This subtle body, also called the Liṅga body, comes from the elements before they have subdivided and combined with one another. It holds desires and makes the soul experience the results of its actions. It is a beginningless superimposition on the soul, brought about by the soul's own ignorance.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नो भवत्यस्य विभक्त्यवस्था स्वमात्रशेषेण विभाति यत्र ।
स्वप्ने तु बुद्धिः स्वयमेव जाग्रत् कालीननानाविधवासनाभिः ॥ ९८ ॥
verses.roman:
svapno bhavatyasya vibhaktyavasthā svamātraśeṣeṇa vibhāti yatra |
svapne tu buddhiḥ svayameva jāgrat kālīnanānāvidhavasanābhiḥ || 98 ||
verses.colloquial:
svapno bhavati asya vibhakti avasthaa sva maatra sheshena vibhaati yatra |
svapne tu buddhih svayam eva jaagrat kaaliina naanaa vidha vaasanaabhih || 98 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Dream is a state of the soul different from waking, in which it shines by itself. In dreams Buddhi on its own takes up the role of agent and the like, because of the many desires of the waking state, while the supreme Ātman shines in Its own glory, with Buddhi as Its only superimposition. It witnesses everything and is untouched by even the smallest work that Buddhi does. Being completely unattached, It is untouched by any work that Its superimpositions may perform.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्त्रादिभावं प्रतिपद्य राजते यत्र स्वयं भाति ह्ययं परात्मा ।
धीमात्रकोपाधिरशेषसाक्षी न लिप्यते तत्कृतकर्मलेशैः यस्मादसङ्गस्तत एव कर्मभिः न लिप्यते किंचिदुपाधिना कृतैः ॥ ९९ ॥
verses.roman:
kartrādibhāvaṃ pratipadya rājate yatra svayaṃ bhāti hyayaṃ parātmā |
dhīmātrakopādhiraśeṣasākṣī na lipyate tatkṛtakarmaleśaiḥ yasmādasaṅgastata eva karmabhiḥ na lipyate kiñcidupādhinā kṛtaiḥ || 99 ||
verses.colloquial:
kartri aadi bhaavam pratipadya raajate yatra svayam bhaati hi ayam para aatmaa |
dhii maatra ka upaadhih ashesha saakshii na lipyate tat krita karma leshaih yasmaat asangah tatah eva karmabhih na lipyate kinchit upaadhina kritaih || 99 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Dream is a state of the soul different from waking, in which it shines by itself. In dreams Buddhi on its own takes up the role of agent and the like, because of the many desires of the waking state, while the supreme Ātman shines in Its own glory, with Buddhi as Its only superimposition. It witnesses everything and is untouched by even the smallest work that Buddhi does. Being completely unattached, It is untouched by any work that Its superimpositions may perform.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वव्यापृतिकरणं लिङ्गमिदं स्याच्चिदात्मनः पुंसः ।
वास्यादिकमिव तक्ष्णस्तेनैवात्मा भवत्यसङ्गोऽयम् ॥ १00 ॥
verses.roman:
sarvavyāpṛtikaraṇaṃ liṅgamidaṃ syāccidātmanaḥ puṃsaḥ |
vāsyādikamiva takṣṇastenaivātmā bhavatyasaṅgo'yam || 100 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarva vyaaprit i karanam lingam idam syaat chid aatmanah pumsah |
vaasya aadikam iva takshnah tena eva aatmaa bhavati asangah ayam || 99 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This subtle body is the tool for every activity of the Ātman, who is Knowledge Absolute, much as an adze and other implements serve a carpenter. For this reason the Ātman is perfectly unattached.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्धत्वमन्दत्वपटुत्वधर्माः सौगुण्यवैगुण्यवशाद्धि चक्षुषः ।
बाधिर्यमूकत्वमुखास्तथैव श्रोत्रादिधर्मा न तु वेत्तुरात्मनः ॥ १0१ ॥
verses.roman:
andhatvamandatvapaṭutvadharmāḥ sauguṇyavaiguṇyavaśāddhi cakṣuṣaḥ |
bādhiryamūkatvamukhāstathaiva śrotrādidharmā na tu vetturātmanaḥ || 101 ||
verses.colloquial:
andhatvam andatvam patutva dharmaah sau guniya vaigunyaa vashaad dhi chakshusheh |
baadhiryam muukatvam mukhaastat thaiva shrotra aadi dharmaah na tu vettuh aatmanah || 100 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Blindness, weakness, and sharpness are conditions of the eye, resulting simply from its soundness or its defects. Deafness, muteness, and the like likewise belong to the ear and the other organs. They never belong to the Ātman, the Knower.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Functions of Prāna</vt>
उच्छ्वासनिःश्वासविजृम्भणक्षुत् प्रस्यन्दनाद्युत्क्रमणादिकाः क्रियाः ।
प्राणादिकर्माणि वदन्ति तज्ञाः प्राणस्य धर्मावशनापिपासे ॥ १0२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Functions of Prāna</vt>
ucchvāsaniḥśvāsavijṛmbhaṇakṣut prasyandanādyutkramaṇādikāḥ kriyāḥ |
prāṇādikarmāṇi vadanti tajñāḥ prāṇasya dharmāvaśanāpipāse || 102 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Functions of Prāna</vt>
ucchvaasa nihshvaasa vijrimbhana ksut prasyandana aadi utkramana aadikaa kriyaah |
praana aadi karmaani vadanti tajnaah praanasya dharmaav ashana apipaase || 102 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Breathing in and out, yawning, sneezing, secretion, leaving this body, and so on are said by experts to be functions of Prāṇa and the others. Hunger and thirst are characteristics of Prāṇa proper.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Ego Discussed</vt>
अन्तःकरणमेतेषु चक्षुरादिषु वर्ष्मणि ।
अहमित्यभिमानेन तिष्ठत्याभासतेजसा ॥ १0३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Ego Discussed</vt>
antaḥkaraṇameteṣu cakṣurādiṣu varṣmaṇi |
ahamityabhimānena tiṣṭhatyābhāsatejasā || 103 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Ego Discussed</vt>
antahkaranam eteshu chakshur aadishu varshhmani |
aham iti abhimaanena tishthati aabhaasa tejasaa || 103 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The inner organ (mind) is seated in organs such as the eye and in the body. It identifies with them and is endowed with a reflection of the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
अहंकारः स विज्ञेयः कर्ता भोक्ताभिमान्ययम् ।
सत्त्वादिगुणयोगेन चावस्थात्रयमश्नुते ॥ १0४ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃkāraḥ sa vijñeyaḥ kartā bhoktābhimānyayam |
sattvādiguṇayogena cāvasthātrayamaśnute || 104 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahankaarah sah vijnaeyah kartaa bhoktaa abhimaanayam |
sattva aadi guna yogena cha avasthaa trayam ashnute || 104 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Understand that it is Egoism that identifies with the body and becomes the doer or the experiencer, and that, joined with the Guṇas such as Sattva, takes on the three different states.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयाणामानुकूल्ये सुखी दुःखी विपर्यये ।
सुखं दुःखं च तद्धर्मः सदानन्दस्य नात्मनः ॥ १0५ ॥
verses.roman:
viṣayāṇāmānukūlye sukhī duḥkhī viparyaye |
sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca taddharmaḥ sadānandasya nātmanaḥ || 105 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishayaanaam aanukuulye sukhii duhkhii viparyaye |
sukham duhkham cha tad dharmaah sadaanandasya na aatmanah || 105 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When sense objects are favorable, it is happy; when they are unfavorable, it is miserable. Happiness and misery therefore belong to Egoism and not to the ever-blissful Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Infinite Love - the Self</vt>
आत्मार्थत्वेन हि प्रेयान्विषयो न स्वतः प्रियः ।
स्वत एव हि सर्वेषामात्मा प्रियतमो यतः तत आत्मा सदानन्दो नास्य दुःखं कदाचन ॥ १0६ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Infinite Love - the Self</vt>
ātmārthatvena hi preyānviṣayo na svataḥ priyaḥ |
svata eva hi sarveṣāmātmā priyatamo yataḥ tata ātmā sadānando nāsya duḥkhaṃ kadācana || 106 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Infinite Love - the Self</vt>
aatma arthatvena hi preyaan vishayah na svatah priyah |
svatah eva hi sarvesham aatmaa priyatamah yatah tatah aatmaa sadaanandah na asya duhkham kadaachana || 106 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Sense objects give pleasure only in dependence on the Ātman manifesting through them, and never on their own, because the Ātman by Its very nature is what is most dear of all. So the Ātman is always blissful and never suffers misery.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्सुषुप्तौ निर्विषय आत्मानन्दोऽनुभूयते ।
श्रुतिः प्रत्यक्षमैतिह्यमनुमानं च जाग्रति ॥ १0७ ॥
verses.roman:
yatsuṣuptau nirviṣaya ātmānando'nubhūyate |
śrutiḥ pratyakṣamaitihyamanumānaṃ ca jāgrati || 107 ||
verses.colloquial:
yat sushuptau nirvisaya aatmaanandah anubhuuyate |
shrutih pratyaksham aitihyam anumaanaam cha jaagrati || 107 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Śruti, direct perception, tradition, and inference all clearly confirm that in deep sleep we experience the bliss of the Ātman without any sense objects.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Māyā - Pointed Out</vt>
अव्यक्तनाम्नी परमेशशक्तिः अनाद्यविद्या त्रिगुणात्मिका परा ।
कार्यानुमेया सुधियैव माया यया जगत्सर्वमिदं प्रसूयते ॥ १0८ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Māyā - Pointed Out</vt>
avyaktanāmnī parameśaśaktiḥ anādyavidyā triguṇātmikā parā |
kāryānumeyā sudhiyaiva māyā yayā jagatsarvamidaṃ prasūyate || 108 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Māyā - Pointed Out</vt>
avyakta naamni paramesh a shaktih anaadi avidyaa tri guna aatmikaa paraa |
kaarya anumeya su dhiyaa eva maayaa yayaa jagat sarvam idam prasuuyate || 108 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Avidya (Nescience), or Māyā, also called the Undifferentiated, is the power of the Lord. She has no beginning, consists of the three Guṇas, and is superior to the effects as their cause. A person of clear intellect can infer Her only from the effects She produces. It is She who gives birth to this entire universe.

verses.sanskrit:
सन्नाप्यसन्नाप्युभयात्मिका नो भिन्नाप्यभिन्नाप्युभयात्मिका नो ।
साङ्गाप्यनङ्गा ह्युभयात्मिका नो महाद्भुतानिर्वचनीयरूपा ॥ १0९ ॥
verses.roman:
sannāpyasannāpyubhayātmikā no bhinnāpyabhinnāpyubhayātmikā no |
sāṅgāpyanaṅgā hyubhayātmikā no mahādbhutānirvacanīyarūpā || 109 ||
verses.colloquial:
sannaa pi asannaa pi ubhaya aatmikaa no bhinnaa pi abhinnaa pi ubhaya aatmikaa no |
saangaa pi anangaa hi ubhaya aatmikaa no mahad adbhutaa nirvachaniiaya ruupaa || 109 ||
verses.translation_reworded: She is not existent, not non-existent, and not a mixture of the two. She is not the same, not different, and not both. She is not made of parts, not an indivisible whole, and not both. She is utterly wondrous and lies beyond description in words.

verses.sanskrit:
शुद्धाद्वयब्रह्मविभोधनाश्या सर्पभ्रमो रज्जुविवेकतो यथा ।
रजस्तमःसत्त्वमिति प्रसिद्धा गुणास्तदीयाः प्रथितैः स्वकार्यैः ॥ ११0 ॥
verses.roman:
śuddhādvayabrahmavibhodhanāśyā sarpabhramo rajjuvivekato yathā |
rajastamaḥsattvamiti prasiddhā guṇāstadīyāḥ prathitaiḥ svakāryaiḥ || 110 ||
verses.colloquial:
shuddha advaya brahma vibhodhana aashyaa sarpa bhramo rajju vivekato yathaa |
rajas tamah sattvam iti prasiddhaa gunaas tadiiyaah prathitaih sva kaaryaih || 110 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Māyā can be destroyed by realizing the pure Brahman, the one without a second, just as the mistaken notion of a snake is dispelled by recognizing the rope. Her Guṇas are Rajas, Tamas, and Sattva, each named for its function.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Rajoguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
विक्षेपशक्ती रजसः क्रियात्मिका यतः प्रवृत्तिः प्रसृता पुराणी ।
रागादयोऽस्याः प्रभवन्ति नित्यं दुःखादयो ये मनसो विकाराः ॥ १११ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Rajoguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
vikṣepaśaktī rajasaḥ kriyātmikā yataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā purāṇī |
rāgādayo'syāḥ prabhavanti nityaṃ duḥkhādayo ye manaso vikārāḥ || 111 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Rajoguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
vikshepa shaktii rajasah kriyaa aatmikaa yatah pravrittihi prasritaa puraanii |
raaga aadayo asyaah prabhavanti nityam duhkha aadayo ye manaso vikaaraah || 111 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Rajas has vikṣepa-Shakti, the projecting power, which is activity in nature. This primeval stream of activity flowed forth from it. From it, too, mental changes such as attachment and grief are constantly generated.

verses.sanskrit:
कामः क्रोधो लोभदम्भाद्यसूया अहंकारेर्ष्यामत्सराद्यास्तु घोराः ।
धर्मा एते राजसाः पुम्प्रवृत्तिः यस्मादेषा तद्रजो बन्धहेतुः ॥ ११२ ॥
verses.roman:
kāmaḥ krodho lobhadambhādyasūyā ahaṃkārerṣyāmatsarādyāstu ghorāḥ |
dharmā ete rājasāḥ pumpravṛttiḥ yasmādeṣā tadrajo bandhahetuḥ || 112 ||
verses.colloquial:
kaamah krodhah lobha dambha aadya asuuyaa ahankaar irshyaa matsara aadyaastu ghoraah |
dharmaah ete raajasaah pum pravrittihi yasmaat eshaa tad rajah bandha hetuh || 112 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Lust, anger, greed, arrogance, spite, egoism, envy, jealousy, and the like are the terrible attributes of Rajas, and they give rise to a person's worldly tendency. Rajas is therefore a cause of bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Tamoguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
एषावृतिर्नाम तमोगुणस्य शक्तिर्मया वस्त्ववभासतेऽन्यथा ।
सैषा निदानं पुरुषस्य संसृतेः विक्षेपशक्तेः प्रवणस्य हेतुः ॥ ११३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Tamoguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
eṣāvṛtirnāma tamoguṇasya śaktirmayā vastvavabhāsate'nyathā |
saiṣā nidānaṃ puruṣasya saṃsṛteḥ vikṣepaśakteḥ pravaṇasya hetuḥ || 113 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Tamoguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
esha aavritih naama tamo gunasya shaktih mayaa vastu avabhaasate anyathaa |
saa eshaa nidaanam purushasya samsriteh vikshepa shakteh pravaanasya hetuh || 113 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Āvṛti, the veiling power, is the power of Tamas that makes things seem other than they are. It is what causes a person's repeated transmigrations, and it sets the projecting power (Vikṣepa) in motion.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रज्ञावानपि पण्डितोऽपि चतुरोऽप्यत्यन्तसूक्ष्मात्मदृग् व्यालीढस्तमसा न वेत्ति बहुधा संबोधितोऽपि स्फुटम् ।
भ्रान्त्यारोपितमेव साधु कलयत्यालम्बते तद्गुणान् हन्तासौ प्रबला दुरन्ततमसः शक्तिर्महत्यावृतिः ॥ ११४ ॥
verses.roman:
prajñāvānapi paṇḍito'pi caturo'pyatyantasūkṣmātmadṛg vyālīḍhastamasā na vetti bahudhā saṃbodhito'pi sphuṭam |
bhrāntyāropitameva sādhu kalayatyālambate tadguṇān hantāsau prabalā durantatamasaḥ śaktirmahatyāvṛtiḥ || 114 ||
verses.colloquial:
prajnaavaan api panditah api chaturah api atyanta suukshma aatma drig vyaaliidhas tamasaa na vetti bahudhaa sambodhito api sphutam |
bhraantyaa aropitam eva saadhu kalayati aalambate tad gunaanaa hanta asau prabalaa dur anta tamasah shaktih mahati aavritih || 114 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Even wise and learned people, clever people skilled in perceiving the extremely subtle Ātman, are overcome by Tamas and fail to understand the Ātman, though it is plainly explained in many ways. They take as true what is only superimposed by delusion, and they cling to its effects. Alas, how mighty is the great Āvṛti Shakti of dreadful Tamas!

verses.sanskrit:
अभावना वा विपरीतभावना असंभावना विप्रतिपत्तिरस्याः ।
संसर्गयुक्तं न विमुञ्चति ध्रुवं विक्षेपशक्तिः क्षपयत्यजस्रम् ॥ ११५ ॥
verses.roman:
abhāvanā vā viparītabhāvanā asaṃbhāvanā vipratipattirasyāḥ |
saṃsargayuktaṃ na vimuñcati dhruvaṃ vikṣepaśaktiḥ kṣapayatyajasram || 115 ||
verses.colloquial:
abhaavana vaa vipariiata bhaavana asamhhaavana vipratipattih asyaah |
samsarga yuktam na vimuhnchati dhruvam vikshepa shaktih kshapayet ajasram || 115 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Lack of right judgment, wrong judgment, absence of firm conviction, and doubt never leave anyone who has any connection with this veiling power. The projecting power then causes endless trouble.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानमालस्यजडत्वनिद्रा प्रमादमूढत्वमुखास्तमोगुणाः ।
एतैः प्रयुक्तो नहि वेत्ति किंचिन् निद्रालुवत्स्तम्भवदेव तिष्ठति ॥ ११६ ॥
verses.roman:
ajñānamālasyajaḍatvanidrā pramādamūḍhatvamukhāstamoguṇāḥ |
etaiḥ prayukto nahi vetti kiṃcin nidrāluvatstambhavadeva tiṣṭhati || 116 ||
verses.colloquial:
ajnaanam aalasya jadatva nidraa pramaada muudhatva mukhaastamogunaah |
etaih prayuktah na hi vetti kinchhin nidraaluvat stambha vad eva tishthati || 116 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance, lethargy, dullness, sleep, carelessness, stupidity, and the like are attributes of Tamas. Someone bound by them grasps nothing and remains like a sleeper, or like a post or a stone.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Sattvaguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
सत्त्वं विशुद्धं जलवत्तथापि ताभ्यां मिलित्वा सरणाय कल्पते ।
यत्रात्मबिम्बः प्रतिबिम्बितः सन् प्रकाशयत्यर्क इवाखिलं जडम् ॥ ११७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Sattvaguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
sattvaṃ viśuddhaṃ jalavattathāpi tābhyāṃ militvā saraṇāya kalpate |
yatrātmabimbaḥ pratibimbitaḥ san prakāśayatyarka ivākhilaṃ jaḍam || 117 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Sattvaguņa - Nature and Effects</vt>
sattvam vishuddham jala vat tathaapi taabhyaam militvaa saranaya kalpate |
yatra aatma bimbah pratibimbitah san prakaashayati arka iva akhilam jadam || 117 ||
