verses.translation_reworded: Pure Sattva is clear like water, yet when joined with Rajas and Tamas it leads to transmigration. The reality of the Ātman is reflected in Sattva and, like the sun, illuminates the whole world of matter.

verses.sanskrit:
मिश्रस्य सत्त्वस्य भवन्ति धर्माः त्वमानिताद्या नियमा यमाद्याः ।
श्रद्धा च भक्तिश्च मुमुक्षता च दैवी च सम्पत्तिरसन्निवृत्तिः ॥ ११८ ॥
verses.roman:
miśrasya sattvasya bhavanti dharmāḥ tvamānitādyā niyamā yamādyāḥ |
śraddhā ca bhaktiśca mumukṣatā ca daivī ca sampattirasannivṛttiḥ || 118 ||
verses.colloquial:
mishrasya sattvasya bhavanti dharmaah tv amaanita aadyaa niyamaa yama aadyaah |
shraddhaa cha bhaktih cha mumukshhataa cha daivii cha sampattih asat nivrittihi || 118 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Mixed Sattva shows itself in a complete absence of pride and the like, in Niyama, Yama, and so on, and in faith, devotion, longing for Liberation, the divine tendencies, and turning away from the unreal.

verses.sanskrit:
विशुद्धसत्त्वस्य गुणाः प्रसादः स्वात्मानुभूतिः परमा प्रशान्तिः ।
तृप्तिः प्रहर्षः परमात्मनिष्ठा यया सदानन्दरसं समृच्छति ॥ ११९ ॥
verses.roman:
viśuddhasattvasya guṇāḥ prasādaḥ svātmānubhūtiḥ paramā praśāntiḥ |
tṛptiḥ praharṣaḥ paramātmaniṣṭhā yayā sadānandarasaṃ samṛcchati || 119 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishuddha sattvasya gunaah prasaadah sv aatmaa anubhuutih paramaa prashhaantih |
triptih praharshoh paramaa aatma nishthaa yayaa sadaa aananda rasam samrichchhati || 119 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Pure Sattva shows itself in cheerfulness, realization of one's own Self, supreme peace, contentment, bliss, and steady devotion to the Ātman, through which the aspirant enjoys everlasting bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Causal Body - Its Nature</vt>
अव्यक्तमेतत्त्रिगुणैर्निरुक्तं तत्कारणं नाम शरीरमात्मनः ।
सुषुप्तिरेतस्य विभक्त्यवस्था प्रलीनसर्वेन्द्रियबुद्धिवृत्तिः ॥ १२0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Causal Body - Its Nature</vt>
avyaktametattriguṇairniruktaṃ tatkāraṇaṃ nāma śarīramātmanaḥ |
suṣuptiretasya vibhaktyavasthā pralīnasarvendriyabuddhivṛttiḥ || 120 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Causal Body - Its Nature</vt>
avyaktam etat tri gunaih niruktam tat kaaranam naama shariram aatmanah |
sushuptir etasya vibhakti avasthaa praliinat sarva indriya buddhi vrittih || 120 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The causal body of the soul is this Undifferentiated, which is said to be a compound of the three Guṇas. Its particular state is deep sleep, when the mind and all the organs stop functioning.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वप्रकारप्रमितिप्रशान्तिः बीजात्मनावस्थितिरेव बुद्धेः ।
सुषुप्तिरेतस्य किल प्रतीतिः किंचिन्न वेद्मीति जगत्प्रसिद्धेः ॥ १२१ ॥
verses.roman:
sarvaprakārapramitipraśāntiḥ bījātmanāvasthitireva buddheḥ |
suṣuptiretasya kila pratītiḥ kiṃcinna vedmīti jagatprasiddheḥ || 121 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarva prakaara pramiti prashaantih biija aatmanaa avasthitir eva buddhe |
sushuptir etasya kila pratiitih kimcin na vedmiiti jagat prasiddheh || 121 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In deep sleep every kind of perception stops, and the mind stays on in a subtle, seed-like form. The proof is what everyone says afterward: "I knew nothing then."

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Not-Self - Description</vt>
देहेन्द्रियप्राणमनोऽहमादयः सर्वे विकारा विषयाः सुखादयः ।
व्योमादिभूतान्यखिलं न विश्वं अव्यक्तपर्यन्तमिदं ह्यनात्मा ॥ १२२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Not-Self - Description</vt>
dehendriyaprāṇamano'hamādayaḥ sarve vikārā viṣayāḥ sukhādayaḥ |
vyomādibhūtānyakhilaṃ na viśvaṃ avyaktaparyantamidaṃ hyanātmā || 122 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Not-Self - Description</vt>
deha indriya praana mano aham aadayah sarve vikaaraa vishaayaah sukha aadayah |
vyoma aadi bhuutaani akhilam vishvam avyakta paryantam idam hi anaatmaa || 122 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The body, the organs, the Prāṇas, Manas, egoism and the like, all modifications, the objects of the senses, pleasure and so on, the gross elements such as ether, indeed the entire universe up to the Undifferentiated: all of this is the non-Self.

verses.sanskrit:
माया मायाकार्यं सर्वं महदादिदेहपर्यन्तम् ।
असदिदमनात्मतत्त्वं विद्धि त्वं मरुमरीचिकाकल्पम् ॥ १२३ ॥
verses.roman:
māyā māyākāryaṃ sarvaṃ mahadādidehaparyantam |
asadidamanātmatattvaṃ viddhi tvaṃ marumarīcikākalpam || 123 ||
verses.colloquial:
maayaa maayaa kaaryam sarvam mahad aadi deha paryantam |
asad idam anaatma tattvam viddhi tvam maru mariicikaa kalpam || 123 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Everything from Mahat down to the gross body is produced by Māyā. Understand that all these, and Māyā itself, are the non-Self, and so are as unreal as a mirage in the desert.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Self - Its Nature</vt>
अथ ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि स्वरूपं परमात्मनः ।
यद्विज्ञाय नरो बन्धान्मुक्तः कैवल्यमश्नुते ॥ १२४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Self - Its Nature</vt>
atha te saṃpravakṣyāmi svarūpaṃ paramātmanaḥ |
yadvijñāya naro bandhānmuktaḥ kaivalyamaśnute || 124 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Self - Its Nature</vt>
atha te sampravakshaami svaruupam param aatmanah |
yad vijnaaya naro bandhaan muktah kaivalyam ashnute || 124 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Now I will explain to you the true nature of the supreme Self. By realizing it, a person is released from bondage and attains Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्ति कश्चित्स्वयं नित्यमहंप्रत्ययलम्बनः ।
अवस्थात्रयसाक्षी संपञ्चकोशविलक्षणः ॥ १२५ ॥
verses.roman:
asti kaścitsvayaṃ nityamahaṃpratyayalambanaḥ |
avasthātrayasākṣī saṃpañcakośavilakṣaṇaḥ || 125 ||
verses.colloquial:
asti kashcit svayam nityam aham pratyaya lambhanah |
avasthaa traya saakshii san panca kosha vilakshanah || 125 ||
verses.translation_reworded: There is a certain Absolute Entity that is the eternal ground of the sense of ego. It witnesses the three states and is distinct from the five sheaths or coverings.

verses.sanskrit:
यो विजानाति सकलं जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु ।
बुद्धितद्वृत्तिसद्भावमभावमहमित्ययम् ॥ १२६ ॥
verses.roman:
yo vijānāti sakalaṃ jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu |
buddhitadvṛttisadbhāvamabhāvamahamityayam || 126 ||
verses.colloquial:
yo vijaanaati sakalam jaagrat svapna sushuptishu |
buddhi tad vritti sad bhaavam abhaavam aham ity ayam || 126 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It knows all that occurs in waking, in dream, and in deep sleep. It is aware of whether the mind and its functions are present or absent. It underlies the notion of ego. This is That.

verses.sanskrit:
यः पश्यति स्वयं सर्वं यं न पश्यति कश्चन ।
यश्चेतयति बुद्ध्यादि न तद्यं चेतयत्ययम् ॥ १२७ ॥
verses.roman:
yaḥ paśyati svayaṃ sarvaṃ yaṃ na paśyati kaścana |
yaścetayati buddhyādi na tadyaṃ cetayatyayam || 127 ||
verses.colloquial:
yah pashyati svayam sarvam yam na pashyati kashcana |
yash cetayati buddhi aadi na tad yam cetayati ayam || 127 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It sees everything, yet no one sees It. It lights up the intellect and the rest, yet they cannot light It up. This is That.

verses.sanskrit:
येन विश्वमिदं व्याप्तं यं न व्याप्नोति किंचन ।
अभारूपमिदं सर्वं यं भान्त्यमनुभात्ययम् ॥ १२८ ॥
verses.roman:
yena viśvamidaṃ vyāptaṃ yaṃ na vyāpnoti kiṃcana |
abhārūpamidaṃ sarvaṃ yaṃ bhāntyamanubhātyayam || 128 ||
verses.colloquial:
yena vishvam idam vyaaptam yam na vyaapnoti kimcana |
aabhaa ruupam idam sarvam yam bhaanti anu bhaaty ayam || 128 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It pervades this universe, yet nothing pervades It. When It shines, all this (universe) shines as Its reflection. This is That.

verses.sanskrit:
यस्य सन्निधिमात्रेण देहेन्द्रियमनोधियः ।
विषयेषु स्वकीयेषु वर्तन्ते प्रेरिता इव ॥ १२९ ॥
verses.roman:
yasya sannidhimātreṇa dehendriyamanodhiyaḥ |
viṣayeṣu svakīyeṣu vartante preritā iva || 129 ||
verses.colloquial:
yasya sannidhi maatrenaa deha indriya mano dhiyah |
vishaayeshu svaakiiyeshu vartante preritaa iva || 129 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Simply because It is present, the body, the organs, the mind, and the intellect stay within their own fields of action, as servants do!

verses.sanskrit:
अहङ्कारादिदेहान्ता विषयाश्च सुखादयः ।
वेद्यन्ते घटवद्येन नित्यबोधस्वरूपिणा ॥ १३0 ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṅkārādidehāntā viṣayāśca sukhādayaḥ |
vedyante ghaṭavadyena nityabodhasvarūpiṇā || 130 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahamkaara aadi deha antaa vishaayaash ca sukha aadayah |
vedyante ghata vad yena nitya bodha svaruupinaa || 130 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through It, everything from the ego down to the body, the objects of the senses, pleasure and so on is known as plainly as a jar, for It is the very essence of Eternal Knowledge!

verses.sanskrit:
एषोऽन्तरात्मा पुरुषः पुराणो निरन्तराखण्डसुखानुभूतिः ।
सदैकरूपः प्रतिबोधमात्रो येनेषिता वागसवश्चरन्ति ॥ १३१ ॥
verses.roman:
eṣo'ntarātmā puruṣaḥ purāṇo nirantarākhaṇḍasukhānubhūtiḥ |
sadaikarūpaḥ pratibodhamātro yeneṣitā vāgasavaścaranti || 131 ||
verses.colloquial:
esho antar aatmaa purushah puraano nirantara akhanda sukha anubhuutih |
sadaa eka ruupah prati bodha maatrah yena ishitaa vaag asavash caranti || 131 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This is the innermost Self, the primeval Purusha (Being). Its essence is the unbroken experience of infinite Bliss. It stays always the same, yet is reflected through the various modifications of the mind, and at Its command the organs and Prāṇas carry out their work.

verses.sanskrit:
अत्रैव सत्त्वात्मनि धीगुहायां अव्याकृताकाश उशत्प्रकाशः ।
आकाश उच्चै रविवत्प्रकाशते स्वतेजसा विश्वमिदं प्रकाशयन् ॥ १३२ ॥
verses.roman:
atraiva sattvātmani dhīguhāyāṃ avyākṛtākāśa uśatprakāśaḥ |
ākāśa uccai ravivatprakāśate svatejasā viśvamidaṃ prakāśayan || 132 ||
verses.colloquial:
atra eva sattva aatmani dhii guhaayaam avyaakrita aakaashe ushat prakashah |
aakaashe uccai ravi vat prakaashate sva tejasaa vishvam idam prakaashayan || 132 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Right here in this body, in the mind full of Sattva, in the hidden chamber of the intellect, in the Akasha called the Unmanifested, the Ātman of enchanting splendor shines like the sun on high, revealing this universe by Its own radiance.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञाता मनोऽहंकृतिविक्रियाणां देहेन्द्रियप्राणकृतक्रियाणाम् ।
अयोऽग्निवत्ताननुवर्तमानो न चेष्टते नो विकरोति किंचन ॥ १३३ ॥
verses.roman:
jñātā mano'haṃkṛtivikriyāṇāṃ dehendriyaprāṇakṛtakriyāṇām |
ayo'gnivattānanuvartamāno na ceṣṭate no vikaroti kiṃcana || 133 ||
verses.colloquial:
jnaataa mano aham kriti vikriyaanaam deha indriya praana krita kriyaanaam |
ayo agni vat taan anuvartamaano na ceshtate no vikaroti kimcana || 133 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It knows the movements of the mind and ego, and the activities of the body, organs, and Prāṇas. It seems to take on their forms, as fire takes the form of a ball of iron. Yet It does not act and does not change in the slightest.

verses.sanskrit:
न जायते नो म्रियते न वर्धते न क्षीयते नो विकरोति नित्यः ।
विलीयमानेऽपि वपुष्यमुष्मिन् न लीयते कुम्भ इवाम्बरं स्वयम् ॥ १३४ ॥
verses.roman:
na jāyate no mriyate na vardhate na kṣīyate no vikaroti nityaḥ |
vilīyamāne'pi vapuṣyamuṣmin na līyate kumbha ivāmbaraṃ svayam || 134 ||
verses.colloquial:
na jaayate no mriyate na vardhate na kshiiyate no vikaroti nityah |
viliiyamaane api vapushi amusmin na liiyate kumbha iva ambaram svayam || 134 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is not born and does not die. It neither grows nor declines, and being eternal It undergoes no change. It does not stop existing even when this body is destroyed, just as the sky in a jar remains (after the jar is broken), because It depends on nothing.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रकृतिविकृतिभिन्नः शुद्धबोधस्वभावः सदसदिदमशेषं भासयन्निर्विशेषः ।
विलसति परमात्मा जाग्रदादिष्ववस्था स्वहमहमिति साक्षात्साक्षिरूपेण बुद्धेः ॥ १३५ ॥
verses.roman:
prakṛtivikṛtibhinnaḥ śuddhabodhasvabhāvaḥ sadasadidamaśeṣaṃ bhāsayannirviśeṣaḥ |
vilasati paramātmā jāgradādiṣvavasthā svahamahamiti sākṣātsākṣirūpeṇa buddheḥ || 135 ||
verses.colloquial:
prakriti vikrti bhinnah shuddha bodha svabhaavah sad asad idam ashesham bhaasayan nirvisheshuh |
vilasati param aatmaa jaagrat aadishu avasthaa sva aham aham iti saakshaat saakshi ruupena buddhe || 135 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Supreme Self is different from Prakriti and its modifications; Its essence is Pure Knowledge, and It is Absolute. In waking and the other states It directly reveals this whole gross and subtle universe as the ground of the persisting sense of ego, and It reveals Itself as the Witness of the Buddhi, the faculty that determines.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Advice for Self-control</vt>
नियमितमनसामुं त्वं स्वमात्मानमात्मन्य् अयमहमिति साक्षाद्विद्धि बुद्धिप्रसादात् ।
जनिमरणतरङ्गापारसंसारसिन्धुं प्रतर भव कृतार्थो ब्रह्मरूपेण संस्थः ॥ १३६ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Advice for Self-control</vt>
niyamitamanasāmuṃ tvaṃ svamātmānamātmany ayamahamiti sākṣādviddhi buddhiprasādāt |
janimaraṇataraṅgāpārasaṃsārasindhuṃ pratara bhava kṛtārtho brahmarūpeṇa saṃsthaḥ || 136 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Advice for Self-control</vt>
niyamita manasaa amum tvam svam aatmaanam aatmani ayam aham iti saakshaad viddhi buddhi prasaadaat |
jani marana taranga apaara samsaara sindhum pratara bhava krita artho brahma ruupena samsthah || 136 ||
verses.translation_reworded: With a disciplined mind and a purified intellect (Buddhi), directly realize your own Self within the body and become one with It. Cross the endless ocean of Samsara, whose waves are birth and death, and be blessed, firmly rooted in Brahman as your own essence.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>What is Bondage - The Reply</vt>
अत्रानात्मन्यहमिति मतिर्बन्ध एषोऽस्य पुंसः प्राप्तोऽज्ञानाज्जननमरणक्लेशसंपातहेतुः ।
येनैवायं वपुरिदमसत्सत्यमित्यात्मबुद्ध्या पुष्यत्युक्षत्यवति विषयैस्तन्तुभिः कोशकृद्वत् ॥ १३७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>What is Bondage - The Reply</vt>
atrānātmanyahamiti matirbandha eṣo'sya puṃsaḥ prāpto'jñānājjananamaraṇakleśasaṃpātahetuḥ |
yenaivāyaṃ vapuridamasatsatyamityātmabuddhyā puṣyatyukṣatyavati viṣayaistantubhiḥ kośakṛdvat || 137 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>What is Bondage - The Reply</vt>
atra anaatmani aham iti matir bandha esho asya pumsah praapto ajnaanaat janana marana klesha sampaata hetuh |
yena eva ayam vapuh idam asat satyam ity aatma buddhyaa pushyati ukshati avati vishaayais tantubhih kosha krit vat || 137 ||
verses.translation_reworded: To identify the Self with what is not the Self: this is human bondage. It comes from ignorance and brings the sufferings of birth and death in its wake. Because of it, a person takes this fleeting body to be real, identifies with it, and feeds, bathes, and protects it with (pleasant) objects of the senses. In this way he becomes bound, as a caterpillar is bound by the threads of its cocoon.

verses.sanskrit:
अतस्मिंस्तद्बुद्धिः प्रभवति विमूढस्य तमसा विवेकाभावाद्वै स्फुरति भुजगे रज्जुधिषणा ।
ततोऽनर्थव्रातो निपतति समादातुरधिकः ततो योऽसद्ग्राहः स हि भवति बन्धः शृणु सखे ॥ १३८ ॥
verses.roman:
atasmiṃstadbuddhiḥ prabhavati vimūḍhasya tamasā vivekābhāvādvai sphurati bhujage rajjudhiṣaṇā |
tato'narthavrāto nipatati samādāturadhikaḥ tato yo'sadgrāhaḥ sa hi bhavati bandhaḥ śṛṇu sakhe || 138 ||
verses.colloquial:
atasmin tad buddhih prabhavati vimuudasya tamasaa viveka abhaavaat vai sphurati bhujage rajju dhishanaa |
tato anarthavraato nipatati sam aadaatuh adhikah tato yo asad graahah sa hi bhavati bandhah shrinu sakhe || 138 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Someone overcome by ignorance takes a thing to be what it is not. Lack of discrimination makes a person mistake a snake for a rope, and when he grabs it under that false idea, great danger comes upon him. So listen, my friend: taking passing things to be real is what constitutes bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
अखण्डनित्याद्वयबोधशक्त्या स्फुरन्तमात्मानमनन्तवैभवम् ।
समावृणोत्यावृतिशक्तिरेषा तमोमयी राहुरिवार्कबिम्बम् ॥ १३९ ॥
verses.roman:
akhaṇḍanityādvayabodhaśaktyā sphurantamātmānamanantavaibhavam |
samāvṛṇotyāvṛtiśaktireṣā tamomayī rāhurivārkabimbam || 139 ||
verses.colloquial:
akhanda nitya advaya bodha shaktyaa sphurantam aatmaanam ananta vaibhavam |
sam aavrinoti aavrti shaktir eshaa tamo mayii raahu iva arka bimbam || 139 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This veiling power (Avriti), which dominates in ignorance, covers the Self, just as Rāhu covers the disc of the sun. The Self has infinite glories, reveals Itself through the power of knowledge, and is indivisible, eternal, and one without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
तिरोभूते स्वात्मन्यमलतरतेजोवति पुमान् अनात्मानं मोहादहमिति शरीरं कलयति ।
ततः कामक्रोधप्रभृतिभिरमुं बन्धनगुणैः परं विक्षेपाख्या रजस उरुशक्तिर्व्यथयति ॥ १४0 ॥
verses.roman:
tirobhūte svātmanyamalataratejovati pumān anātmānaṃ mohādahamiti śarīraṃ kalayati |
tataḥ kāmakrodhaprabhṛtibhiramuṃ bandhanaguṇaiḥ paraṃ vikṣepākhyā rajasa uruśaktirvyathayati || 140 ||
verses.colloquial:
tiro bhuute sva aatmani amala tara tejo vati pumaan anaatmaanam mohaad aham iti shariram kalayati |
tatah kaama krodha prabhritibhih amum bandhana gunaih param vikshepa aakhyaa rajasa uru shaktir vyathayati || 140 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When a person's own Self, shining with the purest splendor, is hidden from sight, ignorance leads him to identify falsely with this body, which is the non-Self. Then the great power of rajas known as the projecting power torments him severely with the binding chains of lust, anger, and the like.

verses.sanskrit:
महामोहग्राहग्रसनगलितात्मावगमनो धियो नानावस्थां स्वयमभिनयंस्तद्गुणतया ।
अपारे संसरे विषयविषपूरे जलनिधौ निमज्योन्मज्यायं भ्रमति कुमतिः कुत्सितगतिः ॥ १४१ ॥
verses.roman:
mahāmohagrāhagrasanagalitātmāvagamano dhiyo nānāvasthāṃ svayamabhinayaṃstadguṇatayā |
apāre saṃsare viṣayaviṣapūre jalanidhau nimajyonmajyāyaṃ bhramati kumatiḥ kutsitagatiḥ || 141 ||
verses.colloquial:
mahaa moha graaha grasana galita aatma avagamanah dhiyo naanaa avasthaam svayam abhinayan tad gunatayaa |
apaare samsaare vishaya visha puure jala nidhau nimajya unmajya ayam bhramati kumatih kutsita gatih || 141 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A person of distorted intellect, whose Self-knowledge has been swallowed by the shark of total ignorance, imitates the various states of the intellect (Buddhi), since that is Its superimposed attribute. He drifts up and down in this limitless ocean of Samsara, full of the poison of sense-enjoyment, now sinking, now rising. What a wretched fate!

verses.sanskrit:
भानुप्रभासंजनिताभ्रपङ्क्तिः भानुं तिरोधाय विजृम्भते यथा ।
आत्मोदिताहंकृतिरात्मतत्त्वं तथा तिरोधाय विजृम्भते स्वयम् ॥ १४२ ॥
verses.roman:
bhānuprabhāsaṃjanitābhrapaṅktiḥ bhānuṃ tirodhāya vijṛmbhate yathā |
ātmoditāhaṃkṛtirātmatattvaṃ tathā tirodhāya vijṛmbhate svayam || 142 ||
verses.colloquial:
bhaanu prabhaa sam janita abhra panktih bhaanum tiro dhaaya vijrimbhate yathaa |
aatma uditaa aham kritih aatma tattvam tathaa tiro dhaaya vijrimbhate svayam || 142 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Banks of cloud produced by the sun's rays cover the sun, and they alone are then visible (in the sky). In the same way ego, produced by the Self, covers the reality of the Self and appears on its own.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Powers - Agitation and Veiling</vt>
कवलितदिननार्थे दुर्दिने सान्द्रमेघैः व्यथयति हिमझंझावायुरुग्रो यथैतान् ।
अविरततमसात्मन्यावृते मूढबुद्धिं क्षपयति बहुदुःखैस्तीव्रविक्षेपशक्तिः ॥ १४३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Powers - Agitation and Veiling</vt>
kavalitadinanārthe durdine sāndrameghaiḥ vyathayati himajhaṃjhāvāyurugro yathaitān |
aviratatamasātmanyāvṛte mūḍhabuddhiṃ kṣapayati bahuduḥkhaistīvravikṣepaśaktiḥ || 143 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Powers - Agitation and Veiling</vt>
kavalita dina aarthe dur dine saandra meghais vyathayati hima jhanjhaa vaayur ugro yathaa etaan |
avirata tamasaa aatmani aavrite muudha buddhim kshapayati bahu duhkhais tiivra vikshepa shaktih || 143 ||
verses.translation_reworded: On an overcast day, when thick clouds have swallowed the sun, fierce cold winds harass them. In the same way, when intense ignorance has hidden the Ātman, the terrible Vikṣepa Shakti (projecting power) afflicts the foolish person with many sorrows.

verses.sanskrit:
एताभ्यामेव शक्तिभ्यां बन्धः पुंसः समागतः ।
याभ्यां विमोहितो देहं मत्वात्मानं भ्रमत्ययम् ॥ १४४ ॥
verses.roman:
etābhyāmeva śaktibhyāṃ bandhaḥ puṃsaḥ samāgataḥ |
yābhyāṃ vimohito dehaṃ matvātmānaṃ bhramatyayam || 144 ||
verses.colloquial:
etaabhyaam eva shaktibhyaam bandhah pumsah samaagataah |
yaabhyaam vimohito deham matvaa aatmaanam bhramaty ayam || 144 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Human bondage has arisen from these two powers. Deceived by them, a person mistakes the body for the Self and wanders (from body to body).

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Bondage in Action</vt>
बीजं संसृतिभूमिजस्य तु तमो देहात्मधीरङ्कुरो रागः पल्लवमम्बु कर्म तु वपुः स्कन्धोओऽसवः शाखिकाः ।
अग्राणीन्द्रियसंहतिश्च विषयाः पुष्पाणि दुःखं फलं नानाकर्मसमुद्भवं बहुविधं भोक्तात्र जीवः खगः ॥ १४५ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Bondage in Action</vt>
bījaṃ saṃsṛtibhūmijasya tu tamo dehātmadhīraṅkuro rāgaḥ pallavamambu karma tu vapuḥ skandhoo'savaḥ śākhikāḥ |
agrāṇīndriyasaṃhatiśca viṣayāḥ puṣpāṇi duḥkhaṃ phalaṃ nānākarmasamudbhavaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhoktātra jīvaḥ khagaḥ || 145 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Bondage in Action</vt>
biijam samsriti bhuumijasya tu tamo deha aatma dhii ankuro raagah pallavam ambu karma tu vapuh skandhah asavah shaakhikaa |
agra indriya samhatish ca vishaayaah pushpaani duhkham phalam naanaa karma sam udbhavam bahu vidham bhoktaa atra jiivah khagah || 145 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance is the seed of the tree of Samsara. Identification with the body is its sprout, attachment its tender leaves, work its water, the body its trunk, the vital forces its branches, the organs its twigs, the objects of the senses its flowers, the many sufferings from various works its fruits, and the individual soul is the bird sitting on it.

verses.sanskrit:
अज्ञानमूलोऽयमनात्मबन्धो नैसर्गिकोऽनादिरनन्त ईरितः ।
जन्माप्ययव्याधिजरादिदुःख प्रवाहपातं जनयत्यमुष्य ॥ १४६ ॥
verses.roman:
ajñānamūlo'yamanātmabandho naisargiko'nādirananta īritaḥ |
janmāpyayavyādhijarādiduḥkha pravāhapātaṃ janayatyamuṣya || 146 ||
verses.colloquial:
ajnaana muulo ayam anaatma bandho naisargiko anaadir ananta iiritah |
janma apyaya vyaadhi jaraa aadi duhkha pravaaha paatam janayaty amusya || 146 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This bondage of the non-Self arises from ignorance, is self-caused, and is said to be without beginning or end. It exposes a person to the long chain of sufferings such as birth, death, disease, and old age.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Ātman and Anātman - Discrimination</vt>
नास्त्रैर्न शस्त्रैरनिलेन वन्हिना छेत्तुं न शक्यो न च कर्मकोटिभिः ।
विवेकविज्ञानमहासिना विना धातुः प्रसादेन शितेन मञ्जुना ॥ १४७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Ātman and Anātman - Discrimination</vt>
nāstrairna śastrairanilena vanhinā chettuṃ na śakyo na ca karmakoṭibhiḥ |
vivekavijñānamahāsinā vinā dhātuḥ prasādena śitena mañjunā || 147 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Aatman and Anaatman - Discrimination</vt>
na astrair na shastrair anilena vanhinaa chettum na shakyo na ca karma kotibhih |
viveka vijnaana mahaa asinaa vinaa dhaatuh prasaadena shitena manjunaa || 147 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Weapons cannot destroy this bondage, nor wind, nor fire, nor millions of acts. Nothing can, except the marvelous sword of knowledge born of discrimination and sharpened by the grace of the Lord.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतिप्रमाणैकमतेः स्वधर्म निष्ठा तयैवात्मविशुद्धिरस्य ।
विशुद्धबुद्धेः परमात्मवेदनं तेनैव संसारसमूलनाशः ॥ १४८ ॥
verses.roman:
śrutipramāṇaikamateḥ svadharma niṣṭhā tayaivātmaviśuddhirasya |
viśuddhabuddheḥ paramātmavedanaṃ tenaiva saṃsārasamūlanāśaḥ || 148 ||
verses.colloquial:
shruti pramaana eka mateh sva dharma nishthaa tayaa eva aatma vishuddhir asya |
vishuddha buddhe param aatma vedanam tena eva samsaara samuula naashaha || 148 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whoever is ardently devoted to the authority of the Śrutis becomes steady in his Svadharma, and that alone leads to purity of mind. A person of pure mind realizes the Supreme Self, and by this alone Samsara is destroyed, root and all.

verses.sanskrit:
कोशैरन्नमयाद्यैः पञ्चभिरात्मा न संवृतो भाति ।
निजशक्तिसमुत्पन्नैः शैवालपटलैरिवाम्बु वापीस्थम् ॥ १४९ ॥
verses.roman:
kośairannamayādyaiḥ pañcabhirātmā na saṃvṛto bhāti |
nijaśaktisamutpannaiḥ śaivālapaṭalairivāmbu vāpīstham || 149 ||
verses.colloquial:
koshaih anna mayaa aadyaih pancabhir aatmaa na samvrto bhaati |
nija shakti sam utpannaih shaivaalaa patalai iva ambu vaapii stham || 149 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Covered by the five sheaths, starting with the material one, which are products of Its own power, the Self no longer appears, just as the water of a tank is hidden when moss builds up on it.

verses.sanskrit:
तच्छैवालापनये सम्यक्सलिलं प्रतीयते शुद्धम् ।
तृष्णासन्तापहरं सद्यः सौख्यप्रदं परं पुंसः ॥ १५0 ॥
verses.roman:
tacchaivālāpanaye samyaksalilaṃ pratīyate śuddham |
tṛṣṇāsantāpaharaṃ sadyaḥ saukhyapradaṃ paraṃ puṃsaḥ || 150 ||
verses.colloquial:
tac chaivaalaa apanaye samyak saliilam pratiiyate shuddham |
trishnaa santaapa haram sadyah saukhya pradam param pumsah || 150 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When that moss is cleared away, perfectly pure water, which relieves the pain of thirst and brings instant joy, lies open before the person.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चानामपि कोशानामपवादे विभात्ययं शुद्धः ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसः प्रत्यग्रूपः परः स्वयंज्योतिः ॥ १५१ ॥
verses.roman:
pañcānāmapi kośānāmapavāde vibhātyayaṃ śuddhaḥ |
nityānandaikarasaḥ pratyagrūpaḥ paraḥ svayaṃjyotiḥ || 151 ||
verses.colloquial:
pancaanaam api koshaanaam apavaade vibhaaty ayam shuddhah |
nitya ananda eka rasah pratyag ruupah parah svayam jyotih || 151 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When all five sheaths have been set aside, a person's Self appears: pure, made of lasting and unmixed bliss, indwelling, supreme, and self-radiant.

verses.sanskrit:
आत्मानात्मविवेकः कर्तव्यो बन्धमुक्तये विदुषा ।
तेनैवानन्दी भवति स्वं विज्ञाय सच्चिदानन्दम् ॥ १५२ ॥
verses.roman:
ātmānātmavivekaḥ kartavyo bandhamuktaye viduṣā |
tenaivānandī bhavati svaṃ vijñāya saccidānandam || 152 ||
verses.colloquial:
aatmaa anaatma vivekah kartavyo bandha muktaye vidushaa |
tena eva aanandii bhavati svam vijnaaya sac cid aanandam || 152 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A wise person who wants to end his bondage should discriminate between the Self and the non-Self. That alone lets him know his own Self as Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, and he becomes happy.

verses.sanskrit:
मुञ्जादिषीकामिव दृश्यवर्गात् प्रत्यञ्चमात्मानमसङ्गमक्रियम् ।
विविच्य तत्र प्रविलाप्य सर्वं तदात्मना तिष्ठति यः स मुक्तः ॥ १५३ ॥
verses.roman:
muñjādiṣīkāmiva dṛśyavargāt pratyañcamātmānamasaṅgamakriyam |
vivicya tatra pravilāpya sarvaṃ tadātmanā tiṣṭhati yaḥ sa muktaḥ || 153 ||
verses.colloquial:
munja aadi shiikaam iva drishya vargaat pratyancam aatmaanam asangam akriyam |
vivicya tatra pravilaapya sarvam tad aatmanaa tishtati yah sa muktah || 153 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That person is truly free who separates all objects of the senses from the indwelling, unattached, and inactive Self, the way one pulls a stalk of grass from its enclosing sheath, and who, merging everything in It, stays in identity with That.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>a) Annamaya kośa (Food sheath)</vt>
देहोऽयमन्नभवनोऽन्नमायास्तु कोशः चान्नेन जीवति विनश्यति तद्विहीनः ।
त्वक्चर्ममांसरुधिरास्थिपुरीषराशिः नायं स्वयं भवितुमर्हति नित्यशुद्धः ॥ १५४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>a) Annamaya kośa (Food sheath)</vt>
deho'yamannabhavano'nnaMāyāstu kośaḥ cānnena jīvati vinaśyati tadvihīnaḥ |
tvakcarmamāṃsarudhirāsthipurīṣarāśiḥ nāyaṃ svayaṃ bhavitumarhati nityaśuddhaḥ || 154 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>a) Annamaya kosha (Food sheath)</vt>
deho ayam anna bhavanah anna maayaas tu koshah ca annena jiivati vinashyati tad viihinah |
tvak carma maamsaa rudhira asthi puriisha raashih na ayam svayam bhavitum arhati nitya shuddhah || 154 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This body of ours is made from food and constitutes the material sheath. It lives on food and dies without it. It is a heap of skin, flesh, blood, bones, and filth, and it can never be the eternally pure, self-existent Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
पूर्वं जनेरधिमृतेरपि नायमस्ति जातक्षणः क्षणगुणोऽनियतस्वभावः ।
नैको जडश्च घटवत्परिदृश्यमानः स्वात्मा कथं भवति भावविकारवेत्ता ॥ १५५ ॥
verses.roman:
pūrvaṃ janeradhimṛterapi nāyamasti jātakṣaṇaḥ kṣaṇaguṇo'niyatasvabhāvaḥ |
naiko jaḍaśca ghaṭavatparidṛśyamānaḥ svātmā kathaṃ bhavati bhāvavikāravettā || 155 ||
verses.colloquial:
puurvam janer adhi mriter api na ayam asti jaata kshanah kshana guno aniyata svabhaavah |
na ekah jadash ca ghata vat pari drishyamaanah sva aatmaa katham bhavati bhaava vikaara vettaa || 155 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It does not exist before its origin or after its dissolution; it lasts only for a short (intervening) period. Its good qualities are fleeting, and by nature it keeps changing. It is manifold and inert, and is an object of the senses, like a jar. How could it be one's own Self, the Witness of the changes in all things?

verses.sanskrit:
पाणिपादादिमान्देहो नात्मा व्यङ्गेऽपि जीवनात् ।
तत्तच्छक्तेरनाशाच्च न नियम्यो नियामकः ॥ १५६ ॥
verses.roman:
pāṇipādādimāndeho nātmā vyaṅge'pi jīvanāt |
tattacchakteranāśācca na niyamyo niyāmakaḥ || 156 ||
verses.colloquial:
paani paada aadi maan deho na aatmaa vyange api jiivanaah |
tat tac shakter anaashaash ca na niyamyo niyaamakaah || 156 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The body, made up of arms, legs, and so on, cannot be the Ātman, since a person goes on living when particular limbs are lost, and the organism's various functions also remain intact. A body subject to another's rule cannot be the Self, which is the Ruler of all.

verses.sanskrit:
देहतद्धर्मतत्कर्मतदवस्थादिसाक्षिणः ।
सत एव स्वतःसिद्धं तद्वैलक्षण्यमात्मनः ॥ १५७ ॥
verses.roman:
dehataddharmatatkarmatadavasthādisākṣiṇaḥ |
sata eva svataḥsiddhaṃ tadvailakṣaṇyamātmanaḥ || 157 ||
verses.colloquial:
deha tad dharma tat karma tad avasthaa aadi saakshinah |
sata eva svatah siddham tad vailaksanyam aatmanah || 157 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is self-evident that the Ātman, the abiding Reality, is different from the body and from its characteristics, activities, states, and so on, all of which It witnesses.

verses.sanskrit:
शल्यराशिर्मांसलिप्तो मलपूर्णोऽतिकश्मलः ।
कथं भवेदयं वेत्ता स्वयमेतद्विलक्षणः ॥ १५८ ॥
verses.roman:
śalyarāśirmāṃsalipto malapūrṇo'tikaśmalaḥ |
kathaṃ bhavedayaṃ vettā svayametadvilakṣaṇaḥ || 158 ||
verses.colloquial:
shalya raashir maamsaa lipto mala puurno ati kashmala |
katham bhaved ayam vettaa svayam etad vilakshanah || 158 ||
verses.translation_reworded: How can the body, a bundle of bones wrapped in flesh, full of filth and extremely impure, be the self-existent Ātman, the Knower, which is always distinct from it?

verses.sanskrit:
त्वङ्मांसमेदोऽस्थिपुरीषराशा वहंमतिं मूढजनः करोति ।
विलक्षणं वेत्ति विचारशीलो निजस्वरूपं परमार्थ भूतम् ॥ १५९ ॥
verses.roman:
tvaṅmāṃsamedo'sthipurīṣarāśā vahaṃmatiṃ mūḍhajanaḥ karoti |
vilakṣaṇaṃ vetti vicāraśīlo nijasvarūpaṃ paramārtha bhūtam || 159 ||
verses.colloquial:
tvang maamsaa medo asthi puriisha raashaa vaham matim muudha janah karoti |
vilakshanam vetti vicaara shiilo nija svaruupam param artha bhuutam || 159 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The foolish person identifies with a mass of skin, flesh, fat, bones, and filth. The person of discrimination knows his own Self, the only Reality there is, as distinct from the body.

verses.sanskrit:
देहोऽहमित्येव जडस्य बुद्धिः देहे च जीवे विदुषस्त्वहंधीः ।
विवेकविज्ञानवतो महात्मनो ब्रह्माहमित्येव मतिः सदात्मनि ॥ १६0 ॥
verses.roman:
deho'hamityeva jaḍasya buddhiḥ dehe ca jīve viduṣastvahaṃdhīḥ |
vivekavijñānavato mahātmano brahmāhamityeva matiḥ sadātmani || 160 ||
verses.colloquial:
deho aham ity eva jadhasya buddhih dehe ca jiive vidushah tv aham dhii |
viveka vijnaana vatah mahaa aatmanah brahma aham ity eva matih sadaa aatmani || 160 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The dull person believes he is the body. The book-learned person identifies with the mixture of body and soul. The sage, who has realization born of discrimination, regards the eternal Ātman as his Self and thinks, "I am Brahman."

verses.sanskrit:
अत्रात्मबुद्धिं त्यज मूढबुद्धे त्वङ्मांसमेदोऽस्थिपुरीषराशौ ।
सर्वात्मनि ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पे कुरुष्व शान्ति परमां भजस्व ॥ १६१ ॥
verses.roman:
atrātmabuddhiṃ tyaja mūḍhabuddhe tvaṅmāṃsamedo'sthipurīṣarāśau |
sarvātmani brahmaṇi nirvikalpe kuruṣva śānti paramāṃ bhajasva || 161 ||
verses.colloquial:
atra aatma buddhim tyaja muudha buddhe tvang maamsaa medo asthi puriisha raashau |
sarva aatmani brahmani nirvikalpe kurusha shaantim paramaam bhajasva || 161 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Foolish one, stop identifying with this bundle of skin, flesh, fat, bones, and filth. Identify instead with the Absolute Brahman, the Self of all, and so reach supreme Peace.

verses.sanskrit:
देहेन्द्रियादावसति भ्रमोदितां विद्वानहं तां न जहाति यावत् ।
तावन्न तस्यास्ति विमुक्तिवार्ताप्य् अस्त्वेष वेदान्तनयान्तदर्शी ॥ १६२ ॥
verses.roman:
dehendriyādāvasati bhramoditāṃ vidvānahaṃ tāṃ na jahāti yāvat |
tāvanna tasyāsti vimuktivārtāpy astveṣa vedāntanayāntadarśī || 162 ||
verses.colloquial:
deha indriya aadau asati bhrama uditaam vidvaan aham taam na jahaati yaavat |
taavannat tasya asti vimukti vaartaa apy astu esha vedaanta naya anta darshii || 162 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So long as the book-learned person does not give up his mistaken identification with the body, the organs, and so on, which are unreal, there can be no talk of emancipation for him, however learned he may be in Vedanta philosophy.

verses.sanskrit:
छायाशरीरे प्रतिबिम्बगात्रे यत्स्वप्नदेहे हृदि कल्पिताङ्गे ।
यथात्मबुद्धिस्तव नास्ति काचिज् जीवच्छरीरे च तथैव मास्तु ॥ १६३ ॥
verses.roman:
chāyāśarīre pratibimbagātre yatsvapnadehe hṛdi kalpitāṅge |
yathātmabuddhistava nāsti kācij jīvaccharīre ca tathaiva māstu || 163 ||
verses.colloquial:
chaayaa shariire pratibimba gaatre yat svapna dehe hridi kalpita ange |
yathaa aatma buddhis tava naasti kaacij jiivac chariire ca tathaa eva maastu || 163 ||
verses.translation_reworded: You do not identify with your shadow-body, your image-body, your dream-body, or the body you have in your heart's imaginings. Stop doing so with the living body as well.

verses.sanskrit:
देहात्मधीरेव नृणामसद्धियां जन्मादिदुःखप्रभवस्य बीजम् ।
यतस्ततस्त्वं जहि तां प्रयत्नात् त्यक्ते तु चित्ते न पुनर्भवाशा ॥ १६४ ॥
verses.roman:
dehātmadhīreva nṛṇāmasaddhiyāṃ janmādiduḥkhaprabhavasya bījam |
yatastatastvaṃ jahi tāṃ prayatnāt tyakte tu citte na punarbhavāśā || 164 ||
verses.colloquial:
deha aatma dhiir eva nrinaaam asad dhiyaam janma aadi duhkha prabhaavasya biijam |
yatas tatas tvam jahi taam prayatnaat tyakte tu citte na punar bhava aashaa || 164 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Identification with the body is the sole root that gives rise to the misery of birth and so on for those attached to the unreal. So destroy it with the greatest care. Once this mind-made identification is given up, there is no further possibility of rebirth.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>b) Prņamaya kośa (Vital air sheath)</vt>
कर्मेन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिरञ्चितोऽयं प्राणो भवेत्प्राणमायास्तु कोशः ।
येनात्मवानन्नमयोऽनुपूर्णः प्रवर्ततेऽसौ सकलक्रियासु ॥ १६५ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>b) Prņamaya kośa (Vital air sheath)</vt>
karmendriyaiḥ pañcabhirañcito'yaṃ prāṇo bhavetprāṇaMāyāstu kośaḥ |
yenātmavānannamayo'nupūrṇaḥ pravartate'sau sakalakriyāsu || 165 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>b) Praanamaya kosha (Vital air sheath)</vt>
karma indriyaih pancabhir ancito ayam praano bhavet praana maayaas tu koshah |
yena aatma vaan anna mayo anupuurno pravartate asau sakala kriyaashu || 165 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The familiar Prāṇa, joined with the five organs of action, forms the vital sheath. Permeated by it, the material sheath takes part in all activities as if it were alive.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवात्मापि प्राणमयो वायुविकारो गन्तागन्ता वायुवदन्तर्बहिरेषः ।
यस्मात्किंचित्क्वापि न वेत्तीष्टमनिष्टं स्वं वान्यं वा किंचन नित्यं परतन्त्रः ॥ १६६ ॥
verses.roman:
naivātmāpi prāṇamayo vāyuvikāro gantāgantā vāyuvadantarbahireṣaḥ |
yasmātkiṃcitkvāpi na vettīṣṭamaniṣṭaṃ svaṃ vānyaṃ vā kiṃcana nityaṃ paratantraḥ || 166 ||
verses.colloquial:
na eva aatma api praana mayo vaayuvikaaro gantaa agantaa vaayuvad antar bahir eshah |
yasmaat kimcit kvaapi na vetti ishtam anishtam svam vaa anyam vaa kimcana nityam para tantrah || 166 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The vital sheath is not the Self either. It is a modification of Vayu, and like air it moves into and out of the body. It never has the least knowledge of its own good and ill or of anyone else's, being forever dependent on the Self.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>c) Manomaya kosa (Mental sheath)</vt>
ज्ञानेन्द्रियाणि च मनश्च मनोमायाः स्यात् कोशो ममाहमिति वस्तुविकल्पहेतुः ।
संज्ञादिभेदकलनाकलितो बलीयांस् तत्पूर्वकोशमभिपूर्य विजृम्भते यः ॥ १६७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>c) Manomaya kosa (Mental sheath)</vt>
jñānendriyāṇi ca manaśca manoMāyāḥ syāt kośo mamāhamiti vastuvikalpahetuḥ |
saṃjñādibhedakalanākalito balīyāṃs tatpūrvakośamabhipūrya vijṛmbhate yaḥ || 167 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>c) Manomaya kosa (Mental sheath)</vt>
jnaana indriyaani ca manash ca mano maayaah syaat kosha mama aham iti vastu vikalpa hetuh |
samjnaa aadi bheda kalanaa kalito baliiyaams tat puurva kosham abhi puurya vijrimbhate yah || 167 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The organs of knowledge together with the mind make up the mental sheath, which is the cause of the diversity of things such as "I" and "mine." It is powerful and has the ability to create differences of name and so on. It shows itself as permeating the preceding sheath, the vital sheath.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चेन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिरेव होतृभिः प्रचीयमानो विषयाज्यधारया ।
जाज्वल्यमानो बहुवासनेन्धनैः मनोमयाग्निर्दहति प्रपञ्चम् ॥ १६८ ॥
verses.roman:
pañcendriyaiḥ pañcabhireva hotṛbhiḥ pracīyamāno viṣayājyadhārayā |
jājvalyamāno bahuvāsanendhanaiḥ manomayāgnirdahati prapañcam || 168 ||
verses.colloquial:
panca indriyaih pancabhir eva hotribhih praciiyamaano vishaya aajya dhaarayaa |
jaajvalyamaano bahu vaasana indhanai mano maya agnir dahati prapancam || 168 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The mental sheath is the (sacrificial) fire that produces this phenomenal universe. The five sense-organs, acting as priests, feed it with the fuel of many desires, and the objects of the senses, acting as the stream of oblations, set it ablaze.

verses.sanskrit:
न ह्यस्त्यविद्या मनसोऽतिरिक्ता मनो ह्यविद्या भवबन्धहेतुः ।
तस्मिन्विनष्टे सकलं विनष्टं विजृम्भितेऽस्मिन्सकलं विजृम्भते ॥ १६९ ॥
verses.roman:
na hyastyavidyā manaso'tiriktā mano hyavidyā bhavabandhahetuḥ |
tasminvinaṣṭe sakalaṃ vinaṣṭaṃ vijṛmbhite'sminsakalaṃ vijṛmbhate || 169 ||
verses.colloquial:
na hi asty avidyaa manaso atiriktaa mano hi avidyaa bhava bandha hetuh |
tasmin vinashte sakalam vinastam vijrimbhite asmin sakalam vijrimbhate || 169 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Ignorance (Avidya) does not exist outside the mind. The mind alone is Avidya, the cause of the bondage of transmigration. When the mind is destroyed, all else is destroyed; when it is manifest, everything else is manifest.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्नेऽर्थशून्ये सृजति स्वशक्त्या भोक्त्रादिविश्वं मन एव सर्वम् ।
तथैव जाग्रत्यपि नो विशेषः तत्सर्वमेतन्मनसो विजृम्भणम् ॥ १७0 ॥
verses.roman:
svapne'rthaśūnye sṛjati svaśaktyā bhoktrādiviśvaṃ mana eva sarvam |
tathaiva jāgratyapi no viśeṣaḥ tatsarvametanmanaso vijṛmbhaṇam || 170 ||
verses.colloquial:
svapne artha shuunye srijati sva shaktyaa bhoktri aadi vishvam mana eva sarvam |
tathaa eva jaagraty api no visheshah tat sarvam etat manaso vijrimbhanam || 170 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In dreams, with no real contact with the outer world, the mind by itself creates a whole universe, including the experiencer and the rest. The waking state is no different. So all of this (phenomenal universe) is the mind's projection.

verses.sanskrit:
सुषुप्तिकाले मनसि प्रलीने नैवास्ति किंचित्सकलप्रसिद्धेः ।
अतो मनःकल्पितेव पुंसः संसार एतस्य न वस्तुतोऽस्ति ॥ १७१ ॥
verses.roman:
suṣuptikāle manasi pralīne naivāsti kiṃcitsakalaprasiddheḥ |
ato manaḥkalpiteva puṃsaḥ saṃsāra etasya na vastuto'sti || 171 ||
verses.colloquial:
sushupti kaale manasi praliine na eva asti kimcit sakala prasiddheh |
ato manah kalpita eva pumsah samsaara etasya na vastu to asti || 171 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In dreamless sleep, when the mind has been reduced to its causal state, nothing exists (for the sleeper), as everyone's experience shows. So a person's relative existence is merely the creation of his mind and has no objective reality.

verses.sanskrit:
वायुनानीयते मेधः पुनस्तेनैव नीयते ।
मनसा कल्प्यते बन्धो मोक्षस्तेनैव कल्प्यते ॥ १७२ ॥
verses.roman:
vāyunānīyate medhaḥ punastenaiva nīyate |
manasā kalpyate bandho mokṣastenaiva kalpyate || 172 ||
verses.colloquial:
vaayunaa niiyate medhah punas tena eva niiyate |
manasaa kalpyate bandho mokshah tena eva kalpyate || 172 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The wind brings the clouds in, and the same wind drives them away. In the same way the mind causes a person's bondage, and the mind alone causes Liberation too.

verses.sanskrit:
देहादिसर्वविषये परिकल्प्य रागं बध्नाति तेन पुरुषं पशुवद्गुणेन ।
वैरस्यमत्र विषवत्सुवुधाय पश्चाद् एनं विमोचयति तन्मन एव बन्धात् ॥ १७३ ॥
verses.roman:
dehādisarvaviṣaye parikalpya rāgaṃ badhnāti tena puruṣaṃ paśuvadguṇena |
vairasyamatra viṣavatsuvudhāya paścād enaṃ vimocayati tanmana eva bandhāt || 173 ||
verses.colloquial:
deha aadi sarva vishaye parikalpya raagam badhnati tena purusham pashu vad gunena |
vairasyam atra visha vat suvudhaya pashcaad enam vimocayati tan mana eva bandhaat || 173 ||
verses.translation_reworded: (First) it creates in a person an attachment to the body and to all other objects of the senses, and through that attachment it ties him up, like an animal with ropes. Later, that very mind creates in him a complete distaste for these objects, as if they were poison, and frees him from bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मान्मनः कारणमस्य जन्तोः बन्धस्य मोक्षस्य च वा विधाने ।
बन्धस्य हेतुर्मलिनं रजोगुणैः मोक्षस्य शुद्धं विरजस्तमस्कम् ॥ १७४ ॥
verses.roman:
tasmānmanaḥ kāraṇamasya jantoḥ bandhasya mokṣasya ca vā vidhāne |
bandhasya heturmalinaṃ rajoguṇaiḥ mokṣasya śuddhaṃ virajastamaskam || 174 ||
verses.colloquial:
tasmaan manah kaaranam asya jantoh bandhasya mokshasya ca vaa vidhaane |
bandhasya hetur malinam rajo gunaih mokshasya shuddham virajas tamaskam || 174 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So the mind is the sole cause of a person's bondage or Liberation. When stained by the effects of Rajas it leads to bondage; when pure and stripped of Rajas and Tamas it leads to Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
विवेकवैराग्यगुणातिरेकाच् छुद्धत्वमासाद्य मनो विमुक्त्यै ।
भवत्यतो बुद्धिमतो मुमुक्षोस् ताभ्यां दृढाभ्यां भवितव्यमग्रे ॥ १७५ ॥
verses.roman:
vivekavairāgyaguṇātirekāc chuddhatvamāsādya mano vimuktyai |
bhavatyato buddhimato mumukṣos tābhyāṃ dṛḍhābhyāṃ bhavitavyamagre || 175 ||
verses.colloquial:
viveka vairaagya guna atirekaac chuddhatvam aasaadya mano vimuktyai |
bhavaty ato buddhi mato mumukshosh taabhyaam dridhhaabhyaam bhavitavyam agre || 175 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Made pure by a strong measure of discrimination and renunciation, the mind leads to Liberation. So the wise seeker of Liberation must first strengthen these two.

verses.sanskrit:
मनो नाम महाव्याघ्रो विषयारण्यभूमिषु ।
चरत्यत्र न गच्छन्तु साधवो ये मुमुक्षवः ॥ १७६ ॥
verses.roman:
mano nāma mahāvyāghro viṣayāraṇyabhūmiṣu |
caratyatra na gacchantu sādhavo ye mumukṣavaḥ || 176 ||
verses.colloquial:
mano naama mahaa vyaagro vishaya aranya bhuumishu |
caraty atra na gacchantu saadhaavo ye mumukshavah || 176 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A huge tiger called the mind prowls the forest of sense-pleasures. Let good people who long for Liberation never go there.

verses.sanskrit:
मनः प्रसूते विषयानशेषान् स्थूलात्मना सूक्ष्मतया च भोक्तुः ।
शरीरवर्णाश्रमजातिभेदान् गुणक्रियाहेतुफलानि नित्यम् ॥ १७७ ॥
verses.roman:
manaḥ prasūte viṣayānaśeṣān sthūlātmanā sūkṣmatayā ca bhoktuḥ |
śarīravarṇāśramajātibhedān guṇakriyāhetuphalāni nityam || 177 ||
verses.colloquial:
manah prasuute vishayaan asheshaan sthuula aatmanaa suukshmatayaa ca bhoktuh |
shariira varna aashrama jaati bhedaan guna kriyaa hetu phalaani nityam || 177 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The mind continually produces for the experiencer every object of the senses without exception, whether perceived as gross or subtle, along with the differences of body, caste, order of life, and tribe, and the varieties of qualification, action, means, and results.

verses.sanskrit:
असङ्गचिद्रूपममुं विमोह्य देहेन्द्रियप्राणगुणैर्निबद्ध्य ।
अहंममेति भ्रमायात्यजस्रं मनः स्वकृत्येषु फलोपभुक्तिषु ॥ १७८ ॥
verses.roman:
asaṅgacidrūpamamuṃ vimohya dehendriyaprāṇaguṇairnibaddhya |
ahaṃmameti bhraMāyātyajasraṃ manaḥ svakṛtyeṣu phalopabhuktiṣu || 178 ||
verses.colloquial:
asanga cid ruupam amum vimohya deha indriya praana gunaih nibaddhya |
aham mama iti bhrama aaty ajasram manah sva krityeshu phala upabhuktiishu || 178 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The mind deludes the Jīva, which is unattached Pure Intelligence, and binds it with the ties of body, organs, and Prāṇas. With ideas of "I" and "mine," it makes the Jīva wander among the many enjoyments of results it has brought about itself.

verses.sanskrit:
अध्यासदोषात्पुरुषस्य संसृतिः अध्यासबन्धस्त्वमुनैव कल्पितः ।
रजस्तमोदोषवतोऽविवेकिनो जन्मादिदुःखस्य निदानमेतत् ॥ १७९ ॥
verses.roman:
adhyāsadoṣātpuruṣasya saṃsṛtiḥ adhyāsabandhastvamunaiva kalpitaḥ |
rajastamodoṣavato'vivekino janmādiduḥkhasya nidānametat || 179 ||
verses.colloquial:
adhyaasa doshaat purushasya samsritih adhyaasa bandhas tv amunaa eva kalpitah |
rajas tamo dosha vato avivekino janma aadi duhkhasya nidaanam etat || 179 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A person's transmigration comes from the evil of superimposition, and the bondage of superimposition is created by the mind alone. This is what brings the misery of birth and so on to the person without discrimination, stained by Rajas and Tamas.

verses.sanskrit:
अतः प्राहुर्मनोऽविद्यां पण्डितास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ।
येनैव भ्राम्यते विश्वं वायुनेवाभ्रमण्डलम् ॥ १८0 ॥
verses.roman:
ataḥ prāhurmano'vidyāṃ paṇḍitāstattvadarśinaḥ |
yenaiva bhrāmyate viśvaṃ vāyunevābhramaṇḍalam || 180 ||
verses.colloquial:
atah praahurmano avidyaam panditaas tattva darshinah |
yena eva bhraamyate vishvam vaayuneva abhra mandalam || 180 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That is why sages who have grasped its secret have called the mind Avidya, or ignorance. By it alone the universe is pushed back and forth, like masses of cloud by the wind.

verses.sanskrit:
तन्मनःशोधनं कार्यं प्रयत्नेन मुमुक्षुणा ।
विशुद्धे सति चैतस्मिन्मुक्तिः करफलायते ॥ १८१ ॥
verses.roman:
tanmanaḥśodhanaṃ kāryaṃ prayatnena mumukṣuṇā |
viśuddhe sati caitasminmuktiḥ karaphalāyate || 181 ||
verses.colloquial:
tan manah shodhanam kaaryam prayatnena mumukshinaa |
vishuddhe sati ca etasmin muktih kara phalaaayate || 181 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So anyone seeking Liberation must take care to purify the mind. Once it is pure, Liberation is as easy to reach as a fruit lying in one's palm.

verses.sanskrit:
मोक्षैकसक्त्या विषयेषु रागं निर्मूल्य संन्यस्य च सर्वकर्म ।
सच्छ्रद्धया यः श्रवणादिनिष्ठो रजःस्वभावं स धुनोति बुद्धेः ॥ १८२ ॥
verses.roman:
mokṣaikasaktyā viṣayeṣu rāgaṃ nirmūlya saṃnyasya ca sarvakarma |
sacchraddhayā yaḥ śravaṇādiniṣṭho rajaḥsvabhāvaṃ sa dhunoti buddheḥ || 182 ||
verses.colloquial:
moksha eka saktyaa vishayeshu raagam nirmuulya samnyasya ca sarva karma |
sac chraddhayaa yah shravana aadi nishthah rajah svabhaavam sa dhunoti buddhe || 182 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A person who, through one-pointed devotion to Liberation, tears out attachment to sense-objects, gives up all actions, and with faith in the Real Brahman regularly practises hearing and the rest, succeeds in cleansing the intellect of its Rājasika nature.

verses.sanskrit:
मनोमयो नापि भवेत्परात्मा ह्याद्यन्तवत्त्वात्परिणामिभावात् ।
दुःखात्मकत्वाद्विषयत्वहेतोः द्रष्टा हि दृश्यात्मतया न दृष्टः ॥ १८३ ॥
verses.roman:
manomayo nāpi bhavetparātmā hyādyantavattvātpariṇāmibhāvāt |
duḥkhātmakatvādviṣayatvahetoḥ draṣṭā hi dṛśyātmatayā na dṛṣṭaḥ || 183 ||
verses.colloquial:
mano mayo na api bhavet param aatmaa hi aadi anta vat tvaat parinaami bhaavaat |
duhkha aatmakatvaat vishaya tvat hetoh drashthaa hi drishya aatmatayaa na drishtah || 183 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The mental sheath cannot be the Supreme Self either. It has a beginning and an end, it undergoes change, it is marked by pain and suffering, and it is an object. The subject can never be identified with the things it knows.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>d) Vijnanamaya kośa (Intellectual sheath)</vt>
बुद्धिर्बुद्धीन्द्रियैः सार्धं सवृत्तिः कर्तृलक्षणः ।
विज्ञानमायाकोशः स्यात्पुंसः संसारकारणम् ॥ १८४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>d) Vijnanamaya kośa (Intellectual sheath)</vt>
buddhirbuddhīndriyaiḥ sārdhaṃ savṛttiḥ kartṛlakṣaṇaḥ |
vijñānaMāyākośaḥ syātpuṃsaḥ saṃsārakāraṇam || 184 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>d) Vijnanamaya kosha (Intellectual sheath)</vt>
buddhir buddhi indriyaih saardham sa vrittih kartri lakshanah |
vijnaana maayaa koshah syaat pumsah samsaara kaaranam || 184 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Buddhi, together with its modifications and the organs of knowledge, makes up the Vijñānamāyā Kośa, the knowledge sheath. It has the character of an agent, and it is what causes a person's transmigration.

verses.sanskrit:
अनुव्रजच्चित्प्रतिबिम्बशक्तिः विज्ञानसंज्ञः प्रकृतेर्विकारः ।
ज्ञानक्रियावानहमित्यजस्रं देहेन्द्रियादिष्वभिमन्यते भृशम् ॥ १८५ ॥
verses.roman:
anuvrajaccitpratibimbaśaktiḥ vijñānasaṃjñaḥ prakṛtervikāraḥ |
jñānakriyāvānahamityajasraṃ dehendriyādiṣvabhimanyate bhṛśam || 185 ||
verses.colloquial:
anu vrajat cit prati bimba shaktih vijnaana samjnah prakriter vikaarah |
jnaana kriyaa vaan aham ity ajasram deha indriya aadishu abhimanyate bhrisham || 185 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This knowledge sheath, which a reflection of the power of the Chit seems to accompany, is a modification of Prakriti. It has the function of knowing, and it always identifies itself completely with the body, the organs, and so on.

verses.sanskrit:
अनादिकालोऽयमहंस्वभावो जीवः समस्तव्यवहारवोढा ।
करोति कर्माण्यपि पूर्ववासनः पुण्यान्यपुण्यानि च तत्फलानि ॥ १८६ ॥
verses.roman:
anādikālo'yamahaṃsvabhāvo jīvaḥ samastavyavahāravoḍhā |
karoti karmāṇyapi pūrvavāsanaḥ puṇyānyapuṇyāni ca tatphalāni || 186 ||
verses.colloquial:
anaadi kaalo ayam aham svabhaavo jiivah samasta vyavahaara vodhaa |
karoti karmaani api puurva vaasanah punyaani apunyaani ca tat phalaani || 186 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It has no beginning, it is marked by egoism, it is called the Jiva, and it carries out all activity on the relative plane. Driven by past desires, it does good and evil deeds and tastes their results. Born into one body after another, it comes and goes, rising and falling. It is this knowledge sheath that passes through waking, dream, and the other states, and that feels joy and grief.

verses.sanskrit:
भुङ्क्ते विचित्रास्वपि योनिषु व्रजन् नायाति निर्यात्यध ऊर्ध्वमेषः ।
अस्यैव विज्ञानमायास्य जाग्रत् स्वप्नाद्यवस्थाः सुखदुःखभोगः ॥ १८७ ॥
verses.roman:
bhuṅkte vicitrāsvapi yoniṣu vrajan nāyāti niryātyatha ūrdhvameṣaḥ |
asyaiva vijñānamāyāsya jāgrat svapnādyavasthāḥ sukhaduḥkhabhogaḥ || 187 ||
verses.colloquial:
bhunkte vicitraasu api yonishu vrajan na aayaati niryaati atha uurdhvam eshah |
asya eva vijnyaanam aayaasya jaagrat svapna aadi avasthah sukha duhkha bhogah || 187 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It has no beginning, it is marked by egoism, it is called the Jiva, and it carries out all activity on the relative plane. Driven by past desires, it does good and evil deeds and tastes their results. Born into one body after another, it comes and goes, rising and falling. It is this knowledge sheath that passes through waking, dream, and the other states, and that feels joy and grief.

verses.sanskrit:
देहादिनिष्ठाश्रमधर्मकर्म गुणाभिमानः सततं ममेति ।
विज्ञानकोशोऽयमतिप्रकाशः प्रकृष्टसान्निध्यवशात्परात्मनः ।
अतो भवत्येष उपाधिरस्य यदात्मधीः संसरति भ्रमेण ॥ १८८ ॥
verses.roman:
dehādiniṣṭhāśramadharmakarma guṇābhimānaḥ satataṃ mameti |
vijñānakośo'yamatiprakāśaḥ prakṛṣṭasānnidhyavaśātparātmanaḥ |
ato bhavatyeṣa upādhirasya yadātmadhīḥ saṃsarati bhrameṇa || 188 ||
verses.colloquial:
deha aadi nishthaa ashrama dharma karma guna abhimaanah satatam mama iti |
vijnaana kosha ayam ati prakaashaha prakrishta saannidhi vashaad param aatmanah |
ato bhavati esha upaadhi asya yad aatma dhiih samsarati bhramena || 188 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It constantly takes the duties, functions, and attributes of the orders of life, which belong to the body, to be its own. Because it lies so close to the Supreme Self, the knowledge sheath shines with great brilliance; and the Self, identifying with it through delusion, undergoes transmigration. The sheath is therefore a superimposition on the Self.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Ātman - Unattached</vt>
योऽयं विज्ञानमायाः प्राणेषु हृदि स्फुरत्ययं ज्योतिः ।
कूटस्थः सन्नात्मा कर्ता भोक्ता भवत्युपाधिस्थः ॥ १८९ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Ātman - Unattached</vt>
yo'yaṃ vijñānaMāyāḥ prāṇeṣu hṛdi sphuratyayaṃ jyotiḥ |
kūṭasthaḥ sannātmā kartā bhoktā bhavatyupādhisthaḥ || 189 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Aatman - Unattached</vt>
yo ayam vijnaana maayaah praanashu hridi sphuraty ayam jyotih |
kuuta sthah san aatmaa kartaa bhoktaa bhavaty upaadhi sthah || 189 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The self-luminous Ātman, which is Pure Knowledge, shines among the Prāṇas, within the heart. It never changes, yet because of the knowledge sheath superimposed on It, It becomes the doer and the experiencer.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वयं परिच्छेदमुपेत्य बुद्धेः तादात्म्यदोषेण परं मृषात्मनः ।
सर्वात्मकः सन्नपि वीक्षते स्वयं स्वतः पृथक्त्वेन मृदो घटानिव ॥ १९0 ॥
verses.roman:
svayaṃ paricchedamupetya buddheḥ tādātmyadoṣeṇa paraṃ mṛṣātmanaḥ |
sarvātmakaḥ sannapi vīkṣate svayaṃ svataḥ pṛthaktvena mṛdo ghaṭāniva || 190 ||
verses.colloquial:
svayam parichedam upetya buddhe taadaatmya doshenaa param mrishaa aatmanah |
sarva aatmakah san api viikshate svayam svata prithaktvena mrido ghataan iva || 190 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This Ātman is the Self of all that exists. Yet by taking on the limits of the Buddhi and wrongly identifying with that wholly unreal thing, It regards Itself as something different, just as earthen jars might be thought different from the clay that forms them.

verses.sanskrit:
उपाधिसंबन्धवशात्परात्मा ह्युपाधिधर्माननुभाति तद्गुणः ।
अयोविकारानविकारिवन्हिवत् सदैकरूपोऽपि परः स्वभावात् ॥ १९१ ॥
verses.roman:
upādhisaṃbandhavaśātparātmā hyupādhidharmānanubhāti tadguṇaḥ |
ayovikārānavikārivanhivat sadaikarūpo'pi paraḥ svabhāvāt || 191 ||
verses.colloquial:
upaadhi sambandha vashaad param aatmaa hi upaadhi dharmaan anubhaati tad gunah |
ayo vikaaraan avikaarivanhivat sadaa eka ruupo api parah svabhaavaat || 191 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through Its connection with the superimpositions, the Supreme Self, though perfect by nature (transcending Nature) and forever unchanging, takes on their qualities and appears to act just as they do. In the same way, changeless fire takes on the shapes of the iron it makes red-hot.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>What is Liberation? - Disciple</vt>
शिष्य उवाच भ्रमेणाप्यन्यथा वास्तु जीवभावः परात्मनः ।
तदुपाधेरनादित्वान्नानादेर्नाश इष्यते ॥ १९२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>What is Liberation? - Disciple</vt>
śiṣya uvāca bhrameṇāpyanyathā vāstu jīvabhāvaḥ parātmanaḥ |
tadupādheranāditvānnānādernāśa iṣyate || 192 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>What is Liberation? - Disciple</vt>
shishya uvaaca bhramena api anyathaa vaastu jiiva bhaavah param aatmanah |
tad upaadher anaaditvaan na anaaader naasha ishyate || 192 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The disciple asked: Whether by delusion or by some other cause, the Supreme Self has come to regard Itself as the Jīva. This superimposition has no beginning, and what has no beginning cannot be supposed to have an end either.

verses.sanskrit:
अतोऽस्य जीवभावोऽपि नित्या भवति संसृतिः ।
न निवर्तेत तन्मोक्षः कथं मे श्रीगुरो वद ॥ १९३ ॥
verses.roman:
ato'sya jīvabhāvo'pi nityā bhavati saṃsṛtiḥ |
na nivarteta tanmokṣaḥ kathaṃ me śrīguro vada || 193 ||
verses.colloquial:
ato asya jiiva bhaavo api nityaa bhavati samsritih |
na nivarteta tan mokshah katham me shri guro vada || 193 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So the soul's state as a Jīva must also be endless, and its transmigration must go on forever. How then can the soul ever be liberated? Please make this clear to me, revered Master.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Self-Knowledge gives Liberation</vt>
श्रीगुरुरुवाच सम्यक्पृष्टं त्वया विद्वन्सावधानेन तच्छृणु ।
प्रामाणिकी न भवति भ्रान्त्या मोहितकल्पना ॥ १९४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Self-Knowledge gives Liberation</vt>
śrīgururuvāca samyakpṛṣṭaṃ tvayā vidvansāvadhānena tacchṛṇu |
prāmāṇikī na bhavati bhrāntyā mohitakalpanā || 194 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Self-Knowledge gives Liberation</vt>
shri gurur uvaaca samyak prishtham tvayaa vidvan saavadhnaanena tac chhrinu |
praamaanakii na bhavati bhraantyaa mohita kalpanaa || 194 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Teacher said: Your question is a good one, learned man. So listen closely. What has been conjured up by delusion in the imagination can never be accepted as fact.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रान्तिं विना त्वसङ्गस्य निष्क्रियस्य निराकृतेः ।
न घटेतार्थसंबन्धो नभसो नीलतादिवत् ॥ १९५ ॥
verses.roman:
bhrāntiṃ vinā tvasaṅgasya niṣkriyasya nirākṛteḥ |
na ghaṭetārthasaṃbandho nabhaso nīlatādivat || 195 ||
verses.colloquial:
bhraantim vinaa tv asangasya nishkriyasya niraakriteh |
na ghateta artha sambandho nabhaso niila taa divat || 195 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Apart from delusion, the Self, which is unattached, free of activity, and formless, can have no connection with the objective world, any more than the sky has any real connection with blueness and the like.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्य द्रष्टुर्निर्गुणस्याक्रियस्य प्रत्यग्बोधानन्दरूपस्य बुद्धेः ।
भ्रान्त्या प्राप्तो जीवभावो न सत्यो मोहापाये नास्त्यवस्तुस्वभावात् ॥ १९६ ॥
verses.roman:
svasya draṣṭurnirguṇasyākriyasya pratyagbodhānandarūpasya buddheḥ |
bhrāntyā prāpto jīvabhāvo na satyo mohāpāye nāstyavastusvabhāvāt || 196 ||
verses.colloquial:
svasya drashthur nirgunasya akriyasya pratyag bodha aananda ruupasya buddhe |
bhraantyaa praapto jiiva bhaavo na satyo moha apaaye na asti avastu svabhaavaat || 196 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Ātman is the Witness, beyond qualities and beyond activity, and It is realized within as Knowledge and Bliss Absolute. Its state as a Jīva has been superimposed by the delusion of the Buddhi and is not real. Being unreal by nature, that state ceases to exist once the delusion is gone.

verses.sanskrit:
यावद्भ्रान्तिस्तावदेवास्य सत्ता मिथ्याज्ञानोज्जृम्भितस्य प्रमादात् ।
रज्ज्वां सर्पो भ्रान्तिकालीन एव भ्रान्तेर्नाशे नैव सर्पोऽपि तद्वत् ॥ १९७ ॥
verses.roman:
yāvadbhrāntistāvadevāsya sattā mithyājñānojjṛmbhitasya pramādāt |
rajjvāṃ sarpo bhrāntikālīna eva bhrānternāśe naiva sarpo'pi tadvat || 197 ||
verses.colloquial:
yaavad bhraantis taavad eva asya sattaa mithyaa jnaana ujjrimbhitasya pramaadaat |
rajjvaam sarpo bhraanti kaaliina eva bhraantter naashe na eva sarpo api tad vat || 197 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It lasts only as long as the delusion lasts, since it arises from a lack of discrimination caused by illusion. A rope is taken for a snake only while the mistake continues; when the illusion vanishes, there is no snake any more. So it is here.

verses.sanskrit:
अनादित्वमविद्यायाः कार्यस्यापि तथेष्यते ।
उत्पन्नायां तु विद्यायामाविद्यकमनाद्यपि ॥ १९८ ॥
verses.roman:
anāditvamavidy āyāḥ kāryasyāpi tatheṣyate |
utpannāyāṃ tu vidyāyāmāvidyakamanādyapi || 198 ||
verses.colloquial:
anaaditvam avidyaayaah kaaryasya api tathaa ishyate |
utpannaayaam tu vidyaayaam aavidyakam anaadi api || 198 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Avidya, or Nescience, and its effects are also regarded as beginningless. But when Vidyā, or realization, dawns, all the effects of Avidya, beginningless though they are, are destroyed along with their root, as dreams are on waking from sleep. Clearly the phenomenal universe, even though it has no beginning, is not eternal; it is like previous non-existence.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रबोधे स्वप्नवत्सर्वं सहमूलं विनश्यति ।
अनाद्यपीदं नो नित्यं प्रागभाव इव स्फुटम् ॥ १९९ ॥
verses.roman:
prabodhe svapnavatsarvaṃ sahamūlaṃ vinaśyati |
anādyapīdaṃ no nityaṃ prāgabhāva iva sphuṭam || 199 ||
verses.colloquial:
prabodhe svapnavat sarvam saha muulam vinashyati |
anaadi api idam no nityam praag abhaava iva sphutam || 199 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Avidya, or Nescience, and its effects are also regarded as beginningless. But when Vidyā, or realization, dawns, all the effects of Avidya, beginningless though they are, are destroyed along with their root, as dreams are on waking from sleep. Clearly the phenomenal universe, even though it has no beginning, is not eternal; it is like previous non-existence.

verses.sanskrit:
अनादेरपि विध्वंसः प्रागभावस्य वीक्षितः ।
यद्बुद्ध्युपाधिसंबन्धात्परिकल्पितमात्मनि ॥ २00 ॥
verses.roman:
anāderapi vidhvaṃsaḥ prāgabhāvasya vīkṣitaḥ |
yadbuddhyupādhisaṃbandhātparikalpitamātmani || 200 ||
verses.colloquial:
anaader api vidhvamsah praag abhavasya viikshitah |
yad buddhi upaadhi sambandhaat parikalpitam aatmani || 200 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Previous non-existence has no beginning, yet it is seen to come to an end. In the same way, the Jīvahood imagined in the Ātman through its relation to superimposed attributes such as the Buddhi is not real, while the Ātman is essentially different from it. The relation between the Ātman and the Buddhi comes from false knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवत्वं न ततोऽन्यस्तु स्वरूपेण विलक्षणः ।
संबन्धस्त्वात्मनो बुद्ध्या मिथ्याज्ञानपुरःसरः ॥ २0१ ॥
verses.roman:
jīvatvaṃ na tato'nyastu svarūpeṇa vilakṣaṇaḥ |
saṃbandhastvaatmano buddhyā mithyājñānapuraḥsaraḥ || 201 ||
verses.colloquial:
jiivatvam na tatah anyah tu svaruupena vilakshanah |
sambandhah tu aatmanah buddhyaa mithyaa jnaana purahsarah || 201 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Previous non-existence has no beginning, yet it is seen to come to an end. In the same way, the Jīvahood imagined in the Ātman through its relation to superimposed attributes such as the Buddhi is not real, while the Ātman is essentially different from it. The relation between the Ātman and the Buddhi comes from false knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
विनिवृत्तिर्भवेत्तस्य सम्यग्ज्ञानेन नान्यथा ।
ब्रह्मात्मैकत्वविज्ञानं सम्यग्ज्ञानं श्रुतेर्मतम् ॥ २0२ ॥
verses.roman:
vinivṛttirbhavettasya samyagjñānena nānyathā |
brahmātmaikatvavijñānaṃ samyagjñānaṃ śrutermatam || 202 ||
verses.colloquial:
vinivrttih bhavet tasya samyag jnaanena na anyathaa |
brahma aatma ekatva vijnaanm samyag jnaanam shruter matam || 202 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That superimposition ends through perfect knowledge and in no other way. According to the Śrutis, perfect knowledge is the realization that the individual soul and Brahman are one.

verses.sanskrit:
तदात्मानात्मनोः सम्यग्विवेकेनैव सिध्यति ।
ततो विवेकः कर्तव्यः प्रत्यगात्मसदात्मनोः ॥ २0३ ॥
verses.roman:
tadātmānātmanoḥ samyagvivekenaiva sidhyati |
tato vivekaḥ kartavyaḥ pratyagātmasadātmanoḥ || 203 ||
verses.colloquial:
tad aatmaa anaatmanoh samyag vivekena eva sidhyati |
tato vivekah kartavyah pratyag aatma sad aatmanoh || 203 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This realization comes through perfect discrimination between the Self and the non-Self. One must therefore strive to discriminate between the individual soul and the eternal Self.

verses.sanskrit:
जलं पङ्कवदत्यन्तं पङ्कापाये जलं स्फुटम् ।
यथा भाति तथात्मापि दोषाभावे स्फुटप्रभः ॥ २0४ ॥
verses.roman:
jalaṃ paṅkavadatyantaṃ paṅkāpāye jalaṃ sphuṭam |
yathā bhāti tathātmāpi doṣābhāve sphuṭaprabhaḥ || 204 ||
verses.colloquial:
jalam panka vad atyantam panka apaaye jalam sphutam |
yathaa bhaati tathaa aatmaa api dosha abhaave sphuta prabhah || 204 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Very muddy water becomes clear again once the mud is taken away. In the same way, the Ātman shows Its undimmed radiance once the taint has been removed.

verses.sanskrit:
असन्निवृत्तौ तु सदात्मना स्फुटं प्रतीतिरेतस्य भवेत्प्रतीचः ।
ततो निरासः करणीय एव सदात्मनः साध्वहमादिवस्तुनः ॥ २0५ ॥
verses.roman:
asannivṛttau tu sadātmanā sphuṭaṃ pratītiretasya bhavetpratīcaḥ |
tato nirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva sadātmanaḥ sādhvahamādivastunaḥ || 205 ||
verses.colloquial:
asat nivri ttau tu sad aatmanaa sphutam pratiiti retasya bhavet pratiicah |
tato niraasah karaniiya eva sad aatmanah saadhv aham aadi vastunah || 205 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the unreal ceases to exist, this very individual soul is known with certainty to be the eternal Self. One must therefore make a point of removing egoism and all such things entirely from the eternal Self.

verses.sanskrit:
अतो नायं परात्मा स्याद्विज्ञानमायाशब्दभाक् ।
विकारित्वाज्जडत्वाच्च परिच्छिन्नत्वहेतुतः ।
दृश्यत्वाद्व्यभिचारित्वान्नानित्यो नित्य इष्यते ॥ २0६ ॥
verses.roman:
ato nāyaṃ parātmā syādvijñānaMāyāśabdabhāk |
vikāritvājjaḍatvācca paricchinnatvahetutaḥ |
dṛśyatvādvyabhicāritvānnānityo nitya iṣyate || 206 ||
verses.colloquial:
ato na ayam para aatmaa syaad vijnyaana maayaa shabda bhaak |
vikaaritvaat jadatvaat ca paricchinna tva hetutah |
drishyatvaat vyabhicaaritvaat na anityah nitya ishyate || 206 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The knowledge sheath (Vijñānamāyā Kośa) we have been discussing cannot be the Supreme Self, for these reasons: it changes, it is insentient, it is limited, it is an object of the senses, and it is not always present. Something unreal cannot be taken for the real Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Anandamaya kośa (Bliss sheath)</vt>
आनन्दप्रतिबिम्बचुम्बिततनुर्वृत्तिस्तमोजृम्भिता स्यादानन्दमायाः प्रियादिगुणकः स्वेष्टार्थलाभोदयः ।
पुण्यस्यानुभवे विभाति कृतिनामानन्दरूपः स्वयं सर्वो नन्दति यत्र साधु तनुभृन्मात्रः प्रयत्नं विना ॥ २0७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Anandamaya kośa (Bliss sheath)</vt>
ānandapratibimbacumbitatanurvṛttistamojṛmbhitā syādānandaMāyāḥ priyādiguṇakaḥ sveṣṭārthalābhodayaḥ |
puṇyasyānubhave vibhāti kṛtināmānandarūpaḥ svayaṃ sarvo nandati yatra sādhu tanubhṛnmātraḥ prayatnaṃ vinā || 207 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Anandamaya kośa (Bliss sheath)</vt>
aananda pratibimba chumbita tanuh vrittih tamah jrimbhitaa syaat aanandamayaah priya aadi gunakah sva ishta artha laabha udayah |
punyasya anubhave vibhaati kritinaam aananda ruupah svayam sarvo nandati yatra saadhu tanubhrit maatrah prayatnam vinaa || 207 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The blissful sheath (Ānandamāyā Kośa) is the modification of Nescience that appears by catching a reflection of the Ātman, which is Bliss Absolute. Its attributes are pleasure and the like, and it comes into view when something agreeable presents itself. The fortunate feel it arise on its own when their virtuous deeds bear fruit, and from it every embodied being draws great joy without the least effort.

verses.sanskrit:
आनन्दमायाकोशस्य सुषुप्तौ स्फूर्तिरुत्कटा ।
स्वप्नजागरयोरीषदिष्टसंदर्शनाविना ॥ २0८ ॥
verses.roman:
ānandaMāyākośasya suṣuptau sphūrtirutkaṭā |
svapnajāgarayorīṣadiṣṭasaṃdarśanāvinā || 208 ||
verses.colloquial:
aananda maaya koshasya sushuptau sphurtir utkataa |
svapna jaagarayor iishad ishta samdarshana avinaa || 208 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The blissful sheath comes into its fullest play in deep sleep. In the dream and waking states it shows itself only in part, prompted by the sight of pleasant objects and the like.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवायमानन्दमायाः परात्मा सोपाधिकत्वात्प्रकृतेर्विकारात् ।
कार्यत्वहेतोः सुकृतक्रियाया विकारसङ्घातसमाहितत्वात् ॥ २0९ ॥
verses.roman:
naivāyamānandaMāyāḥ parātmā sopādhikatvātprakṛtervikārāt |
kāryatvahetoḥ sukṛtakriyāyā vikārasaṅghātasamāhitatvāt || 209 ||
verses.colloquial:
na eva ayam aananda maayaah para aatmaa sa upadhikatvaat prakriter vikaaraat |
kaaryatva hetoh sukrita kriyaayaa vikaara sanghaata samaahitatvaat || 209 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The blissful sheath is not the Supreme Self either, since it has changing attributes, is a modification of Prakriti, results from past good deeds, and lies embedded in the other sheaths, which are themselves modifications.

verses.sanskrit:
पञ्चानामपि कोशानां निषेधे युक्तितः श्रुतेः ।
तन्निषेधावधि साक्षी बोधरूपोऽवशिष्यते ॥ २१0 ॥
verses.roman:
pañcānāmapi kośānāṃ niṣedhe yuktitaḥ śruteḥ |
tanniṣedhāvadhi sākṣī bodharūpo'vaśiṣyate || 210 ||
verses.colloquial:
panchaanaam api koshaanaam nishedhe yuktitah shruteh |
tan nishedha avadhi saakshii bodha ruupo avashishyate || 210 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When all five sheaths have been set aside through reasoning on the Shruti passages, what remains at the culmination of the process is the Witness, Knowledge Absolute: the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Ātman - Other than the Five Kośas</vt>
योऽयमात्मा स्वयंज्योतिः पञ्चकोशविलक्षणः ।
अवस्थात्रयसाक्षी सन्निर्विकारो निरञ्जनः सदानन्दः स विज्ञेयः स्वात्मत्वेन विपश्चिता ॥ २११ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Ātman - Other than the Five Kośas</vt>
yo'yamātmā svayaṃjyotiḥ pañcakośavilakṣaṇaḥ |
avasthātrayasākṣī sannirvikāro nirañjanaḥ sadānandaḥ sa vijñeyaḥ svātmatvena vipaścitā || 211 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Ātman - Other than the Five Kośas</vt>
yo ayam aatmaa svayam jyotih pancha kosha vilakshanah |
avasthaa traya saakshii san nirvikaro niranjanah sadaa aanandah sa vijnyeyah sva aatmatvena vipashcitaa || 211 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This self-luminous Ātman stands apart from the five sheaths. It is the Witness of the three states, the Real, the Changeless, the Untainted, everlasting Bliss. The wise person should realize It as his own Self.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>What is Ātman? - Disciple</vt>
शिष्य उवाच मिथ्यात्वेन निषिद्धेषु कोशेष्वेतेषु पञ्चसु ।
सर्वाभावं विना किंचिन्न पश्याम्यत्र हे गुरो विज्ञेयं किमु वस्त्वस्ति स्वात्मनात्मविपश्चिता ॥ २१२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>What is Ātman? - Disciple</vt>
śiṣya uvāca mithyātvena niṣiddheṣu kośeṣveteṣu pañcasu |
sarvābhāvaṃ vinā kiṃcinna paśyāmyatra he guro vijñeyaṃ kimu vastvasti svātmanātmavipaścitā || 212 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>What is Ātman? - Disciple</vt>
shishya uvaaca mithyaatvena nishiddhesu kosheshv eteshu panchasu |
sarva abhaavam vinaa kimchin na pashyaamy atra he guro vijneyam kimu vastu asti svaatmanaa aatma vipashchitaa || 212 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The disciple asked: Once these five sheaths have been set aside as unreal, Master, I find nothing in this universe but a Void, the absence of everything. What entity, then, is left for the wise knower of the Self to realize his identity with?

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Nature of the Self - Discussion</vt>
श्रीगुरुरुवाच सत्यमुक्तं त्वया विदन्निपुणोऽसि विचारणे ।
अहमादिविकारास्ते तदभावोऽयमप्यनु ॥ २१३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Nature of the Self - Discussion</vt>
śrīgururuvāca satyamuktaṃ tvayā vidannipuṇo'si vicāraṇe |
ahamādivikārāste tadabhāvo'yamapyanu || 213 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Nature of the Self - Discussion</vt>
shrii gurur uvaaca satyam uktam tvayaa vidan nipunah asi vicaarane |
aham aadi vikaaraah te tad abhaavah ayam api anu || 213 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Guru answered: You have spoken rightly, learned man, and you are skilled indeed in discrimination. That by which all these modifications such as egoism, and also their later absence (in deep sleep), are perceived, but which is not Itself perceived: know that to be the Ātman, the Knower, by means of the sharpest intellect.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वे येनानुभूयन्ते यः स्वयं नानुभूयते ।
तमात्मानं वेदितारं विद्दि बुद्ध्या सुसूक्ष्मया ॥ २१४ ॥
verses.roman:
sarve yenānubhūyante yaḥ svayaṃ nānubhūyate |
tamātmānaṃ veditāraṃ viddhi buddhyā susūkṣmayā || 214 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarve yena anubhuuyante yah svayam na anubhuuyate |
tam aatmaanam veditaaram viddhi buddhyaa susookshmayaa || 214 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Guru answered: You have spoken rightly, learned man, and you are skilled indeed in discrimination. That by which all these modifications such as egoism, and also their later absence (in deep sleep), are perceived, but which is not Itself perceived: know that to be the Ātman, the Knower, by means of the sharpest intellect.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्साक्षिकं भवेत्तत्तद्यद्यद्येनानुभूयते ।
कस्याप्यननुभूतार्थे साक्षित्वं नोपयुज्यते ॥ २१५ ॥
verses.roman:
tatsākṣikaṃ bhavettattadyadyadyenānubhūyate |
kasyāpyananubhūtārthe sākṣitvaṃ nopayujyate || 215 ||
verses.colloquial:
tat saakshikam bhavet tat tad yad yad yena anubhuuyate |
kasya api ananubhuuta arthe saakshitvam na upayujyate || 215 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whatever is perceived by something else has that other thing as its witness. Where no agent exists to perceive a thing, we cannot say it has been perceived at all.

verses.sanskrit:
असौ स्वसाक्षिको भावो यतः स्वेनानुभूयते ।
अतः परं स्वयं साक्षात्प्रत्यगात्मा न चेतरः ॥ २१६ ॥
verses.roman:
asau svasākṣiko bhāvo yataḥ svenānubhūyate |
ataḥ paraṃ svayaṃ sākṣātpratyagātmā na cetaraḥ || 216 ||
verses.colloquial:
asau sva saakshiko bhaavo yatah svena anubhuuyate |
atah param svayam saakshaat pratyag aatmaa na ca itarah || 216 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This Ātman is known by Itself, and so It is self-cognized. The individual soul is therefore itself, directly, the Supreme Brahman and nothing else.

verses.sanskrit:
जाग्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु स्फुटतरं योऽसौ समुज्जृम्भते प्रत्यग्रूपतया सदाहमहमित्यन्तः स्फुरन्नैकधा ।
नानाकारविकारभागिन इमान् पश्यन्नहंधीमुखान् नित्यानन्दचिदात्मना स्फुरति तं विद्धि स्वमेतं हृदि ॥ २१७ ॥
verses.roman:
jāgratsvapnasuṣuptiṣu sphuṭataraṃ yo'sau samujjṛmbhate pratyagrūpatayā sadāhamahamityantaḥ sphurannaikadhā |
nānākāravikārabhāgina imān paśyannahaṃdhīmukhān nityānandacidātmanā sphurati taṃ viddhi svametaṃ hṛdi || 217 ||
verses.colloquial:
jaagrat svapna sushuptishu sphutataaram yo asau samujjrimbhate pratyag ruupatayaa sadaa aham aham iti antah sphuran na ekadhaa |
naanaa aakaara vikaara bhaagina imaan pashyan aham dhii mukhaan nitya aananda cit aatmanaa sphurati tam viddhi svam etam hridi || 217 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It shows Itself clearly in waking, dream, and deep sleep. It is felt inwardly in the mind, in many forms, as an unbroken series of egoistic impressions. It witnesses the ego, the Buddhi, and the rest, with their varied forms and modifications. It makes Itself known as Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute. Know this Ātman, your own Self, within your heart.

verses.sanskrit:
घटोदके बिम्बितमर्कबिम्बम् आलोक्य मूढो रविमेव मन्यते ।
तथा चिदाभासमुपाधिसंस्थं भ्रान्त्याहमित्येव जडोऽभिमन्यते ॥ २१८ ॥
verses.roman:
ghaṭodake bimbitamarkabimbam ālokya mūḍho ravimeva manyate |
tathā cidābhāsamupādhisaṃsthaṃ bhrāntyāhamityeva jaḍo'bhimanyate || 218 ||
verses.colloquial:
ghata udake bimbitam arka bimbam aalokya muudho ravim eva manyate |
tathaa cid aabhaasam upaadhi samstham bhraantyaa aham iti eva jado abhimanyate || 218 ||
verses.translation_reworded: On seeing the sun's reflection in the water of a jar, a fool takes it for the sun itself. In the same way the dull person, through delusion, identifies himself with the reflection of the Chit caught in the Buddhi, which is Its superimposition.

verses.sanskrit:
घटं जलं तद्गतमर्कबिम्बं विहाय सर्वं विनिरीक्ष्यतेऽर्कः ।
तटस्थ एतत्त्रितयावभासकः स्वयंप्रकाशो विदुषा यथा तथा ॥ २१९ ॥
verses.roman:
ghaṭaṃ jalaṃ tadgatamarkabimbaṃ vihāya sarvaṃ vinirīkṣyate'rkaḥ |
taṭastha etattritayāvabhāsakaḥ svayaṃprakāśo viduṣā yathā tathā || 219 ||
verses.colloquial:
ghatam jalam tad gatam arka bimbam vihaaya sarvam vinirikshyate arkah |
tatasstha etat tritaya avabhaasakah svayam prakaasho vidushaa yathaa tathaa || 219 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The wise person sets aside the jar, the water, and the reflection of the sun in it, and sees the self-luminous sun that lights all three and does not depend on them.

verses.sanskrit:
देहं धियं चित्प्रतिबिम्बमेवं विसृज्य बुद्धौ निहितं गुहायाम् ।
द्रष्टारमात्मानमखण्डबोधं सर्वप्रकाशं सदसद्विलक्षणम् ॥ २२0 ॥
verses.roman:
dehaṃ dhiyaṃ citpratibimbamevaṃ visṛjya buddhau nihitaṃ guhāyām |
draṣṭāramātmānamakhaṇḍabodhaṃ sarvaprakāśaṃ sadasadvilakṣaṇam || 220 ||
verses.colloquial:
deham dhiyam cit pratibimbam evam visrijya buddhau nihitam guhaayaam |
drashtaaram aatmaanam akhanda bodham sarva prakaasham sad asad vilakshanam || 220 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, one sets aside the body, the Buddhi, and the reflection of the Chit in it, and realizes the Witness, the Self, Knowledge Absolute, the cause by which everything is manifested. It is hidden in the depths of the Buddhi, distinct from gross and subtle, eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading, and supremely subtle. It has no inside or outside and is one with oneself. Fully realizing this true nature of one's own, a person becomes free of sin, taint, death, and grief, and becomes the very embodiment of Bliss. Illumined, he fears no one. A seeker of Liberation has no other way to break the bonds of transmigration than realizing the truth of his own Self.

verses.sanskrit:
नित्यं विभुं सर्वगतं सुसूक्ष्मं अन्तर्बहिःशून्यमनन्यमात्मनः ।
विज्ञाय सम्यङ्निजरूपमेतत् पुमान् विपाप्मा विरजो विमृत्युः ॥ २२१ ॥
verses.roman:
nityaṃ vibhuṃ sarvagataṃ susūkṣmaṃ antarbahiḥśūnyamananayamātmanaḥ |
vijñāya samyaṅnijarūpametat pumān vipāpmā virajo vimṛtyuḥ || 221 ||
verses.colloquial:
nityam vibhum sarvagatam susookshmam antar bahih shoonyam ananyam aatmanah |
vijnaaya samyak nija roopam etat pumaan vipaapamaa virajo vimrityuh || 221 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, one sets aside the body, the Buddhi, and the reflection of the Chit in it, and realizes the Witness, the Self, Knowledge Absolute, the cause by which everything is manifested. It is hidden in the depths of the Buddhi, distinct from gross and subtle, eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading, and supremely subtle. It has no inside or outside and is one with oneself. Fully realizing this true nature of one's own, a person becomes free of sin, taint, death, and grief, and becomes the very embodiment of Bliss. Illumined, he fears no one. A seeker of Liberation has no other way to break the bonds of transmigration than realizing the truth of his own Self.

verses.sanskrit:
विशोक आनन्दघनो विपश्चित्
स्वयं कुतश्चिन्न बिभेति कश्चित् ।
नान्योऽस्ति पन्था भवबन्धमुक्तेः
विना स्वतत्त्वावगमं मुमुक्षोः ॥ २२२ ॥
verses.roman:
viśoka ānandaghano vipaścit
svayaṃ kutaścinna bibheti kaścit |
nānyo'sti panthā bhavabandhamukteḥ
vinā svatattvāvagamaṃ mumukṣoḥ || 222 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishoka aanandaghano vipashchit
svayam kutashchinna bibheti kashchit |
naanyo'sti panthaa bhavabandhamuktehi
vinaa svatattvavagamam mumukshoho || 222 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, one sets aside the body, the Buddhi, and the reflection of the Chit in it, and realizes the Witness, the Self, Knowledge Absolute, the cause by which everything is manifested. It is hidden in the depths of the Buddhi, distinct from gross and subtle, eternal, omnipresent, all-pervading, and supremely subtle. It has no inside or outside and is one with oneself. Fully realizing this true nature of one's own, a person becomes free of sin, taint, death, and grief, and becomes the very embodiment of Bliss. Illumined, he fears no one. A seeker of Liberation has no other way to break the bonds of transmigration than realizing the truth of his own Self.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वविज्ञानं भवमोक्षस्य कारणम् ।
येनाद्वितीयमानन्दं ब्रह्म सम्पद्यते बुधैः ॥ २२३ ॥
verses.roman:
brahmābhinnatvavijñānaṃ bhavamokṣasya kāraṇam |
yenādvitīyamānandaṃ brahma sampadyate budhaiḥ || 223 ||
verses.colloquial:
brahma abhinnatva vijnjaanam bhava mokshasya kaaranam |
yena adviitiiyam aanandam brahma sampadyate budhaih || 223 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Realizing one's identity with Brahman is what brings Liberation from the bonds of Samsara. Through it the wise person reaches Brahman, the One without a second, Bliss Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मभूतस्तु संसृत्यै विद्वान्नावर्तते पुनः ।
विज्ञातव्यमतः सम्यग्ब्रह्माभिन्नत्वमात्मनः ॥ २२४ ॥
verses.roman:
brahmabhūtastu saṃsṛtyai vidvānnāvartate punaḥ |
vijñātavyamataḥ samyagbrahmābhinnatvamātmanaḥ || 224 ||
verses.colloquial:
brahma bhuutastu samsrityai vidvaan na aavartate punah |
vijnaatavyam atah samyag brahma abhinnatvam aatmanah || 224 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Once Brahman is realized, one does not come back to the realm of transmigration. One must therefore fully realize one's identity with Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
