सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म विशुद्धं परं स्वतःसिद्धम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं प्रत्यगभिन्नं निरन्तरं जयति ॥ २२५ ॥
verses.roman:
satyaṃ jñānamanantaṃ brahma viśuddhaṃ paraṃ svataḥsiddham |
nityānandaikarasaṃ pratyagabhinnaṃ nirantaraṃ jayati || 225 ||
verses.colloquial:
satyam jnaanam anantam brahma vishuddham param svatah siddham |
nitya aananda eka rasam pratyag abhinnam nirantaram jayati || 225 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Brahman is Existence, Knowledge, and Infinity. It is pure, supreme, self-existent, eternal, undivided Bliss. It is not, in reality, different from the individual soul, and It has no inside or outside. It is ever triumphant.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>All Manifestation Absolute</vt>
सदिदं परमाद्वैतं स्वस्मादन्यस्य वस्तुनोऽभावात् ।
न ह्यन्यदस्ति किंचित्सम्यक्परमार्थतत्त्वबोधदशायाम् ॥ २२६ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>All Manifestation Absolute</vt>
sadidaṃ paramādvaitaṃ svasmādanyasya vastuno'bhāvāt |
na hyanyadasti kiṃcitsamyakparamārthatattvabodhadaśāyām || 226 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>All Manifestation Absolute</vt>
sat idam parama advaitam svasmaat anyasya vastuno abhaavaat |
na hi anyat asti kimchit samyak parama artha tattva bodha dashaayaam || 226 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This Supreme Oneness alone is real, since nothing exists but the Self. Truly, when the highest Truth is realized, no other independent entity remains.

verses.sanskrit:
यदिदं सकलं विश्वं नानारूपं प्रतीतमज्ञानात् ।
तत्सर्वं ब्रह्मैव प्रत्यस्ताशेषभावनादोषम् ॥ २२७ ॥
verses.roman:
yadidaṃ sakalaṃ viśvaṃ nānārūpaṃ pratītamajñānāt |
tatsarvaṃ brahmaiva pratyastāśeṣabhāvanādoṣam || 227 ||
verses.colloquial:
yad idam sakalam vishvam naanaa ruupam pratiitam ajnaanaat |
tat sarvam brahma eva pratyasta ashesha bhaavanaa dosham || 227 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This whole universe, which ignorance makes appear in many forms, is nothing other than Brahman, which is completely free of all the limits of human thought.

verses.sanskrit:
मृत्कार्यभूतोऽपि मृदो न भिन्नः कुम्भोऽस्ति सर्वत्र तु मृत्स्वरूपात् ।
न कुम्भरूपं पृथगस्ति कुम्भः कुतो मृषा कल्पितनाममात्रः ॥ २२८ ॥
verses.roman:
mṛtkāryabhūto'pi mṛdo na bhinnaḥ kumbho'sti sarvatra tu mṛtsvarūpāt |
na kumbharūpaṃ pṛthagasti kumbhaḥ kuto mṛṣā kalpitanāmamātraḥ || 228 ||
verses.colloquial:
mrit kaarya bhuuto api mrido na bhinnah kumbho asti sarvatra tu mrit svaruupaat |
na kumbha ruupam prithag asti kumbhah kuto mrishaa kalpita naama maatrah || 228 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A jar is a modification of clay, yet it is not different from clay; throughout, the jar is essentially the same as the clay. Why then call it a jar? It is a fiction, merely a name someone has imagined.

verses.sanskrit:
केनापि मृद्भिन्नतया स्वरूपं घटस्य संदर्शयितुं न शक्यते ।
अतो घटः कल्पित एव मोहान् मृदेव सत्यं परमार्थभूतम् ॥ २२९ ॥
verses.roman:
kenāpi mṛdbhinnatayā svarūpaṃ ghaṭasya saṃdarśayituṃ na śakyate |
ato ghaṭaḥ kalpita eva mohān mṛdeva satyaṃ paramārthabhūtam || 229 ||
verses.colloquial:
kena api mrit bhinna tayaa svaruupam ghatasya samdarshayitum na shakyate |
ato ghatah kalpita eva mohaat mrit eva satyam paramaartha bhuutam || 229 ||
verses.translation_reworded: No one can show that the essence of a jar is anything other than the clay that makes it up. The jar is only imagined as separate through delusion; the clay that composes it is the one lasting reality in the matter.

verses.sanskrit:
सद्ब्रह्मकार्यं सकलं सदेवं तन्मात्रमेतन्न ततोऽन्यदस्ति ।
अस्तीति यो वक्ति न तस्य मोहो विनिर्गतो निद्रितवत्प्रजल्पः ॥ २३0 ॥
verses.roman:
sadbrahmakāryaṃ sakalaṃ sadevaṃ tanmātrametanna tato'nyadasti |
astīti yo vakti na tasya moho vinirgato nidritavatprajalpaḥ || 230 ||
verses.colloquial:
sad brahma kaaryam sakalam sa devam tan maatram etat na tato anyad asti |
asti iti yo vakti na tasya moho vinirgato nidritavat prajalpaah || 230 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, the whole universe, as the effect of the real Brahman, is in truth nothing but Brahman. That is its essence, and it has no existence apart from That. Whoever claims otherwise is still deluded and is babbling like someone asleep.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मैवेदं विश्वमित्येव वाणी श्रौती ब्रूतेऽथर्वनिष्ठा वरिष्ठा ।
तस्मादेतद्ब्रह्ममात्रं हि विश्वं नाधिष्ठानाद्भिन्नतारोपितस्य ॥ २३१ ॥
verses.roman:
brahmaivedaṃ viśvamityeva vāṇī śrautī brūte'tharvaniṣṭhā variṣṭhā |
tasmādetadbrahmamātraṃ hi viśvaṃ nādhiṣṭhānādbhinnatāropitasya || 231 ||
verses.colloquial:
brahma eva idam vishvam iti eva vaanii shrutii bruute atharva nishthaa varishthaa |
tasmaat etad brahma maatram hi vishvam na adhishthaanaat bhinna taa ropitasya || 231 ||
verses.translation_reworded: "This universe is truly Brahman": so runs the solemn declaration of the Atharva Veda. The universe, then, is nothing but Brahman, for what is superimposed on something has no existence separate from its substratum.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्यं यदि स्याज्जगदेतदात्मनो ऽनन्तत्त्वहानिर्निगमाप्रमाणता ।
असत्यवादित्वमपीशितुः स्यान् नैतत्त्रयं साधु हितं महात्मनाम् ॥ २३२ ॥
verses.roman:
satyaṃ yadi syājjagadetadātmano 'nantattvahānirnigamāpramāṇatā |
asatyavāditvamapīśituḥ syān naitattrayaṃ sādhu hitaṃ mahātmanām || 232 ||
verses.colloquial:
satyam yadi syaat jagat etad aatmano ananta tattva haanih nigama apramaanataa |
asatya vaaditvam api iishituh syaat na etat trayam saadhu hitam mahaatmanaam || 232 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If the universe, just as it appears, were real, duality would never end, the scriptures would be proved false, and the Lord Himself would be guilty of untruth. The noble-minded regard none of these three as desirable or wholesome.

verses.sanskrit:
ईश्वरो वस्तुतत्त्वज्ञो न चाहं तेष्ववस्थितः ।
न च मत्स्थानि भूतानीत्येवमेव व्यचीकॢपत् ॥ २३३ ॥
verses.roman:
īśvaro vastutattvajño na cāhaṃ teṣvavasthitaḥ |
na ca matsthāni bhūtānītyevameva vyacīkḷpat || 233 ||
verses.colloquial:
iishvaro vastu tattva jno na ca aham teshu avasthitah |
na ca mat sthaani bhuutaani iti evam eva vyachiiklipat || 233 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Lord, who knows the secret of all things, has upheld this view in the words: "But I am not in them" … "nor are the beings in Me."

verses.sanskrit:
यदि सत्यं भवेद्विश्वं सुषुप्तामुपलभ्यताम् ।
यन्नोपलभ्यते किंचिदतोऽसत्स्वप्नवन्मृषा ॥ २३४ ॥
verses.roman:
yadi satyaṃ bhavedviśvaṃ suṣuptāmupalabhyatām |
yannopalabhyate kiṃcidato'satsvapnavanmṛṣā || 234 ||
verses.colloquial:
yadi satyam bhaved vishvam sushuptau upalabhyataam |
yan na upalabhyate kimcid ato asat svapnavat mrishaa || 234 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If the universe is true, let it be perceived in deep sleep as well. Since it is not perceived there at all, it must be unreal and false, like a dream.

verses.sanskrit:
अतः पृथङ्नास्ति जगत्परात्मनः पृथक्प्रतीतिस्तु मृषा गुणादिवत् ।
आरोपितस्यास्ति किमर्थवत्ताद् धिष्ठानमाभाति तथा भ्रमेण ॥ २३५ ॥
verses.roman:
ataḥ pṛthaṅnāsti jagatparātmanaḥ pṛthakpratītistu mṛṣā guṇādivat |
āropitasyāsti kimarthavattād dhiṣṭhānamābhāti tathā bhrameṇa || 235 ||
verses.colloquial:
atah prithak na asti jagat para aatmanah prithak pratiitis tu mrishaa guna aadi vat |
aaropitasya asti kim arthavattaa adhishthhaanam aabhaati tathaa bhrameena || 235 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So the universe does not exist apart from the Supreme Self, and to perceive it as separate is as false as the qualities (blueness and so on) seen in the sky. Does a superimposed attribute have any meaning apart from its substratum? It is the substratum that appears in that way through delusion.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रान्तस्य यद्यद्भ्रमतः प्रतीतं भ्रामैव तत्तद्रजतं हि शुक्तिः ।
इदंतया ब्रह्म सदैव रूप्यते त्वारोपितं ब्रह्मणि नाममात्रम् ॥ २३६ ॥
verses.roman:
bhrāntasya yadyadbhramataḥ pratītaṃ bhrāmaiva tattadrajataṃ hi śuktiḥ |
idaṃtayā brahma sadaiva rūpyate tvāropitaṃ brahmaṇi nāmamātram || 236 ||
verses.colloquial:
bhraantasya yad yad bhramatah pratiitam bhraama eva tat tad rajatam hi shuktih |
idamtayaa brahma sada eva ruupyate tv aaropitam brahmani naama maatram || 236 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whatever a deluded person mistakenly perceives is Brahman and Brahman alone. The silver is nothing but mother-of-pearl. It is Brahman that is constantly taken to be this universe, while the universe superimposed on Brahman is merely a name.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Brahman - Its Nature</vt>
अतः परं ब्रह्म सदद्वितीयं विशुद्धविज्ञानघनं निरञ्जनम् ।
प्राशान्तमाद्यन्तविहीनमक्रियं निरन्तरानन्दरसस्वरूपम् ॥ २३७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Brahman - Its Nature</vt>
ataḥ paraṃ brahma sadadvatīyaṃ viśuddhavijñānaghanaṃ nirañjanam |
prāśāntamādyantavihīnamakrīyaṃ nirantarānandarasasvarūpam || 237 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Brahman - Its Nature</vt>
atah param brahma sat advatiiyam vishuddha vijnaana ghanam niranjanam |
praashaantam aadi anta vihiinam akriyam nirantara aananda rasa svaruupam || 237 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So whatever is manifested, this universe, is the Supreme Brahman Itself: the Real, the One without a second, pure, the Essence of Knowledge, stainless, serene, without beginning or end, beyond activity, the Essence of Bliss Absolute. It transcends all the diversity created by Māyā or Nescience. It is eternal, forever out of reach of pain, indivisible, immeasurable, formless, undifferentiated, nameless, immutable, and self-luminous.

verses.sanskrit:
निरस्तमायाकृतसर्वभेदं नित्यं सुखं निष्कलमप्रमेयम् ।
अरूपमव्यक्तमनाख्यमव्ययं ज्योतिः स्वयं किंचिदिदं चकास्ति ॥ २३८ ॥
verses.roman:
nirastamāyākṛtasarvabhedaṃ nityaṃ sukhaṃ niṣkalamaprameyam |
arūpamavyaktamanākhyamavyayaṃ jyotiḥ svayaṃ kiṃcididaṃ cakāsti || 238 ||
verses.colloquial:
nirasta maayaa krita sarva bhedam nityam sukham nishkalam aprameyam |
aruupam avyaktam anaakhyam avyayam jyotih svayam kimchit idam chakaasti || 238 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So whatever is manifested, this universe, is the Supreme Brahman Itself: the Real, the One without a second, pure, the Essence of Knowledge, stainless, serene, without beginning or end, beyond activity, the Essence of Bliss Absolute. It transcends all the diversity created by Māyā or Nescience. It is eternal, forever out of reach of pain, indivisible, immeasurable, formless, undifferentiated, nameless, immutable, and self-luminous.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञातृज्ञेयज्ञानशून्यमनन्तं निर्विकल्पकम् ।
केवलाखण्डचिन्मात्रं परं तत्त्वं विदुर्बुधाः ॥ २३९ ॥
verses.roman:
jñātṛjñeyajñānaśūnyamanantaṃ nirvikalpakam |
kevalākhaṇḍacinmātraṃ paraṃ tattvaṃ vidurbudhāḥ || 239 ||
verses.colloquial:
jnaatri jneya jnaana shuunyam anantam nirvikalpakam |
kevala akhanda cin maatram param tattvam vidur budhaah || 239 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Sages realize the Supreme Truth, Brahman, in which knower, knowledge, and known are not differentiated, and which is infinite, transcendent, and the Essence of Knowledge Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
अहेयमनुपादेयं मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
अप्रमेयमनाद्यन्तं ब्रह्म पूर्णमहं महः ॥ २४0 ॥
verses.roman:
aheyamanupādeyaṃ manovācāmagocaram |
aprameyamanādyantaṃ brahma pūrṇamahaṃ mahaḥ || 240 ||
verses.colloquial:
aheyam anupaaadeyam mano vaacaam agocaram |
aprameyam anaadyantam brahma puurnam aham mahah || 240 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It can be neither cast off nor taken up. It lies beyond the reach of mind and speech. It is immeasurable, without beginning or end, the Whole, one's very Self, and of surpassing glory.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>That Thou Art - Explanation</vt>
तत्त्वंपदाभ्यामभिधीयमानयोः ब्रह्मात्मनोः शोधितयोर्यदीत्थम् ।
श्रुत्या तयोस्तत्त्वमसीति सम्यग् एकत्वमेव प्रतिपाद्यते मुहुः ॥ २४१ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>That Thou Art - Explanation</vt>
tattvaṃpadābhyāmabhidhīyamānayoḥ brahmātmanoḥ śodhitayoryadīttham |
śrutyā tayostattvamasīti samyag ekatvameva pratipādyate muhuḥ || 241 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>That Thou Art - Explanation</vt>
tattvam padaabhyaam abhidhiiyamaanayoh brahma aatmanoh shodhitayoh yadi ittham |
shrutyaa tayoh tat tvam asi iti samyag ekatvam eva pratipaadyate muhuh || 241 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the Shruti, in the saying "Thou art That" (Tat-Tvam-Asi), repeatedly affirms the complete identity of Brahman (or Ishwara) and the Jiva, indicated by the words "That" (Tat) and "thou" (Tvam), while stripping those words of their relative associations, what it means to teach is the identity of their implied meanings, not their literal ones. Taken literally, the two have opposite attributes, like the sun and a glow-worm, a king and a servant, the ocean and a well, or Mount Meru and an atom.

verses.sanskrit:
अइक्यं तयोर्लक्षितयोर्न वाच्ययोः निगद्यतेऽन्योन्यविरुद्धधर्मिणोः ।
खद्योतभान्वोरिव राजभृत्ययोः कूपाम्बुराश्योः परमाणुमेर्वोः ॥ २४२ ॥
verses.roman:
aikyaṃ tayorlakṣitayorna vācyayoḥ nigadyate'nyonyaviruddhadharmiṇoḥ |
khadyotabhānvoriva rājabhṛtyayoḥ kūpāmburāśyoḥ paramāṇumervoḥ || 242 ||
verses.colloquial:
aikyam tayoh lakshitayoh na vaacyayoh nigadyate anyonya viruddha dharminoh |
khadyota bhaanvoh iva raaja bhrityayoh kuupa ambu raashyoh paramaanu mervoh || 242 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the Shruti, in the saying "Thou art That" (Tat-Tvam-Asi), repeatedly affirms the complete identity of Brahman (or Ishwara) and the Jiva, indicated by the words "That" (Tat) and "thou" (Tvam), while stripping those words of their relative associations, what it means to teach is the identity of their implied meanings, not their literal ones. Taken literally, the two have opposite attributes, like the sun and a glow-worm, a king and a servant, the ocean and a well, or Mount Meru and an atom.

verses.sanskrit:
तयोर्विरोधोऽयमुपाधिकल्पितो न वास्तवः कश्चिदुपाधिरेषः ।
ईशस्य माया महदादिकारणं जीवस्य कार्यं शृणु पञ्चकोशम् ॥ २४३ ॥
verses.roman:
tayorvirodho'yamupādhikalpito na vāstavaḥ kaścidupādhireṣaḥ |
īśasya māyā mahadādikāraṇaṃ jīvasya kāryaṃ śṛṇu pañcakośam || 243 ||
verses.colloquial:
tayor virodho ayam upaadhi kalpito na vaastavah kashcid upaadhi reshah |
iishasya maayaa mahad aadi kaaranam jiivasya kaaryam shrinu pancha kosham || 243 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This opposition between them is produced by superimposition; it is not real. In the case of Ishwara (the Lord), the superimposition is Maya, or Nescience, the cause of Mahat and everything that follows. In the case of the Jiva (the individual soul), listen: the five sheaths, which are the products of Maya, play that role.

verses.sanskrit:
एतावुपाधी परजीवयोस्तयोः सम्यङ्निरासे न परो न जीवः ।
राज्यं नरेन्द्रस्य भटस्य खेटक् तयोरपोहे न भटो न राजा ॥ २४४ ॥
verses.roman:
etāvupādhī parajīvayostayoḥ samyaṅnirāse na paro na jīvaḥ |
rājyaṃ narendrasya bhaṭasya kheṭak tayorapohe na bhaṭo na rājā || 244 ||
verses.colloquial:
etau upaadhi para jiivayos tayoh samyak niraase na paro na jiivah |
raajyam narendrasya bhatasya khetaka tayor apohe na bhato na raajaa || 244 ||
verses.translation_reworded: These two are the superimpositions belonging to Ishwara and to the Jiva. When they are completely removed, there is neither Ishwara nor Jiva. A kingdom marks a king, and a shield marks a soldier; take these away, and there is no king and no soldier.

verses.sanskrit:
अथात आदेश इति श्रुतिः स्वयं निषेधति ब्रह्मणि कल्पितं द्वयम् ।
श्रुतिप्रमाणानुगृहीतबोधात् तयोर्निरासः करणीय एव ॥ २४५ ॥
verses.roman:
athāta ādeśa iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ niṣedhati brahmaṇi kalpitaṃ dvayam |
śrutipramāṇānugṛhītabodhāt tayornirāsaḥ karaṇīya eva || 245 ||
verses.colloquial:
atha ata aadesha iti shrutih svayam nishedhati brahmani kalpitam dvayam |
shruti pramaana anugriihiita bodhaat tayor niraasah karaniiya eva || 245 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Vedas themselves, in passages such as "now then is the injunction," reject the duality imagined in Brahman. One must remove those two superimpositions through realization backed by the authority of the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit:
नेदं नेदं कल्पितत्वान्न सत्यं रज्जुदृष्टव्यालवत्स्वप्नवच्च ।
इत्थं दृश्यं साधुयुक्त्या व्यपोह्य ज्ञेयः पश्चादेकभावस्तयोर्यः ॥ २४६ ॥
verses.roman:
nedaṃ nedaṃ kalpitatvānna satyaṃ rajjudṛṣṭavyālavatsvapnavacca |
itthaṃ dṛśyaṃ sādhuyuktyā vyapohya jñeyaḥ paścādekabhāvastayoryaḥ || 246 ||
verses.colloquial:
na idam na idam kalpitatvaat na satyam rajju drishta vyaalavat svapnavat cha |
ittham drishyam saadhu yuktyaa vyapohya jneyah pashchaat eka bhaavas tayor yah || 246 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Neither this gross universe nor this subtle universe is the Atman. Being imagined, they are unreal, like the snake seen in a rope or the things seen in dreams. Having thoroughly eliminated the objective world in this way through reasoning, one should go on to realize the oneness that underlies Ishwara and the Jiva.

verses.sanskrit:
ततस्तु तौ लक्षणया सुलक्ष्यौ तयोरखण्डैकरसत्वसिद्धये ।
नालं जहत्या न तथाजहत्या किन्तूभयार्थात्मिकयैव भाव्यम् ॥ २४७ ॥
verses.roman:
tatastu tau lakṣaṇayā sulakṣyau tayorakhaṇḍaikarasatvasiddhaye |
nālaṃ jahatyā na tathājahatyā kintūbhayārthātmikayaiva bhāvyam || 247 ||
verses.colloquial:
tatas tu tau lakshanaayaa su lakshyau tayor akhanda eka rasa tva siddhaye |
na alam jahatyaa na tathaa jahatyaa kintu ubhaya artha aatmikayaa eva bhaavyam || 247 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Therefore those two terms, Ishwara and Jiva, must be weighed carefully by their implied meanings, so that their complete identity can be established. Neither rejecting their meaning entirely nor keeping it entirely will work. One must reason it out by the method that combines both.

verses.sanskrit:
स देवदत्तोऽयमितीह चैकता विरुद्धधर्मांशमपास्य कथ्यते ।
यथा तथा तत्त्वमसीतिवाक्ये विरुद्धधर्मानुभयत्र हित्वा ॥ २४८ ॥
verses.roman:
sa devadatto'yamitīha caikatā viruddhadharmāṃśamapāsya kathyate |
yathā tathā tattvamasītivākye viruddhadharmānubhayatra hitvā || 248 ||
verses.colloquial:
sa devadattah ayam iti iha ca ekataa viruddha dharma amsham apaasya kathyate |
yathaa tathaa tat tvam asi iti vaakye viruddha dharmaan ubhayatra hitvaa || 248 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Just as the sentence "This is that Devadatta" expresses identity by setting aside the parts that conflict, so in the sentence "Thou art That" the wise person must drop the conflicting elements on both sides and recognize the identity of Ishwara and Jiva, attending closely to the essence shared by both, which is Chit, Knowledge Absolute. In this way hundreds of scriptural texts teach the oneness and identity of Brahman and the Jiva.

verses.sanskrit:
संलक्ष्य चिन्मात्रतया सदात्मनोः अखण्डभावः परिचीयते बुधैः ।
एवं महावाक्यशतेन कथ्यते ब्रह्मात्मनोरैक्यमखण्डभावः ॥ २४९ ॥
verses.roman:
saṃlakṣya cinmātratayā sadātmanoḥ akhaṇḍabhāvaḥ paricīyate budhaiḥ |
evaṃ mahāvākyaśatena kathyate brahmātmanoraikyamakhaṇḍabhāvaḥ || 249 ||
verses.colloquial:
samlakshya chin maatratayaa sat aatmanoh akhanda bhaavah parichiyate budhaih |
evam mahaa vaakya shatena kathyate brahma aatmanoh aikyam akhanda bhaavah || 249 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Just as the sentence "This is that Devadatta" expresses identity by setting aside the parts that conflict, so in the sentence "Thou art That" the wise person must drop the conflicting elements on both sides and recognize the identity of Ishwara and Jiva, attending closely to the essence shared by both, which is Chit, Knowledge Absolute. In this way hundreds of scriptural texts teach the oneness and identity of Brahman and the Jiva.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Attitude in Meditation</vt>
अस्थूलमित्येतदसन्निरस्य सिद्धं स्वतो व्योमवदप्रतर्क्यम् ।
अतो मृषामात्रमिदं प्रतीतं जहीहि यत्स्वात्मतया गृहीतम् ब्रह्माहमित्येव विशुद्धबुद्ध्या विद्धि स्वमात्मानमखण्डबोधम् ॥ २५0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Attitude in Meditation</vt>
asthūlamityetadasannirasya siddhaṃ svato vyomavadapratarkyam |
ato mṛṣāmātramidaṃ pratītaṃ jahīhi yatsvātmatayā gṛhītam brahmāhamityeva viśuddhabuddhyā viddhi svamātmānamakhaṇḍabodham || 250 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Attitude in Meditation</vt>
asthuulam iti etat asat nirasya siddham svato vyomavat apratarkyam |
ato mrishaa maatram idam pratiitam jahiihi yat svaatmatayaa grihiitam brahma aham iti eva vishuddha buddhyaa viddhi svam aatmaanam akhanda bodham || 250 ||
verses.translation_reworded: By eliminating the not-Self in the light of passages such as "It is not gross," one realizes the Atman, which stands on its own, is unattached like the sky, and lies beyond the reach of thought. So dismiss this mere phantom of a body that you perceive and have taken to be your own self. With the purified understanding that you are Brahman, realize your own Self, the Knowledge Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
मृत्कार्यं सकलं घटादि सततं मृन्मात्रमेवाहितं तद्वत्सज्जनितं सदात्मकमिदं सन्मात्रमेवाखिलम् ।
यस्मान्नास्ति सतः परं किमपि तत्सत्यं स आत्मा स्वयं तस्मात्तत्त्वमसि प्रशान्तममलं ब्रह्माद्वयं यत्परम् ॥ २५१ ॥
verses.roman:
mṛtkāryaṃ sakalaṃ ghaṭādi satataṃ mṛnmātramevāhitaṃ tadvatsajjanitaṃ sadātmakamidaṃ sanmātramevākhilam |
yasmānnāsti sataḥ paraṃ kimapi tatsatyaṃ sa ātmā svayaṃ tasmāttattvamasi praśāntamamalaṃ brahmādvayaṃ yatparam || 251 ||
verses.colloquial:
mrit kaaryam sakalam ghata aadi satatam mrin maatram eva aahitam tadvat saj janitam sat aatmakam idam san maatram eva akhilam |
yasmaat na asti satah param kim api tat satyam sa aatmaa svayam tasmaat tat tvam asi prashaantam amalam brahma advayam yat param || 251 ||
verses.translation_reworded: All the forms clay takes, such as a jar, which the mind always accepts as real, are in truth nothing but clay. In the same way, this whole universe, which comes forth from the real Brahman, is Brahman Itself and nothing else. Since there is nothing whatsoever apart from Brahman, and That is the sole self-existent Reality, our very Self, you are that serene, pure, Supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
निद्राकल्पितदेशकालविषयज्ञात्रादि सर्वं यथा मिथ्या तद्वदिहापि जाग्रति जगत्स्वाज्ञानकार्यत्वतः ।
यस्मादेवमिदं शरीरकरणप्राणाहमाद्यप्यसत् तस्मात्तत्त्वमसि प्रशान्तममलं ब्रह्माद्वयं यत्परम् ॥ २५२ ॥
verses.roman:
nidrākalpitadeśakālaviṣayajñātrādi sarvaṃ yathā mithyā tadvadihāpi jāgrati jagatsvājñānakāryatvataḥ |
yasmādevamidaṃ śarīrakaraṇaprāṇāhamādyapyasat tasmāttattvamasi praśāntamamalaṃ brahmādvayaṃ yatparam || 252 ||
verses.colloquial:
nidraa kalpita desha kaala vishaya jnyaatr aadi sarvam yathaa mithyaa tadvat iha api jaagrati jagat sva ajnyaana kaaryatvataaha |
yasmaat evam idam shariira karana praana aham aadi api asat tasmaat tat tvam asi prashaantam amalam brahma advayam yat param || 252 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Just as the place, time, objects, knower, and so on that appear in a dream are all unreal, so too is the world experienced here in the waking state, for it is entirely the product of one's own ignorance. Since this body, the organs, the Pranas, egoism, and the rest are likewise unreal, you are that serene, pure, Supreme Brahman, the One without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र भ्रान्त्या कल्पित तद्विवेके तत्तन्मात्रं नैव तस्माद्विभिन्नम् ।
स्वप्ने नष्टं स्वप्नविश्वं विचित्रं स्वस्माद्भिन्नं किन्नु दृष्टं प्रबोधे ॥ २५३ ॥
verses.roman:
yatra bhrāntyā kalpita tadviveke tattanmātraṃ naiva tasmādvibhinnam |
svapne naṣṭaṃ svapnaviśvaṃ vicitraṃ svasmādbhinnaṃ kinnu dṛṣṭaṃ prabodhe || 253 ||
verses.colloquial:
yatra bhraantyaa kalpita tad viveke tat tan maatram na eva tasmaat vibhinnam |
svapne nashtam svapna vishvam vicitram svasmaat bhinnam kinnu drishtam prabodhe || 253 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whatever is mistakenly thought to exist in something is, once the truth about it is known, nothing but that underlying substratum and in no way different from it. The varied universe of a dream appears and vanishes within the dream itself. On waking, does it appear as anything separate from one's own Self?

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Aids to Meditation</vt>
जातिनीतिकुलगोत्रदूरगं नामरूपगुणदोषवर्जितम् ।
देशकालविषयातिवर्ति यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५४ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Aids to Meditation</vt>
jātinītikulagotradūragaṃ nāmarūpaguṇadoṣavarjitam |
deśakālaviṣayātivarti yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 254 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Aids to Meditation</vt>
jaati niiti kula gotra duuragam naama ruupa guna dosha varjitam |
desha kaala vishaya ativarti yad brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 254 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which is beyond caste and creed, family and lineage; which has no name or form, no merit or demerit; which transcends space, time, and sense-objects: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्परं सकलवागगोचरं गोचरं विमलबोधचक्षुषः ।
शुद्धचिद्घनमनादि वस्तु यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५५ ॥
verses.roman:
yatparaṃ sakalavāgagocaraṃ gocaraṃ vimalabodhacakṣuṣaḥ |
śuddhacidghanamanādi vastu yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 255 ||
verses.colloquial:
yat param sakala vaag agocharam gocharam vimala bodha chakshusah |
shuddha chid ghanam anaadi vastu yat brahma tat tvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 255 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That Supreme Brahman which lies beyond the reach of all speech yet is open to the eye of pure illumination; which is pure, the very Embodiment of Knowledge, the reality without beginning: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
षड्भिरूर्मिभिरयोगि योगिहृद् भावितं न करणैर्विभावितम् ।
बुद्ध्यवेद्यमनवद्यमस्ति यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५६ ॥
verses.roman:
ṣaḍbhirūrmibhirayogi yogihṛd bhāvitaṃ na karaṇairvibhāvitam |
buddhyavedyamanavadyamasti yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 256 ||
verses.colloquial:
shadbhir urmibhir ayogi yogi hrid bhaavitam na karanair vibhaavitam |
buddhi avedyam anavadyam asti yad brahma tat tvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 256 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which the sixfold wave does not touch; which the Yogi's heart meditates upon but the sense-organs cannot grasp; which the Buddhi cannot know; and which cannot be faulted: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
भ्रान्तिकल्पितजगत्कलाश्रयं स्वाश्रयं च सदसद्विलक्षणम् ।
निष्कलं निरुपमानवद्धि यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५७ ॥
verses.roman:
bhrāntikalpitajagatkalāśrayaṃ svāśrayaṃ ca sadasadvilakṣaṇam |
niṣkalaṃ nirupamānavaddhi yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 257 ||
verses.colloquial:
bhraanti kalpita jagat kalaa aashrayam sva aashrayam ca sat asat vilakshanam |
nishkalam nirupamaanavad dhi yad brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 257 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which underlies the universe with all its divisions, every one of them a creation of delusion; which Itself rests on nothing else; which is distinct from the gross and the subtle; which has no parts and truly no model: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
जन्मवृद्धिपरिणत्यपक्षय व्याधिनाशनविहीनमव्ययम् ।
विश्वसृष्ट्यवविघातकारणं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५८ ॥
verses.roman:
janmavṛddhipariṇatyapakṣaya vyādhināśanavihīnamavyayam |
viśvasṛṣṭyavavighātakāraṇaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 258 ||
verses.colloquial:
janma vriddhi parinaati apakshaya vyaadhi naashana vihiinam avyayam |
vishva srishti ava vighaata kaaranam brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 258 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which is free from birth, growth, development, decay, disease, and death; which cannot be destroyed; which is the cause of the projection, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्तभेदमनपास्तलक्षणं निस्तरङ्गजलराशिनिश्चलम् ।
नित्यमुक्तमविभक्तमूर्ति यद् ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २५९ ॥
verses.roman:
astabhedamanapāstalakṣaṇaṃ nistaraṅgajalarāśiniścalam |
nityamuktamavibhaktamūrti yad brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 259 ||
verses.colloquial:
asta bhedam anapaasta lakshanam nistaranga jala raashi nishchalam |
nitya muktam avibhakta muurti yad brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 259 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which is free of all differentiation; whose essence never ceases to exist; which is still like an ocean without waves; ever free; indivisible in Form: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
एकमेव सदनेककारणं कारणान्तरनिरास्यकारणम् ।
कार्यकारणविलक्षणं स्वयं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६0 ॥
verses.roman:
ekameva sadanekakāraṇaṃ kāraṇāntaranirāsyakāraṇam |
kāryakāraṇavilakṣaṇaṃ svayaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 260 ||
verses.colloquial:
ekam eva sat aneka kaaranam kaarana antara niraasya kaaranam |
kaarya kaarana vilakshanam svayam brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 260 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which, though One alone, is the cause of the many; which rules out every other cause yet has no cause Itself; which is distinct from Maya and from its effect, the universe; and which is independent: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्विकल्पकमनल्पमक्षरं यत्क्षराक्षरविलक्षणं परम् ।
नित्यमव्ययसुखं निरञ्जनं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६१ ॥
verses.roman:
nirvikalpakamanalpamakṣaraṃ yatkṣarākṣaravilakṣaṇaṃ param |
nityamavyayasukhaṃ nirañjanaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 261 ||
verses.colloquial:
nirvikalpakam analpam aksharam yat kshara akshara vilakshanam param |
nityam avyaya sukham niranjanam brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 261 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which is free from duality; infinite and indestructible; distinct from the universe and from Maya; supreme and eternal; undying Bliss; without stain: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
यद्विभाति सदनेकधा भ्रमान् नामरूपगुणविक्रियात्मना ।
हेमवत्स्वयमविक्रियं सदा ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६२ ॥
verses.roman:
yadvibhāti sadanekadhā bhramān nāmarūpaguṇavikriyātmanā |
hemavatsvayamavikriyaṃ sadā brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 262 ||
verses.colloquial:
yad vibhaati sad anekadhaa bhramaat naama ruupa guna vikriyaa aatmanaa |
hemavat svayam avikriyam sadaa brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 262 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That Reality which, though One, appears in many ways through delusion, taking on names and forms, qualities and changes, while Itself remaining ever unchanged, like gold in its various shapes: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
यच्चकास्त्यनपरं परात्परं प्रत्यगेकरसमात्मलक्षणम् ।
सत्यचित्सुखमनन्तमव्ययं ब्रह्म तत्त्वमसि भावयात्मनि ॥ २६३ ॥
verses.roman:
yaccakāstyanaparaṃ parātparaṃ pratyagekarasamātmalakṣaṇam |
satyacitsukhamanantamavyayaṃ brahma tattvamasi bhāvayātmani || 263 ||
verses.colloquial:
yat ca kaasti an aparam paraat param pratyak eka rasam aatma lakshanam |
satya cit sukham anantam avyayam brahma tattvam asi bhaavaya aatmani || 263 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That beyond which nothing exists; which shines even above Maya, which in turn stands above its effect, the universe; the innermost Self of all, free from differentiation; the Real Self, Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute; infinite and unchanging: that Brahman you are. Meditate on this in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
उक्तमर्थमिममात्मनि स्वयं भावयेत्प्रथितयुक्तिभिर्धिया ।
संशयादिरहितं कराम्बुवत् तेन तत्त्वनिगमो भविष्यति ॥ २६४ ॥
verses.roman:
uktamarthamimamātmani svayaṃ bhāvayetprathitayuktibhirdhiyā |
saṃśayādirahitaṃ karāmbuvat tena tattvanigamo bhaviṣyati || 264 ||
verses.colloquial:
uktam artham imam aatmani svayam bhaavayet prathita yuktibhir dhiyaa |
samshayaadi rahitam kara ambu vat tena tattva nigamo bhavishyati || 264 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One must meditate in one's own mind on the Truth taught above, using the intellect and the accepted lines of reasoning. By doing so one will realize the truth free of doubt and the like, as plainly as water in the palm of one's hand.

verses.sanskrit:
संबोधमात्रं परिशुद्धतत्त्वं विज्ञाय सङ्घे नृपवच्च सैन्ये ।
तदाश्रयः स्वात्मनि सर्वदा स्थितो विलापय ब्रह्मणि विश्वजातम् ॥ २६५ ॥
verses.roman:
saṃbodhamātraṃ pariśuddhatattvaṃ vijñāya saṅghe nṛpavacca sainye |
tadāśrayaḥ svātmani sarvadā sthito vilāpaya brahmaṇi viśvajātam || 265 ||
verses.colloquial:
sambodha maatram parishuddha tattvam vijnaaya sanghe nripa vat cha sainye |
tad aashrayah sva aatmani sarvadaa sthito vilaapaya brahmani vishva jaatam || 265 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Realizing in this body the Knowledge Absolute, free of Nescience and its effects, as one picks out the king in an army, and remaining always established in your own Self by resting on that Knowledge, dissolve the universe in Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धौ गुहायां सदसद्विलक्षणं ब्रह्मास्ति सत्यं परमद्वितीयम् ।
तदात्मना योऽत्र वसेद्गुहायां पुनर्न तस्याङ्गगुहाप्रवेशः ॥ २६६ ॥
verses.roman:
buddhau guhāyāṃ sadasadvilakṣaṇaṃ brahmāsti satyaṃ paramadvitīyam |
tadātmanā yo'tra vasedguhāyāṃ punarna tasyāṅgaguhāpraveśaḥ || 266 ||
verses.colloquial:
buddhau guhaayaam sad asad vilakshanam brahma asti satyam parama adviitiiyam |
tad aatmanaa yo atra vased guhaayaam punar na tasya anga guhaa praveshah || 266 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the cave of the Buddhi dwells Brahman, distinct from the gross and the subtle, Existence Absolute, Supreme, the One without a second. For the one who lives in this cave as Brahman, O beloved, there is no further entry into a mother's womb.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Give up Vāsanās - the Method</vt>
ज्ञाते वस्तुन्यपि बलवती वासनानादिरेषा कर्ता भोक्ताप्यहमिति दृढा यास्य संसारहेतुः ।
प्रत्यग्दृष्ट्यात्मनि निवसता सापनेया प्रयत्नान् मुक्तिं प्राहुस्तदिह मुनयो वासनातानवं यत् ॥ २६७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Give up Vāsanās - the Method</vt>
jñāte vastunyapi balavatī vāsanānādireṣā kartā bhoktāpyahamiti dṛḍhā yāsya saṃsārahetuḥ |
pratyagdṛṣṭyātmani nivasatā sāpaneyā prayatnān muktiṃ prāhustadiha munayo vāsanātānavaṃ yat || 267 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Give up Vāsanās - the Method</vt>
jnaate vastuni api balavatii vaasanaa anaadih eshaa kartaa bhoktaa api aham iti dridhaa yaa asya samsaara hetuh |
pratyag drishtyaa aatmani nivasataa saa apaneyaa prayatnaat mukti praahuh tat iha munayo vaasanaa taanavam yat || 267 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Even after the Truth has been realized, there persists the strong, beginningless, stubborn impression that one is the doer and the experiencer, and this is the cause of one's transmigration. It must be carefully removed by living in constant identification with the Supreme Self. The sages call Liberation the wearing away of Vasanas (impressions) here and now.

verses.sanskrit:
अहं ममेति यो भावो देहाक्षादावनात्मनि ।
अध्यासोऽयं निरस्तव्यो विदुषा स्वात्मनिष्ठया ॥ २६८ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃ mameti yo bhāvo dehākṣādāvanātmani |
adhyāso'yaṃ nirastavyo viduṣā svātmaniṣṭhayā || 268 ||
verses.colloquial:
aham mama iti yo bhaavo deha aksha aadaav an aatmani |
adhyaaso ayam nirastavyo vidushaa sva aatma nishthayaa || 268 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The notion of "me" and "mine" in the body, the organs, and the rest, which are the non-Self: this superimposition the wise person must bring to an end by identifying himself with the Atman.

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञात्वा स्वं प्रत्यगात्मानं बुद्धितद्वृत्तिसाक्षिणम् ।
सोऽहमित्येव सद्वृत्त्यानात्मन्यात्ममतिं जहि ॥ २६९ ॥
verses.roman:
jñātvā svaṃ pratyagātmānaṃ buddhitadvṛttisākṣiṇam |
so'hamityeva sadvṛttyānātmanyātmamatiṃ jahi || 269 ||
verses.colloquial:
jnaatvaa svam pratyag aatmaanam buddhi tad vritti saakshinam |
so aham iti eva sad vrittyaa anaatmani aatma matim jahi || 269 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Realizing your own innermost Self, the Witness of the Buddhi and its changes, and continually turning over the positive thought "I am That," overcome this identification with the non-Self.

verses.sanskrit:
लोकानुवर्तनं त्यक्त्वा त्यक्त्वा देहानुवर्तनम् ।
शास्त्रानुवर्तनं त्यक्त्वा स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७0 ॥
verses.roman:
lokānuvartanaṃ tyaktvā tyaktvā dehānuvartanam |
śāstrānuvartanaṃ tyaktvā svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 270 ||
verses.colloquial:
loka anuvartanam tyaktvaa tyaktvaa deha anuvartanam |
shaastra anuvartanam tyaktvaa sva adhyaasa apanayam kuru || 270 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Giving up the observance of social conventions, abandoning all concern with adorning the body, and avoiding excessive absorption in the Scriptures, remove the superimposition that has settled on you.

verses.sanskrit:
लोकवासनया जन्तोः शास्त्रवासनयापि च ।
देहवासनया ज्ञानं यथावन्नैव जायते ॥ २७१ ॥
verses.roman:
lokavāsanayā jantoḥ śāstravāsanayāpi ca |
dehavāsanayā jñānaṃ yathāvannaiva jāyate || 271 ||
verses.colloquial:
loka vaasanayaa jantoh shaastra vaasanayaa api ca |
deha vaasanayaa jnaanam yathaavat na eva jaayate || 271 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Because of the urge to chase after society, the passion for excessive study of the Scriptures, and the wish to keep the body in good condition, people fail to reach true Realization.

verses.sanskrit:
संसारकारागृहमोक्षमिच्छोर् अयोमायां पादनिबन्धशृङ्खलम् ।
वदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः पटु वासनात्रयं योऽस्माद्विमुक्तः समुपैति मुक्तिम् ॥ २७२ ॥
verses.roman:
saṃsārakārāgṛhamokṣamicchor ayoMāyāṃ pādanibandhaśṛṅkhalam |
vadanti tajjñāḥ paṭu vāsanātrayaṃ yo'smādvimuktaḥ samupaiti muktim || 272 ||
verses.colloquial:
samsaara kaaraagriha moksham icchor ayo maayaam paada nibandha shrinkhalam |
vadanti tajjnaah patu vaasanaa trayam yo asmaat vimuktah samupaiti muktim || 272 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For one who seeks release from the prison of this world (Samsara), the wise have named those three desires heavy iron chains that bind the feet. The one who is free of them truly reaches Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
जलादिसंसर्गवशात्प्रभूत दुर्गन्धधूतागरुदिव्यवासना ।
संघर्षणेनैव विभाति सम्यग् विधूयमाने सति बाह्यगन्धे ॥ २७३ ॥
verses.roman:
jalādisaṃsargavaśātprabhūta durgandhadhūtāgarudivyavāsanā |
saṃgharṣaṇenaiva vibhāti samyag vidhūyamāne sati bāhyagandhe || 273 ||
verses.colloquial:
jala aadi samsarga vashaat prabhuta durgandha dhuuta agaru divya vaasanaa |
samgharshanena eva vibhaati samyag vidhuuyamaane sati baahya gandhe || 273 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The pleasant fragrance of Agaru (agalochum), hidden by a strong stench from contact with water and the like, comes through as soon as the foreign smell has been fully rubbed away.

verses.sanskrit:
अन्तःश्रितानन्तदूरन्तवासना धूलीविलिप्ता परमात्मवासना ।
प्रज्ञातिसंघर्षणतो विशुद्धा प्रतीयते चन्दनगन्धवत्स्फुटम् ॥ २७४ ॥
verses.roman:
antaḥśritānantadūrantavāsanā dhūlīviliptā paramātmavāsanā |
prajñātisaṃgharṣaṇato viśuddhā pratīyate candanagandhavatsphuṭam || 274 ||
verses.colloquial:
antah shrita ananta duura anta vaasanaa dhuulii viliptaa paramaatma vaasanaa |
prajnaati samgharshanato vishuddhaa pratiiyate chandana gandhavat sphutam || 274 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Like the fragrance of sandalwood, the perfume of the Supreme Self, buried under the dust of countless violent impressions lodged in the mind, is clearly perceived again once it is purified by the constant friction of Knowledge.

verses.sanskrit:
अनात्मवासनाजालैस्तिरोभूतात्मवासना ।
नित्यात्मनिष्ठया तेषां नाशे भाति स्वयं स्फुटम् ॥ २७५ ॥
verses.roman:
anātmavāsanājālaistirobhūtātmavāsanā |
nityātmaniṣṭhayā teṣāṃ nāśe bhāti svayaṃ sphuṭam || 275 ||
verses.colloquial:
anaatma vaasanaa jaalais tirobhuuta aatma vaasanaa |
nitya aatma nishthayaa teshaam naashe bhaati svayam sphutam || 275 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The desire for Self-realization is hidden by countless desires for things other than the Self. When those have been destroyed through constant devotion to the Self, the Atman shows Itself clearly of Its own accord.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा यथा प्रत्यगवस्थितं मनः तथा तथा मुञ्चति बाह्यवासनाम् ।
निःशेषमोक्षे सति वासनानां आत्मानुभूतिः प्रतिबन्धशून्या ॥ २७६ ॥
verses.roman:
yathā yathā pratyagavasthitaṃ manaḥ tathā tathā muñcati bāhyavāsanām |
niḥśeṣamokṣe sati vāsanānāṃ ātmānubhūtiḥ pratibandhaśūnyā || 276 ||
verses.colloquial:
yathaa yathaa pratyag avasthitam manah tathaa tathaa muncati baahya vaasanaam |
nihshesha mokshe sati vaasanaanaam aatma anubhuutih pratibandha shuunyaa || 276 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As the mind becomes step by step established in the innermost Self, it gives up, in the same measure, its desires for external objects. And when all such desires are gone, the Atman is realized without obstruction.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>End Superimposition - The Means</vt>
स्वात्मन्येव सदा स्थित्वा मनो नश्यति योगिनः ।
वासनानां क्षयश्चातः स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७७ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>End Superimposition - The Means</vt>
svātmanyeva sadā sthitvā mano naśyati yoginaḥ |
vāsanānāṃ kṣayaścātaḥ svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 277 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>End Superimposition - The Means</vt>
sva aatmani eva sadaa sthitvaa mano nashyati yoginah |
vaasanaanaam kshayash ca atah sva adhyaasa apanayam kuru || 277 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Yogi's mind dies by being fixed constantly on his own Self. From this follows the ending of desires. Therefore remove your superimposition.

verses.sanskrit:
तमो द्वाभ्यां रजः सत्त्वात्सत्त्वं शुद्धेन नश्यति ।
तस्मात्सत्त्वमवष्टभ्य स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७८ ॥
verses.roman:
tamo dvābhyāṃ rajaḥ sattvātsattvaṃ śuddhena naśyati |
tasmātsattvamavaṣṭabhya svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 278 ||
verses.colloquial:
tamo dvaabhyaam rajah sattvaat sattvam shuddhena nashyati |
tasmaat sattvam avashtabhya svaadhyaasa apanayam kuru || 278 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Tamas is destroyed by both Sattva and Rajas; Rajas by Sattva; and Sattva dies when it is purified. Therefore remove your superimposition with the help of Sattva.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रारब्धं पुष्यति वपुरिति निश्चित्य निश्चलः ।
धैर्यमालम्ब्य यत्नेन स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २७९ ॥
verses.roman:
prārabdhaṃ puṣyati vapuriti niścitya niścalaḥ |
dhairyamālambya yatnena svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 279 ||
verses.colloquial:
praarabdham pushyati vapur iti nishcitya nishcalah |
dhairyam aalambya yatnena sva adhyaasa apanayam kuru || 279 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Knowing for certain that Prarabdha work will sustain this body, stay calm and remove your superimposition carefully and patiently.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहं जीवः परं ब्रह्मेत्यतद्व्यावृत्तिपूर्वकम् ।
वासनावेगतः प्राप्तस्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८0 ॥
verses.roman:
nāhaṃ jīvaḥ paraṃ brahmetyatadvyāvṛttipūrvakam |
vāsanāvegataḥ prāptasvādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 280 ||
verses.colloquial:
na aham jiivah param brahma iti atat vyaavritti puurvakam |
vaasanaa vegata praapta svaadhyaasa apanayam kuru || 280 ||
verses.translation_reworded: "I am not the individual soul but the Supreme Brahman." Eliminating in this way everything that is not the Self, remove your superimposition, which has arisen from the momentum of past impressions.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुत्या युक्त्या स्वानुभूत्या ज्ञात्वा सार्वात्म्यमात्मनः ।
क्वचिदाभासतः प्राप्तस्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८१ ॥
verses.roman:
śrutyā yuktyā svānubhūtyā jñātvā sārvātmyamātmanaḥ |
kvacidābhāsataḥ prāptasvādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 281 ||
verses.colloquial:
shrutyaa yuktyaa sva anubhuutyaa jnaatvaa saarvaatmyam aatmanah |
kvacid aabhaasatah praapta sva adhyaasa apanayam kuru || 281 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Realizing yourself as the Self of all through Scripture, reasoning, and your own experience, remove your superimposition, even when only a trace of it seems to show.

verses.sanskrit:
अनादानविसर्गाभ्यामीषन्नास्ति क्रिया मुनेः ।
तदेकनिष्ठया नित्यं स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८२ ॥
verses.roman:
anādānavisargābhyāmīṣannāsti kriyā muneḥ |
tadekaniṣṭhayā nityaṃ svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 282 ||
verses.colloquial:
anaadaana visargaabhyaam iishat na asti kriyaa muneh |
tad eka nishthayaa nityam svaadhyaasa apanayam kuru || 282 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The sage has no connection with action, since he has no notion of taking up or giving up. Therefore, through constant absorption in Brahman, remove your superimposition.

verses.sanskrit:
तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्योत्थब्रह्मात्मैकत्वबोधतः ।
ब्रह्मण्यात्मत्वदार्ढ्याय स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८३ ॥
verses.roman:
tattvamasyādivākyotthabrahmātmaikatvabodhataḥ |
brahmaṇyātmatvadārḍhyāya svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 283 ||
verses.colloquial:
tattvam asi aadi vaakya uttha brahma aatma ekatva bodhatah |
brahmani aatmatva daardhyaaya sva adhyaasa apanayam kuru || 283 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through realizing the identity of Brahman and the soul, which follows from great sayings such as "Thou art That," remove your superimposition, so as to strengthen your identification with Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
अहंभावस्य देहेऽस्मिन्निःशेषविलयावधि ।
सावधानेन युक्तात्मा स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८४ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃbhāvasya dehe'sminniḥśeṣavilayāvadhi |
sāvadhānena yuktātmā svādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 284 ||
verses.colloquial:
aham bhavasya dehe asmin nihshesha vilaya avadhi |
saavadhaanena yukta aatmaa sva adhyaasa apanayam kuru || 284 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Until identification with this body is completely uprooted, remove your superimposition with vigilance and a concentrated mind.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रतीतिर्जीवजगतोः स्वप्नवद्भाति यावता ।
तावन्निरन्तरं विद्वन्स्वाध्यासापनयं कुरु ॥ २८५ ॥
verses.roman:
pratītirjīvajagatoḥ svapnavadbhāti yāvatā |
tāvannirantaraṃ vidvansvādhyāsāpanayaṃ kuru || 285 ||
verses.colloquial:
pratiitir jiiva jagatoh svapnavad bhaati yaavataa |
taavan nirantaram vidvan svaadhyaasa apanayam kuru || 285 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As long as even a dream-like perception of the universe and of souls remains, remove your superimposition, O learned one, without the slightest pause.

verses.sanskrit:
निद्राया लोकवार्तायाः शब्दादेरपि विस्मृतेः ।
क्वचिन्नावसरं दत्त्वा चिन्तयात्मानमात्मनि ॥ २८६ ॥
verses.roman:
nidrāyā lokavārtāyāḥ śabdāderapi vismṛteḥ |
kvacinnāvasaraṃ dattvā cintayātmānamātmani || 286 ||
verses.colloquial:
nidraayaa loka vaartaayaah shabda aader api vismriteh |
kvacin na avasaram dattvaa cintaya aatmaanam aatmani || 286 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Giving not the least opening to forgetfulness, whether from sleep, worldly concerns, or the sense-objects, reflect on the Self in your mind.

verses.sanskrit:
मातापित्रोर्मलोद्भूतं मलमांसमायां वपुः ।
त्यक्त्वा चाण्डालवद्दूरं ब्रह्मीभूय कृती भव ॥ २८७ ॥
verses.roman:
mātāpitrormalodbhūtaṃ malamāṃsaMāyāṃ vapuḥ |
tyaktvā cāṇḍālavaddūraṃ brahmībhūya kṛtī bhava || 287 ||
verses.colloquial:
maataa pitror mala udbhuutam mala maamsam ayam vapuh |
tyaktvaa caandaala vat duuram brahmii bhuuya kritii bhava || 287 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Keeping a safe distance from the body, which has come from the impurities of the parents and is itself made of flesh and impurities, as one keeps away from an outcast, be Brahman and reach the fulfillment of your life.

verses.sanskrit:
घटाकाशं महाकाश इवात्मानं परात्मनि ।
विलाप्याखण्डभावेन तूष्णी भव सदा मुने ॥ २८८ ॥
verses.roman:
ghaṭākāśaṃ mahākāśa ivātmānaṃ parātmani |
vilāpyākhaṇḍabhāvena tūṣṇī bhava sadā mune || 288 ||
verses.colloquial:
ghata akaasham mahaa akaasha iva aatmaanam para aatmani |
vilaapya akhanda bhaavena tuushnii bhava sadaa mune || 288 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Merging the finite soul in the Supreme Self, as the space enclosed in a jar merges into infinite space, through meditation on their identity, remain always at peace, O sage.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वप्रकाशमधिष्ठानं स्वयंभूय सदात्मना ।
ब्रह्माण्डमपि पिण्डाण्डं त्यज्यतां मलभाण्डवत् ॥ २८९ ॥
verses.roman:
svaprakāśamadhiṣṭhānaṃ svayaṃbhūya sadātmanā |
brahmāṇḍamapi piṇḍāṇḍaṃ tyajyatāṃ malabhāṇḍavat || 289 ||
verses.colloquial:
sva prakaasham adhishthaanam svayam bhuuya sad aatmanaa |
brahma andam api pinda andam tyajyataam mala bhaanda vat || 289 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Becoming yourself the self-luminous Brahman, the substratum of all phenomena, and as that Reality, discard both the macrocosm and the microcosm, like two filthy containers.

verses.sanskrit:
चिदात्मनि सदानन्दे देहारूढामहंधियम् ।
निवेश्य लिङ्गमुत्सृज्य केवलो भव सर्वदा ॥ २९0 ॥
verses.roman:
cidātmani sadānande dehārūḍhāmahaṃdhiyam |
niveśya liṅgamutsṛjya kevalo bhava sarvadā || 290 ||
verses.colloquial:
cid aatmani sada aanande deha aaruudhaam aham dhiyam |
niveshya lingam utsrijya kevalo bhava sarvadaa || 290 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Shifting the identification now rooted in the body over to the Atman, Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, and casting off the subtle body, be forever alone and independent.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्रैष जगदाभासो दर्पणान्तः पुरं यथा ।
तद्ब्रह्माहमिति ज्ञात्वा कृतकृत्यो भविष्यसि ॥ २९१ ॥
verses.roman:
yatraiṣa jagadābhāso darpaṇāntaḥ puraṃ yathā |
tadbrahmāhamiti jñātvā kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyasi || 291 ||
verses.colloquial:
yatra esha jagat aabhaaso darpana antah puram yathaa |
tad brahma aham iti jnaatvaa krita krityo bhavishyasi || 291 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That in which this universe is reflected, like a city in a mirror: that Brahman you are. Knowing this, you will reach the fulfillment of your life.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्सत्यभूतं निजरूपमाद्यं चिदद्वयानन्दमरूपमक्रियम् ।
तदेत्य मिथ्यावपुरुत्सृजेत शैलूषवद्वेषमुपात्तमात्मनः ॥ २९२ ॥
verses.roman:
yatsatyabhūtaṃ nijarūpamādyaṃ cidadvayānandamarūpamakriyam |
tadetya mithyāvapurutsṛjeta śailūṣavadveṣamupāttamātmanaḥ || 292 ||
verses.colloquial:
yat satya bhuutam nija ruupam aadyam cid advaya aanandam aruupam akriyam |
tad etya mithyaa vapur utsrijeta shailuushavat vesham upaattam aatmanah || 292 ||
verses.translation_reworded: That which is real and is one's own original Essence, that Knowledge and Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, beyond form and activity: on attaining That, one should stop identifying with one's false bodies, like an actor setting aside the mask he has put on.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>The Perceived I' Factor - False</vt>
सर्वात्मना दृश्यमिदं मृषैव नैवाहमर्थः क्षणिकत्वदर्शनात् ।
जानाम्यहं सर्वमिति प्रतीतिः कुतोऽहमादेः क्षणिकस्य सिध्येत् ॥ २९३ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>The Perceived I' Factor - False</vt>
sarvātmanā dṛśyamidaṃ mṛṣaiva naivāhamarthaḥ kṣaṇikatvadarśanāt |
jānāmyahaṃ sarvamiti pratītiḥ kuto'hamādeḥ kṣaṇikasya sidhyet || 293 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>The Perceived I' Factor - False</vt>
sarva aatmanaa drishyam idam mrisha eva na eva aham arthah kshanika tva darshanaat |
jaanaami aham sarvam iti pratiitih kutah aham aadeh kshhanikasya sidhyet || 293 ||
verses.translation_reworded: This objective universe is wholly unreal. Nor is egoism real, for it is seen to be momentary. How can the perception "I know all" hold true of egoism and the rest, which are momentary?

verses.sanskrit:
अहंपदार्थस्त्वहमादिसाक्षी नित्यं सुषुप्तावपि भावदर्शनात् ।
ब्रूते ह्यजो नित्य इति श्रुतिः स्वयं तत्प्रत्यगात्मा सदसद्विलक्षणः ॥ २९४ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃpadārthastvahamādisākṣī nityaṃ suṣuptāvapi bhāvadarśanāt |
brūte hyajo nitya iti śrutiḥ svayaṃ tatpratyagātmā sadasadvilakṣaṇaḥ || 294 ||
verses.colloquial:
aham pada artha tvam aham aadi saakshii nityam sushuptaav api bhaava darshanaat |
bruute hi ajo nitya iti shrutih svayam tat pratyag aatmaa sad asad vilakshanah || 294 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The real "I," however, is that which witnesses the ego and everything else. It exists always, even in deep sleep. The Shruti itself says, "It is birthless, eternal," and so on. Therefore the Paramatman is different from the gross and subtle bodies.

verses.sanskrit:
विकारिणां सर्वविकारवेत्ता नित्याविकारो भवितुं समर्हति ।
मनोरथस्वप्नसुषुप्तिषु स्फुटं पुनः पुनर्दृष्टमसत्त्वमेतयोः ॥ २९५ ॥
verses.roman:
vikāriṇāṃ sarvavikāravettā nityāvikāro bhavituṃ samarhati |
manorathasvapnasuṣuptiṣu sphuṭaṃ punaḥ punardṛṣṭamasattvametayoḥ || 295 ||
verses.colloquial:
vikaarinaam sarva vikaara vettaa nitya avikaaro bhavitum samarhati |
mano ratha svapna sushuptishu sphutam punah punar drishtam asattvam etayoh || 295 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The knower of all changes in changing things must itself be eternal and changeless. The unreality of the gross and subtle bodies is observed clearly, again and again, in imagination, dream, and deep sleep.

verses.sanskrit:
अतोऽभिमानं त्यज मांसपिण्डे पिण्डाभिमानिन्यपि बुद्धिकल्पिते ।
कालत्रयाबाध्यमखण्डबोधं ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमुपैहि शान्तिम् ॥ २९६ ॥
verses.roman:
ato'bhimānaṃ tyaja māṃsapiṇḍe piṇḍābhimāninyapi buddhikalpite |
kālatrayābādhyamakhaṇḍabodhaṃ jñātvā svamātmānamupaihi śāntim || 296 ||
verses.colloquial:
ato abhimaanam tyaja maamsa pinde pinda abhimaaniny api buddhi kalpite |
kaala traya abaadhyam akhanda bodham jnaatvaa svam aatmaanam upaihi shaantim || 296 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Therefore give up identification with this lump of flesh, the gross body, and with the ego, the subtle body, both of which are imagined by the Buddhi. Realizing your own Self, which is Knowledge Absolute and cannot be denied in past, present, or future, attain Peace.

verses.sanskrit:
त्यजाभिमानं कुलगोत्रनाम रूपाश्रमेष्वार्द्रशवाश्रितेषु ।
लिङ्गस्य धर्मानपि कर्तृतादिंस् त्यक्ता भवाखण्डसुखस्वरूपः ॥ २९७ ॥
verses.roman:
tyajābhimānaṃ kulagotranāma rūpāśrameṣvārdraśavāśriteṣu |
liṅgasya dharmānapi kartṛtādiṃs tyaktā bhavākhaṇḍasukhasvarūpaḥ || 297 ||
verses.colloquial:
tyaja abhimaanam kula gotra naama ruupa aashrameshu aardra shava aashriteshu |
lingasya dharman api kartritaa adin tyaktaa bhava akhanda sukha svaruupah || 297 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Stop identifying yourself with family, lineage, name, form, and stage of life, which belong to the body, a body that is like a rotting corpse to a person of realization. Likewise, giving up notions of agency and the like, which are attributes of the subtle body, be the Essence of Bliss Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Condemnation of the Ego</vt>
सन्त्यन्ये प्रतिबन्धाः पुंसः संसारहेतवो दृष्टाः ।
तेषामेवं मूलं प्रथमविकारो भवत्यहंकारः ॥ २९८ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Condemnation of the Ego</vt>
santyanye pratibandhāḥ puṃsaḥ saṃsārahetavo dṛṣṭāḥ |
teṣāmevaṃ mūlaṃ prathamavikāro bhavatyahaṃkāraḥ || 298 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Condemnation of the Ego</vt>
santi anye pratibandhaah pumsah samsaara hetavo drishtaah |
teshaam evam muulam prathama vikaaro bhavati ahamkaarah || 298 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Other obstacles too are seen to exist for people, and they lead to transmigration. For the reasons given above, their root is the first modification of Nescience, called egoism.

verses.sanskrit:
यावत्स्यात्स्वस्य संबन्धोऽहंकारेण दुरात्मना ।
तावन्न लेशमात्रापि मुक्तिवार्ता विलक्षणा ॥ २९९ ॥
verses.roman:
yāvatsyātsvasya saṃbandho'haṃkāreṇa durātmanā |
tāvanna leśamātrāpi muktivārtā vilakṣaṇā || 299 ||
verses.colloquial:
yaavat syaat svasya sambandho ahamkaarena duraatmanaa |
taavan na lesha maatraapi mukti vaartaa vilakshanaa || 299 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As long as one keeps any connection with this wicked ego, there can be no talk whatsoever of Liberation, which is unlike anything else.

verses.sanskrit:
अहंकारग्रहान्मुक्तः स्वरूपमुपपद्यते ।
चन्द्रवद्विमलः पूर्णः सदानन्दः स्वयंप्रभः ॥ ३00 ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃkāragrahānmuktaḥ svarūpamupapadyate |
candravadvimalaḥ pūrṇaḥ sadānandaḥ svayaṃprabhaḥ || 300 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahankaar grahaanmuktah svaroopam upapadyate |
chandravat vimalah poornah sadaanandah svayam prabhah || 300 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Released from the grip of egoism, as the moon is released from Rahu, a person attains his true nature and becomes pure, infinite, ever blissful, and self-luminous.

verses.sanskrit:
यो वा पुरे सोऽहमिति प्रतीतो बुद्ध्या प्रकॢप्तस्तमसातिमूढया ।
तस्यैव निःशेषतया विनाशे ब्रह्मात्मभावः प्रतिबन्धशून्यः ॥ ३0१ ॥
verses.roman:
yo vā pure so'hamiti pratīto buddhyā prakḷptastamasātimūḍhayā |
tasyaiva niḥśeṣatayā vināśe brahmātmabhāvaḥ pratibandhaśūnyaḥ || 301 ||
verses.colloquial:
yo vaa pure so aham iti pratiito buddhyaa prakliptah tamasaa atimuu dha yaa |
tasya eva nihsheshatayaa vinaashe brahma aatma bhaavah pratibandha shuunyah || 301 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Buddhi, deeply deluded by Nescience, has produced something that shows up in this body as 'I am such and such'. When that egoism is wholly destroyed, one gains an unobstructed identity with Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
ब्रह्मानन्दनिधिर्महाबलवताहंकारघोराहिना संवेष्ट्यात्मनि रक्ष्यते गुणमायाइश्चण्डेस्त्रिभिर्मस्तकैः ।
विज्ञानाख्यमहासिना श्रुतिमता विच्छिद्य शीर्षत्रयं निर्मूल्याहिमिमं निधिं सुखकरं धीरोऽनुभोक्तुंक्षमः ॥ ३0२ ॥
verses.roman:
brahmānandanidhirmahābalavatāhaṃkāraghorāhinā saṃveṣṭyātmani rakṣyate guṇaMāyāiścaṇḍestribhirmastakaiḥ |
vijñānākhyamahāsinā śrutimatā vicchidya śīrṣatrayaṃ nirmūlyāhimimaṃ nidhiṃ sukhakaraṃ dhīro'nubhoktuṃkṣamaḥ || 302 ||
verses.colloquial:
brahma aananda nidhir mahaa balavataa aham kaara ghora ahinaa samveshty aatmani rakshyate guna maayaish candesh tribhir mastakaihi |
vijnaana aakhya mahaa sinaa shruti mataa vicchidya shiirsha trayam nirmulya ahim imam nidhim sukha karam dhiiro anubhoktum kshamaha || 302 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The mighty, dreadful serpent of egoism has coiled itself around the treasure of the Bliss of Brahman and guards it for its own use with three fierce hoods, the three Guṇas. Only the wise person can enjoy this bliss-giving treasure, by destroying the serpent, cutting off its three hoods with the great sword of realization as the Śrutis teach.

verses.sanskrit:
यावद्वा यत्किंचिद्विषदोषस्फूर्तिरस्ति चेद्देहे ।
कथमारोग्याय भवेत्तद्वदहन्तापि योगिनो मुक्त्यै ॥ ३0३ ॥
verses.roman:
yāvadvā yatkiṃcidviṣadoṣasphūrtirasti ceddehe |
kathamārogyāya bhavettadvadahantāpi yogino muktyai || 303 ||
verses.colloquial:
yaavadvaa yat kim cid visha dosha sphurtir asti ced dehe |
katham aarogyaaya bhavet tadvad ahantaa api yogino muktyai || 303 ||
verses.translation_reworded: How can anyone hope to recover while even a trace of poison remains in the body? Egoism has the same effect on the Yogi's Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
अहमोऽत्यन्तनिवृत्त्या तत्कृतनानाविकल्पसंहृत्या ।
प्रत्यक्तत्त्वविवेकादिदमहमस्मीति विन्दते तत्त्वम् ॥ ३0४ ॥
verses.roman:
ahamo'tyantanivṛttyā tatkṛtanānāvikalpasaṃhṛtyā |
pratyaktattvavivekādidamahamasmīti vindate tattvam || 304 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahamo atyanta nivrittyaa tat krita naanaa vikalpa samhrityaa |
pratyak tattva vivekaad idam aham asmiiti vindate tattvam || 304 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When egoism has ceased entirely, when the many mental waves it produces have been stopped, and when the inner Reality has been discriminated, one realizes that Reality as 'I am This'.

verses.sanskrit:
अहंकारे कर्तर्यहमिति मतिं मुञ्च सहसा विकारात्मन्यात्मप्रतिफलजुषि स्वस्थितिमुषि ।
यदध्यासात्प्राप्ता जनिमृतिजरादुःखबहुला प्रतीचश्चिन्मूर्तेस्तव सुखतनोः संसृतिरियम् ॥ ३0५ ॥
verses.roman:
ahaṃkāre kartaryahamiti matiṃ muñca sahasā vikārātmanyātmapratiphalajuṣi svasthitimuṣi |
yadadhyāsātprāptā janimṛtijarāduḥkhabahulā pratīcaścinmūrtestava sukhatanoḥ saṃsṛtiriyam || 305 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahamkaare kartari aham iti matim muncha sahasaa vikaaraatmani aatma pratiphala jushi sva sthiti mushi |
yad adhyaasaat praaptaa jani mriti jaraa duhkha bahulaa pratiichash chin muurte tava sukha tanoh samsritir iyam || 305 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Drop at once your identification with egoism, the agent. By its nature it is a modification, it carries a reflection of the Self, and it turns one away from being established in the Self. By identifying with it you have fallen into this relative existence, full of the miseries of birth, decay, and death, even though you are the Witness, the Essence of Knowledge and Bliss Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
सदैकरूपस्य चिदात्मनो विभोर् आनन्दमूर्तेरनवद्यकीर्तेः ।
नैवान्यथा क्वाप्यविकारिणस्ते विनाहमध्यासममुष्य संसृतिः ॥ ३0६ ॥
verses.roman:
sadaikarūpasya cidātmano vibhor ānandamūrteranavadyakīrteḥ |
naivānyathā kvāpyavikāriṇaste vināhamadhyāsamamuṣya saṃsṛtiḥ || 306 ||
verses.colloquial:
sadaa eka ruupasya chid aatmano vibhor aananda muurter anavadya kiirteh |
na eva anyathaa kva api avikaarinah te vinaa aham adhyaasam amusya samsritih || 306 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If not for your identification with that egoism, you could never undergo transmigration, for you are unchanging and eternally the same, Knowledge Absolute, present everywhere, Bliss Absolute, and of untarnished glory.

verses.sanskrit:
तस्मादहंकारमिमं स्वशत्रुं भोक्तुर्गले कण्टकवत्प्रतीतम् ।
विच्छिद्य विज्ञानमहासिना स्फुटं भुङ्क्ष्वात्मसाम्राज्यसुखं यथेष्टम् ॥ ३0७ ॥
verses.roman:
tasmādahaṃkāramimaṃ svaśatruṃ bhokturgale kaṇṭakavatpratītam |
vicchidya vijñānamahāsinā sphuṭaṃ bhuṅkṣvātmasāmrājyasukhaṃ yatheṣṭam || 307 ||
verses.colloquial:
tasmaat ahamkaaram imam sva shatrum bhoktur gale kantakavat pratiitam |
vicchidya vijnyaana mahaa asinaa sphutam bhunkshva aatma saamraajya sukham yathaa ishtam || 307 ||
verses.translation_reworded: So destroy this egoism, your enemy, which is like a thorn stuck in the throat of someone eating a meal. Use the great sword of realization, and then enjoy, directly and freely, the bliss of your own empire, the majesty of the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
ततोऽहमादेर्विनिवर्त्य वृत्तिं संत्यक्तरागः परमार्थलाभात् ।
तूष्णीं समास्स्वात्मसुखानुभूत्या पूर्णात्मना ब्रह्मणि निर्विकल्पः ॥ ३0८ ॥
verses.roman:
tato'hamādervinivartya vṛttiṃ saṃtyaktarāgaḥ paramārthalābhāt |
tūṣṇīṃ samāssvātmasukhānubhūtyā pūrṇātmanā brahmaṇi nirvikalpaḥ || 308 ||
verses.colloquial:
tato aham aader vinivartya vrittim samtyakta raagah paramaarthalabhaat |
tuushniim samaassva aatma sukha anubhuutyaa puurna aatmanaa brahmani nirvikalpah || 308 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Restrain the activities of egoism and the like, and let go of all attachment by realizing the Supreme Reality. Through the enjoyment of the Bliss of the Self, be free from all duality, and rest quietly in Brahman, for you have reached your infinite nature.

verses.sanskrit:
समूलकृत्तोऽपि महानहं पुनः व्युल्लेखितः स्याद्यदि चेतसा क्षणम् ।
संजीव्य विक्षेपशतं करोति नभस्वता प्रावृषि वारिदो यथा ॥ ३0९ ॥
verses.roman:
samūlakṛtto'pi mahānahaṃ punaḥ vyullekhitaḥ syādyadi cetasā kṣaṇam |
saṃjīvya vikṣepaśataṃ karoti nabhasvatā prāvṛṣi vārido yathā || 309 ||
verses.colloquial:
samuula kritto api mahaan aham punah vyullekhitah syaat yadi cetasaa kshanam |
samjiivya vikshepa shatam karoti nabhasvataa pravrishi vaarido yathaa || 309 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Even when it has been pulled out by the roots, this terrible egoism, if turned over in the mind for just a moment, springs back to life and causes hundreds of troubles, like a cloud driven in by the wind in the rainy season.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Actions, Thoughts and Vāsanās - Renounce</vt>
निगृह्य शत्रोरहमोऽवकाशः क्वचिन्न देयो विषयानुचिन्तया ।
स एव संजीवनहेतुरस्य प्रक्षीणजम्बीरतरोरिवाम्बु ॥ ३१0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Actions, Thoughts and Vāsanās - Renounce</vt>
nigṛhya śatrorahamo'vakāśaḥ kvacinna deyo viṣayānucintayā |
sa eva saṃjīvanaheturasya prakṣīṇajambīratarorivāmbu || 310 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Actions, Thoughts and Vāsanās - Renounce</vt>
nigrihya shatror ahamo avakaasha kvacin na deyo vishaya anucintayaa |
sa eva samjiivana hetur asya prakshiina jambiira taror iva ambu || 310 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Having overpowered this enemy, egoism, give it not a moment's relief by thinking about sense objects. Such thinking is what revives it, as water revives a citron tree that has nearly dried up.

verses.sanskrit:
देहात्मना संस्थित एव कामी विलक्षणः कामयिता कथं स्यात् ।
अतोऽर्थसन्धानपरत्वमेव भेदप्रसक्त्या भवबन्धहेतुः ॥ ३११ ॥
verses.roman:
dehātmanā saṃsthita eva kāmī vilakṣaṇaḥ kāmayitā kathaṃ syāt |
ato'rthasandhānaparatvameva bhedaprasaktyā bhavabandhahetuḥ || 311 ||
verses.colloquial:
deha aatmanaa samsthita eva kaamii vilakshanah kaamayitaa katham syaat |
ato artha sandhaana paratvam eva bheda prasaktyaa bhava bandha hetuh || 311 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only someone identified with the body is greedy for sense pleasures. How could a person without the body-idea be greedy in that way? So the habit of thinking about sense objects is truly the cause of the bondage of transmigration, since it gives rise to the idea of distinction or duality.

verses.sanskrit:
कार्यप्रवर्धनाद्बीजप्रवृद्धिः परिदृश्यते ।
कार्यनाशाद्बीजनाशस्तस्मात्कार्यं निरोधयेत् ॥ ३१२ ॥
verses.roman:
kāryapravardhanādbījapravṛddhiḥ paridṛśyate |
kāryanāśādbījanāśastasmātkāryaṃ nirodhayet || 312 ||
verses.colloquial:
kaarya pravardhanaad biija pravriddhi paridrishyate |
kaarya naashaad biija naashas tasmaat kaaryam nirodhayet || 312 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the effects develop, the seed is seen to develop as well, and when the effects are destroyed, the seed is seen to be destroyed too. One must therefore subdue the effects.

verses.sanskrit:
वासनावृद्धितः कार्यं कार्यवृद्ध्या च वासना ।
वर्धते सर्वथा पुंसः संसारो न निवर्तते ॥ ३१३ ॥
verses.roman:
vāsanāvṛddhitaḥ kāryaṃ kāryavṛddhyā ca vāsanā |
vardhate sarvathā puṃsaḥ saṃsāro na nivartate || 313 ||
verses.colloquial:
vaasanaa vriddhitah kaaryam kaarya vriddhyaa ca vaasanaa |
vardhate sarvathaa pumsah samsaaro na nivartate || 313 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As desires grow, selfish work grows, and as selfish work grows, desire grows too. And so a person's transmigration never ends.

verses.sanskrit:
संसारबन्धविच्छित्त्यै तद्द्वयं प्रदहेद्यतिः ।
वासनावृद्धिरेताभ्यां चिन्तया क्रियया बहिः ॥ ३१४ ॥
verses.roman:
saṃsārabandhavicchittyai taddvayaṃ pradahedyatiḥ |
vāsanāvṛddhiretābhyāṃ cintayā kriyayā bahiḥ || 314 ||
verses.colloquial:
samsaara bandha vicchittyai tad dvayam pradahed yatih |
vaasanaa vriddhir etaabhyaam cintayaa kriyayaa bahih || 314 ||
verses.translation_reworded: To break the chain of transmigration, the Sannyasin should burn those two to ashes, because thinking about sense objects and performing selfish acts cause desires to increase.

verses.sanskrit:
ताभ्यां प्रवर्धमाना सा सूते संसृतिमात्मनः ।
त्रयाणां च क्षयोपायः सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा ॥ ३१५ ॥
verses.roman:
tābhyāṃ pravardhamānā sā sūte saṃsṛtimātmanaḥ |
trayāṇāṃ ca kṣayopāyaḥ sarvāvasthāsu sarvadā || 315 ||
verses.colloquial:
taabhyaam pravardhamaanaa saa suute samsritim aatmanah |
trayaanaam ca kshaya upaayah sarva avasthasu sarvadaa || 315 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Strengthened by these two, desires produce one's transmigration. But the way to destroy these three is to look on everything, in all circumstances, always, everywhere, and in every respect, as Brahman and Brahman alone. As the longing to be one with Brahman grows stronger, those three are wiped out.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वत्र सर्वतः सर्वब्रह्ममात्रावलोकनैः ।
सद्भाववासनादार्ढ्यात्तत्त्रयं लयमश्नुते ॥ ३१६ ॥
verses.roman:
sarvatra sarvataḥ sarvabrahmamātrāvalokanaiḥ |
sadbhāvavāsanādārḍhyāttattrayaṃ layamaśnute || 316 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarvatra sarvatah sarva brahma maatra avalokanaiih |
sat bhaava vaasanaa daardhyaat tat trayam layam ashnute || 316 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Strengthened by these two, desires produce one's transmigration. But the way to destroy these three is to look on everything, in all circumstances, always, everywhere, and in every respect, as Brahman and Brahman alone. As the longing to be one with Brahman grows stronger, those three are wiped out.

verses.sanskrit:
क्रियानाशे भवेच्चिन्तानाशोऽस्माद्वासनाक्षयः ।
वासनाप्रक्षयो मोक्षः सा जीवन्मुक्तिरिष्यते ॥ ३१७ ॥
verses.roman:
kriyānāśe bhaveccintānāśo'smādvāsanākṣayaḥ |
vāsanāprakṣayo mokṣaḥ sā jīvanmuktiriṣyate || 317 ||
verses.colloquial:
kriyaa naashe bhavet chintaa naasho asmaat vaasanaa kshayah |
vaasanaa prakshayo mokshah saa jiivan muktir ishyate || 317 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When selfish action ceases, brooding on sense objects stops, and the destruction of desires follows. The destruction of desires is Liberation, and it is regarded as Liberation-in-life.

verses.sanskrit:
सद्वासनास्फूर्तिविजृम्भणे सति ह्यसौ विलीनाप्यहमादिवासना ।
अतिप्रकृष्टाप्यरुणप्रभायां विलीयते साधु यथा तमिस्रा ॥ ३१८ ॥
verses.roman:
sadvāsanāsphūrtivijṛmbhaṇe sati hyasau vilīnāpyahamādivāsanā |
atiprakṛṣṭāpyaruṇaprabhāyāṃ vilīyate sādhu yathā tamisrā || 318 ||
verses.colloquial:
sad vaasanaa sphurti vijrimbhane sati hi asau viliinaa api aham aadi vaasanaa |
ati prakrishta api aruna prabhaayaam viliiyate saadhu yathaa tamisraa || 318 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the desire to realize Brahman shows itself strongly, egoistic desires quickly disappear, just as the deepest darkness truly disappears before the glow of the rising sun.

verses.sanskrit:
तमस्तमःकार्यमनर्थजालं न दृश्यते सत्युदिते दिनेशे ।
तथाद्वयानन्दरसानुभूतौ न वास्ति बन्धो न च दुःखगन्धः ॥ ३१९ ॥
verses.roman:
tamastamaḥkāryamanarthajālaṃ na dṛśyate satyudite dineśe |
tathādvayānandarasānubhūtau na vāsti bandho na ca duḥkhagandhaḥ || 319 ||
verses.colloquial:
tamas tamah kaaryam anartha jaalam na drishyate sati udite dineshe |
tathaa advaya aananda rasa anubhutau na vaa asti bandho na ca duhkha gandhah || 319 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the sun rises, darkness and the many evils that come with it are no longer seen. In the same way, on realizing the Bliss Absolute, there is neither bondage nor the slightest trace of misery.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Total Vigilance - Its Price</vt>
दृश्यं प्रतीतं प्रविलापयन्सन् सन्मात्रमानन्दघनं विभावयन् ।
समाहितः सन्बहिरन्तरं वा कालं नयेथाः सति कर्मबन्धे ॥ ३२0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Total Vigilance - Its Price</vt>
dṛśyaṃ pratītaṃ pravilāpayansan sanmātramānandaghanaṃ vibhāvayan |
samāhitaḥ sanbahirantaraṃ vā kālaṃ nayethāḥ sati karmabandhe || 320 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Total Vigilance - Its Price</vt>
drishyam pratiitam pravilaapayan san sat maatram aananda ghanam vibhaavayan |
samaahitah san bahir antaram vaa kaalam nayethaah sati karma bandhe || 320 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Making the outer and inner universe now being perceived disappear, and meditating on the Reality, Bliss Embodied, one should spend one's time watchfully, if any Prārabdha work remains.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रमादो ब्रह्मनिष्ठायां न कर्तव्यः कदाचन ।
प्रमादो मृत्युरित्याह भगवान्ब्रह्मणः सुतः ॥ ३२१ ॥
verses.roman:
pramādo brahmaniṣṭhāyāṃ na kartavyaḥ kadācana |
pramādo mṛtyurityāha bhagavānbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ || 321 ||
verses.colloquial:
pramaado brahma nishthhaayaam na kartavyah kadaachana |
pramaado mrityur iti aaha bhagavaan brahmanah sutah || 321 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One must never be careless in one's steadfastness to Brahman. Bhagavan Sanatkumāra, the son of Brahma, has called inattention death itself.

verses.sanskrit:
न प्रमादादनर्थोऽन्यो ज्ञानिनः स्वस्वरूपतः ।
ततो मोहस्ततोऽहंधीस्ततो बन्धस्ततो व्यथा ॥ ३२२ ॥
verses.roman:
na pramādādanartho'nyo jñāninaḥ svasvarūpataḥ |
tato mohastato'haṃdhīstato bandhastato vyathā || 322 ||
verses.colloquial:
na pramaadaad anartho anyo jnaaninaah sva svaruupatah |
tato mohas tato aham dhiis tato bandhas tato vyathaa || 322 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For the Jñānin there is no greater danger than carelessness about his own real nature. From it comes delusion, from delusion egoism, after that bondage, and then misery.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयाभिमुखं दृष्ट्वा विद्वांसमपि विस्मृतिः ।
विक्षेपयति धीदोषैर्योषा जारमिव प्रियम् ॥ ३२३ ॥
verses.roman:
viṣayābhimukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidvāṃsamapi vismṛtiḥ |
vikṣepayati dhīdoṣairyoṣā jāramiva priyam || 323 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishaya abhimukham drishtvaa vidvaamsam api vismritih |
vikshepayati dhii doshair yoshaa jaaram iva priyam || 323 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When it finds even a wise man hankering after sense objects, forgetfulness torments him through the evil tendencies of the Buddhi, as a woman torments her doting lover.

verses.sanskrit:
यथापकृष्टं शैवालं क्षणमात्रं न तिष्ठति ।
आवृणोति तथा माया प्राज्ञं वापि पराङ्मुखम् ॥ ३२४ ॥
verses.roman:
yathāpakṛṣṭaṃ śaivālaṃ kṣaṇamātraṃ na tiṣṭhati |
āvṛṇoti tathā māyā prājñaṃ vāpi parāṅmukham || 324 ||
verses.colloquial:
yathaa apakristam shaivaalam kshana maatram na tishthati |
aavrinoti tathaa maayaa praajnam vaapi paraang mukham || 324 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Moss, even when cleared away, does not stay away for a moment but spreads over the water again. In the same way, Māyā or Nescience covers even a wise man if he turns away from meditation on the Self.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्यच्युतं चेद्यदि चित्तमीषद् बहिर्मुखं सन्निपतेत्ततस्ततः ।
प्रमादतः प्रच्युतकेलिकन्दुकः सोपानपङ्क्तौ पतितो यथा तथा ॥ ३२५ ॥
verses.roman:
lakṣyacyutaṃ cedyadi cittamīṣad bahirmukhaṃ sannipatettatastataḥ |
pramādataḥ pracyutakelikandukaḥ sopānapaṅktau patito yathā tathā || 325 ||
verses.colloquial:
lakshya cyutam ced yadi cittam iishad bahir mukham sannipatet tatas tatah |
pramaadatah pracyuta keli kandukah sopaana panktau patito yathaa tathaa || 325 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If the mind strays even slightly from the Ideal and turns outward, it keeps sinking lower and lower, like a play-ball accidentally dropped on a staircase, bouncing down from one step to the next.

verses.sanskrit:
विषयेष्वाविशच्चेतः संकल्पयति तद्गुणान् ।
सम्यक्संकल्पनात्कामः कामात्पुंसः प्रवर्तनम् ॥ ३२६ ॥
verses.roman:
viṣayeṣvāviśaccetaḥ saṃkalpayati tadguṇān |
samyaksaṃkalpanātkāmaḥ kāmātpuṃsaḥ pravartanam || 326 ||
verses.colloquial:
vishayeshv aavishac cetah samkalpayati tad gunaan |
samyak samkalpanaat kaamah kaamaat pumsah pravartanam || 326 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A mind attached to sense objects dwells on their qualities. From sustained dwelling comes desire, and once he desires a thing, a man sets about getting it.

verses.sanskrit:
अतः प्रमादान्न परोऽस्ति मृत्युः विवेकिनो ब्रह्मविदः समाधौ ।
समाहितः सिद्धिमुपैति सम्यक् समाहितात्मा भव सावधानः ॥ ३२७ ॥
verses.roman:
ataḥ pramādānna paro'sti mṛtyuḥ vivekino brahmavidaḥ samādhau |
samāhitaḥ siddhimupaiti samyak samāhitātmā bhava sāvadhānaḥ || 327 ||
verses.colloquial:
atah pramaadaan na paro asti mrityuh vivekino brahmavida samadhau |
samaahitah siddhim upaiti samyak samaahita aatmaa bhava saavadhaanah || 327 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For the discriminating knower of Brahman, then, there is no worse death than inattention in concentration. But the concentrated person gains complete success. (Therefore) carefully concentrate your mind (on Brahman).

verses.sanskrit:
ततः स्वरूपविभ्रंशो विभ्रष्टस्तु पतत्यधः ।
पतितस्य विना नाशं पुनर्नारोह ईक्ष्यते ॥ ३२८ ॥
verses.roman:
tataḥ svarūpavibhraṃśo vibhraṣṭastu patatyadhaḥ |
patitasya vinā nāśaṃ punarnāroha īkṣyate || 328 ||
verses.colloquial:
tatah svaruupa vibhramsho vibhrashtah tu patati adhah |
patitasya vinaa naasham punar na aaroha iikshyate || 328 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through inattention a person strays from his real nature, and one who has strayed falls. The fallen person is ruined and is hardly ever seen to rise again.

verses.sanskrit:
संकल्पं वर्जयेत्तस्मात्सर्वानर्थस्य कारणम् ।
जीवतो यस्य कैवल्यं विदेहे स च केवलः यत्किंचित्पश्यतो भेदं भयं ब्रूते यजुःश्रुतिः ॥ ३२९ ॥
verses.roman:
saṃkalpaṃ varjayettasmātsarvānarthasya kāraṇam |
jīvato yasya kaivalyaṃ videhe sa ca kevalaḥ yatkiṃcitpaśyato bhedaṃ bhayaṃ brūte yajuḥśrutiḥ || 329 ||
verses.colloquial:
samkalpam varjayet tasmaat sarva anartha kaaranam |
jiivato yasya kaivalyam videhe sa ca kevalah yat kimchit pashyato bhedam bhayam bruute yajuh shrutih || 329 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One should therefore give up dwelling on sense objects, the root of all trouble. Only someone who is completely detached while living remains detached after the body dissolves. The Yajur-Veda declares that there is fear for anyone who sees even the smallest distinction.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>In the One, No Plurality</vt>
यदा कदा वापि विपश्चिदेष ब्रह्मण्यनन्तेऽप्यणुमात्रभेदम् ।
पश्यत्यथामुष्य भयं तदैव यद्वीक्षितं भिन्नतया प्रमादात् ॥ ३३0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>In the One, No Plurality</vt>
yadā kadā vāpi vipaścideṣa brahmaṇyanante'pyaṇumātrabhedam |
paśyatyathāmuṣya bhayaṃ tadaiva yadvīkṣitaṃ bhinnatayā pramādāt || 330 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>In the One, No Plurality</vt>
yadaa kadaa vaapi vipashchid esha brahmani anante api anu maatra bhedam |
pashyati atha amusya bhayam tad eva yad viikshitam bhinna tayaa pramaadaat || 330 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whenever the wise man sees even the slightest difference in the infinite Brahman, what he has mistakenly seen as different immediately becomes a source of terror for him.

verses.sanskrit:
श्रुतिस्मृतिन्यायशतैर्निषिद्धे दृश्येऽत्र यः स्वात्ममतिं करोति ।
उपैति दुःखोपरि दुःखजातं निषिद्धकर्ता स मलिम्लुचो यथा ॥ ३३१ ॥
verses.roman:
śrutismṛtinyāyaśatairniṣiddhe dṛśye'tra yaḥ svātmamatiṃ karoti |
upaiti duḥkhopari duḥkhajātaṃ niṣiddhakartā sa malimluco yathā || 331 ||
verses.colloquial:
shruti smriti nyaaya shatair nishiddhe drishye atra yah sva aatma matim karoti |
upaiti duhkha upari duhkha jaatam nishiddha kartaa sa malimlucho yathaa || 331 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whoever identifies with the objective universe, which hundreds of Shrutis, Smritis, and reasonings have denied, suffers one misery after another, like a thief, because he is doing what is forbidden.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्याभिसंधानरतो विमुक्तो महत्त्वमात्मीयमुपैति नित्यम् ।
मिथ्याभिसन्धानरतस्तु नश्येद् दृष्टं तदेतद्यदचौरचौरयोः ॥ ३३२ ॥
verses.roman:
satyābhisaṃdhānarato vimukto mahattvamātmīyamupaiti nityam |
mithyābhisandhānaratastu naśyed dṛṣṭaṃ tadetadyadacauracaurayoḥ || 332 ||
verses.colloquial:
satya abhisandhaana rato vimukto mahattvam aatmiiyam upaiti nityam |
mithya abhisandhaana ratastu nashyed drishtam tad etad yad a caura caurayoh || 332 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The person devoted to meditation on the Reality (Brahman) and free from Nescience reaches the eternal glory of the Ātman. But one who dwells on the unreal (the universe) is destroyed. This is shown by the case of someone who is not a thief and someone who is.

verses.sanskrit:
यतिरसदनुसन्धिं बन्धहेतुं विहाय स्वयमायामहमस्मीत्यात्मदृष्ट्यैव तिष्ठेत् ।
सुखयति ननु निष्ठा ब्रह्मणि स्वानुभूत्या हरति परमविद्याकार्यदुःखं प्रतीतम् ॥ ३३३ ॥
verses.roman:
yatirasadanusandhiṃ bandhahetuṃ vihāya svayaMāyāmahamasmītyātmadṛṣṭyaiva tiṣṭhet |
sukhayati nanu niṣṭhā brahmaṇi svānubhūtyā harati paramavidyākāryaduḥkhaṃ pratītam || 333 ||
verses.colloquial:
yatir asad anusandhim bandha hetum vihaaya svayam aham asmi iti aatma drishtya eva tishthet |
sukhayati nanu nishthaa brahmani sva anubhuutyaa harati parama vidyaa kaarya duhkham pratiitam || 333 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Sannyasin should stop dwelling on the unreal, which causes bondage, and should always keep his thoughts on the Ātman as 'I myself am This'. For steadfastness in Brahman, through realizing one's identity with It, gives rise to bliss and completely removes the misery born of nescience that one experiences (in the ignorant state).

verses.sanskrit:
बाह्यानुसन्धिः परिवर्धयेत्फलं दुर्वासनामेव ततस्ततोऽधिकाम् ।
ज्ञात्वा विवेकैः परिहृत्य बाह्यं स्वात्मानुसन्धिं विदधीत नित्यम् ॥ ३३४ ॥
verses.roman:
bāhyānusandhiḥ parivardhayetphalaṃ durvāsanāmeva tatastato'dhikām |
jñātvā vivekaiḥ parihṛtya bāhyaṃ svātmānusandhiṃ vidadhīta nityam || 334 ||
verses.colloquial:
baahya anusandhih parivardhayetphalam durvaasanaam eva tatastato adhikaam |
jnaatvaa vivekaihi parihritya baahyam svaatma anusandhim vidadhiita nityam || 334 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Dwelling on outer objects will only intensify its fruits, namely the growth of evil tendencies, which get worse and worse. Knowing this through discrimination, one should avoid outer objects and devote oneself constantly to meditation on the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
बाह्ये निरुद्धे मनसः प्रसन्नता मनःप्रसादे परमात्मदर्शनम् ।
तस्मिन्सुदृष्टे भवबन्धनाशो बहिर्निरोधः पदवी विमुक्तेः ॥ ३३५ ॥
verses.roman:
bāhye niruddhe manasaḥ prasannatā manaḥprasāde paramātmadarśanam |
tasminsudṛṣṭe bhavabandhanāśo bahirnirodhaḥ padavī vimukteḥ || 335 ||
verses.colloquial:
baahye niruddhe manasah prasannataa manah prasaade paramaatma darshanam |
tasmin sudrishte bhava bandha naasho bahir nirodhah padavii mukteh || 335 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the external world is shut out, the mind is cheerful, and a cheerful mind brings the vision of the Paramātman. When It is perfectly realized, the chain of birth and death is broken. Shutting out the external world is therefore the stepping-stone to Liberation.

verses.sanskrit:
कः पण्डितः सन्सदसद्विवेकी श्रुतिप्रमाणः परमार्थदर्शी ।
जानन्हि कुर्यादसतोऽवलम्बं स्वपातहेतोः शिशुवन्मुमुक्षुः ॥ ३३६ ॥
verses.roman:
kaḥ paṇḍitaḥ sansadasadvivekī śrutipramāṇaḥ paramārthadarśī |
jānanhi kuryādasato'valambaṃ svapātahetoḥ śiśuvanmumukṣuḥ || 336 ||
verses.colloquial:
kah panditah san sad asat vivekii shruti pramaanah parama artha darshii |
jaanan hi kuryaat asato avalambam sva paata hetoh shishu vat mumukshuh || 336 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Where is the person who is learned, able to tell the real from the unreal, who accepts the Vedas as authority, whose gaze is fixed on the Ātman, the Supreme Reality, and who seeks Liberation, yet who would knowingly, like a child, turn to the unreal (the universe) that will bring about his fall?

verses.sanskrit:
देहादिसंसक्तिमतो न मुक्तिः मुक्तस्य देहाद्यभिमत्यभावः ।
