adatvā svaphalaṃ lakṣyamuddiśyotsṛṣṭabāṇavat || 451 ||
verses.colloquial:
jnaana udayaat puraa aarabdham karma jnaanaan na nashyati |
adatvaa sva phalam lakshyam uddishya utsrishta baana vat || 451 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The work that shaped this body before knowledge dawned is not destroyed by that knowledge until it has yielded its fruits, like an arrow already shot at a target.

verses.sanskrit:
व्याघ्रबुद्ध्या विनिर्मुक्तो बाणः पश्चात्तु गोमतौ ।
न तिष्ठति छिनत्येव लक्ष्यं वेगेन निर्भरम् ॥ ४५२ ॥
verses.roman:
vyāghrabuddhyā vinirmukto bāṇaḥ paścāttu gomatau |
na tiṣṭhati chinatyeva lakṣyaṃ vegena nirbharam || 452 ||
verses.colloquial:
vyaaghra buddhyaa vinirmukto baanah pashchaattu gomatau |
na tishthati chinatyeva lakshyam vegena nirbharam || 452 ||
verses.translation_reworded: An arrow shot at something taken to be a tiger does not stop itself when the target turns out to be a cow; it pierces the target with full force.

verses.sanskrit:
प्राब्धं बलवत्तरं खलु विदां भोगेन तस्य क्षयः सम्यग्ज्ञानहुताशनेन विलयः प्राक्षंचितागामिनाम् ।
ब्रह्मात्मैक्यमवेक्ष्य तन्मायातया ये सर्वदा संस्थिताः तेषां तत्त्रितयं नहि क्वचिदपि ब्रह्मैव ते निर्गुणम् ॥ ४५३ ॥
verses.roman:
prābdhaṃ balavattaraṃ khalu vidāṃ bhogena tasya kṣayaḥ samyagjñānahutāśanena vilayaḥ prākṣaṃcitāgāminām |
brahmātmaikyamavekṣya tanMāyātayā ye sarvadā saṃsthitāḥ teṣāṃ tattritayaṃ nahi kvacidapi brahmaiva te nirguṇam || 453 ||
verses.colloquial:
praabdham balavattaram khalu vidaam bhogena tasya kshayah samyag jnaana huta ashanena vilayah praak sanchita aagaaminaam |
brahma aatma aikyam avekshya tat maayaatayaa ye sarvadaa samsthitaah teshaam tat tritayam nahi kvachid api brahma eva te nirgunam || 453 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For the person of realization, Prārabdha work is certainly very strong and is used up only by actually experiencing its fruit, while previously accumulated actions and those yet to come are destroyed by the fire of perfect knowledge. Yet none of the three affects in any way those who have realized their identity with Brahman and live always absorbed in that idea. They are truly the transcendent Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
उपाधितादात्म्यविहीनकेवल ब्रह्मात्मनैवात्मनि तिष्ठतो मुनेः ।
प्रारब्धसद्भावकथा न युक्ता स्वप्नार्थसंबन्धकथेव जाग्रतः ॥ ४५४ ॥
verses.roman:
upādhitādātmyavihīnakevala brahmātmanaivātmani tiṣṭhato muneḥ |
prārabdhasadbhāvakathā na yuktā svapnārthasaṃbandhakatheva jāgrataḥ || 454 ||
verses.colloquial:
upaadhi taadaatmya vihiina kevala brahma aatmanaa eva aatmani tishthato muneh |
praarabdha sadbhaava kathaa na yuktaa svapna artha sambandha kathaa iva jaagratah || 454 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For the sage who lives in his own Self as Brahman, the One without a second, and who does not identify with the limiting adjuncts, asking whether Prārabdha work exists makes no sense. It would be like asking whether someone awake from sleep has any connection with the objects seen in a dream.

verses.sanskrit:
न हि प्रबुद्धः प्रतिभासदेहे देहोपयोगिन्यपि च प्रपञ्चे ।
करोत्यहन्तां ममतानिदन्तां किन्तु स्वयं तिष्ठति जागरेण ॥ ४५५ ॥
verses.roman:
na hi prabuddhaḥ pratibhāsadehe dehopayoginyapi ca prapañce |
karotyahantāṃ mamatānidantāṃ kintu svayaṃ tiṣṭhati jāgareṇa || 455 ||
verses.colloquial:
na hi prabuddha pratibhaasa dehe deha upayoginy api ca prapanche |
karoty ahantaam mamataa nidantaam kintu svayam tishthati jaagarena || 455 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Someone awake from sleep never thinks "I" or "mine" about his dream-body and the dream-objects that served that body. He lives fully awake, as his own Self.

verses.sanskrit:
न तस्य मिथ्यार्थसमर्थनेच्छा न संग्रहस्तज्जगतोऽपि दृष्टः ।
तत्रानुवृत्तिर्यदि चेन्मृषार्थे न निद्रया मुक्त इतीष्यते ध्रुवम् ॥ ४५६ ॥
verses.roman:
na tasya mithyārthasamarthanecchā na saṃgrahastajjagato'pi dṛṣṭaḥ |
tatrānuvṛttiryadi cenmṛṣārthe na nidrayā mukta itīṣyate dhruvam || 456 ||
verses.colloquial:
na tasya mithyaa artha samarthane icchaa na samgrahah tat jagato api drishtah |
tatra anuvrittih yadi cet mrishaa arthe na nidrayaa mukta iti ishyate dhruvam || 456 ||
verses.translation_reworded: He has no wish to make the unreal objects real, and he is not seen keeping up that dream-world. If he still clings to those unreal objects, it is stated firmly that he has not yet left sleep behind.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वत्परे ब्रह्मणि वर्तमानः सदात्मना तिष्ठति नान्यदीक्षते ।
स्मृतिर्यथा स्वप्नविलोकितार्थे तथा विदः प्राशनमोचनादौ ॥ ४५७ ॥
verses.roman:
tadvatpare brahmaṇi vartamānaḥ sadātmanā tiṣṭhati nānyadīkṣate |
smṛtiryathā svapnavilokitārthe tathā vidaḥ prāśanamocanādau || 457 ||
verses.colloquial:
tadvat pare brahmani vartamaanah sadaatmanaa tishthati na anyad iikshate |
smritir yathaa svapna vilokita arthe tathaa vidah praashana mochana aadau || 457 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, one absorbed in Brahman lives identified with that eternal Reality and sees nothing else. Just as one remembers things seen in a dream, the person of realization has a memory of everyday actions such as eating.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्मणा निर्मितो देहः प्रारब्धं तस्य कल्प्यताम् ।
नानादेरात्मनो युक्तं नैवात्मा कर्मनिर्मितः ॥ ४५८ ॥
verses.roman:
karmaṇā nirmito dehaḥ prārabdhaṃ tasya kalpyatām |
nānāderātmano yuktaṃ naivātmā karmanirmitaḥ || 458 ||
verses.colloquial:
karmanaa nirmito dehah praarabdham tasya kalpyataam |
naa naader aatmano yuktam naiva aatmaa karma nirmitah || 458 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Karma has shaped the body, so one may imagine Prarabdha work in relation to it. But attributing the same to the Ātman is unreasonable, since the Ātman is never the product of work.

verses.sanskrit:
अजो नित्यः शाश्वत इति ब्रूते श्रुतिरमोघवाक् ।
तदात्मना तिष्ठतोऽस्य कुतः प्रारब्धकल्पना ॥ ४५९ ॥
verses.roman:
ajo nityaḥ śāśvata iti brūte śrutiramoghavāk |
tadātmanā tiṣṭhato'sya kutaḥ prārabdhakalpanā || 459 ||
verses.colloquial:
ajo nityah shaashvata iti bruute shrutir amogha vaak |
tad aatmanaa tishthato asya kutah praarabdha kalpanaa || 459 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Śrutis, whose words cannot err, declare the Ātman to be "birthless, eternal and undecaying." So how can Prārabdha work be attributed to the person who lives identified with That?

verses.sanskrit:
प्रारब्धं सिध्यति तदा यदा देहात्मना स्थितिः ।
देहात्मभावो नैवेष्टः प्रारब्धं त्यज्यतामतः ॥ ४६0 ॥
verses.roman:
prārabdhaṃ sidhyati tadā yadā dehātmanā sthitiḥ |
dehātmabhāvo naiveṣṭaḥ prārabdhaṃ tyajyatāmataḥ || 460 ||
verses.colloquial:
praarabdham sidhyati tadaa yadaa deha aatmanaa sthitih |
deha aatma bhaavo na eva ishtah praarabdham tyajyataam atah || 460 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Prārabdha work can be upheld only so long as a person lives identified with the body. But no one claims that the person of realization ever identifies with the body. So Prārabdha work should be rejected in his case.

verses.sanskrit:
शरीरस्यापि प्रारब्धकल्पना भ्रान्तिरेव हि ।
अध्यस्तस्य कुतः सत्त्वमसत्यस्य कुतो जनिः अजातस्य कुतो नाशः प्रारब्धमसतः कुतः ॥ ४६१ ॥
verses.roman:
śarīrasyāpi prārabdhakalpanā bhrāntireva hi |
adhyastasya kutaḥ sattvamasatyasya kuto janiḥ ajātasya kuto nāśaḥ prārabdhamasataḥ kutaḥ || 461 ||
verses.colloquial:
shariirasya api praarabdha kalpanaa bhraantir eva hi |
adhyastasya kutah sattvam asatyasya kuto janih ajaatasya kuto naashah praarabdham asatah kutah || 461 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Attributing Prārabdha work even to the body is certainly a mistake. How can something superimposed on another have any existence, and how can what is unreal be born? And how can what was never born die? So how can Prārabdha work exist for something unreal?

verses.sanskrit:
ज्ञानेनाज्ञानकार्यस्य समूलस्य लयो यदि ।
तिष्ठत्ययं कथं देह इति शङ्कावतो जडान् ॥ ४६२ ॥
verses.roman:
jñānenājñānakāryasya samūlasya layo yadi |
tiṣṭhatyayaṃ kathaṃ deha iti śaṅkāvato jaḍān || 462 ||
verses.colloquial:
jnyanenajnyanakaryasya samulasya layo yadi .
tishthatyayam katham deha iti shankavato jadan || 462 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Some fools raise this doubt: "If knowledge destroys the effects of ignorance along with their root, how does the body go on living?" It is to convince them that the Śrutis, from a relative standpoint, posit Prārabdha work, and not to prove that the body and so on of the person of realization are real.

verses.sanskrit:
समाधातुं बाह्यदृष्ट्या प्रारब्धं वदति श्रुतिः ।
न तु देहादिसत्यत्वबोधनाय विपश्चिताम् ॥ ४६३ ॥
verses.roman:
samādhātuṃ bāhyadṛṣṭyā prārabdhaṃ vadati śrutiḥ |
na tu dehādisatyatvabodhanāya vipaścitām || 463 ||
verses.colloquial:
samadhatum bahyadrishtya prarabdham vadati shrutih .
na tu dehadisatyatvabodhanaya vipashchitam || 463 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Some fools raise this doubt: "If knowledge destroys the effects of ignorance along with their root, how does the body go on living?" It is to convince them that the Śrutis, from a relative standpoint, posit Prārabdha work, and not to prove that the body and so on of the person of realization are real.

verses.sanskrit:
परिपूर्णमनाद्यन्तमप्रमेयमविक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६४ ॥
verses.roman:
paripūrṇamanādyantamaprameyamavikriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 464 ||
verses.colloquial:
paripuurnam anaadi antam aprameyam avikriyam |
ekam eva advayam brahma neha naanaa asti kimcana || 464 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: infinite, without beginning or end, transcendent and changeless. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>There is No Plurality</vt>
सद्गनं चिद्घनं नित्यमानन्दघनमक्रियम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६५ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>There is No Plurality</vt>
sadganaṃ cidghanaṃ nityamānandaghanamakriyam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 465 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>There is No Plurality</vt>
sad ghanam chid ghanam nityam aananda ghanam akriyam |
ekam eva advayam brahma neha naanaa asti kimchana || 465 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: the Essence of Existence, Knowledge and Eternal Bliss, and free of activity. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रत्यगेकरसं पूर्णमनन्तं सर्वतोमुखम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६६ ॥
verses.roman:
pratyagekarasaṃ pūrṇamanantaṃ sarvatomukham |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 466 ||
verses.colloquial:
pratyag eka rasam puurnam anantam sarvato mukham |
ekam eva advayam brahma na iha naanaa asti kimcana || 466 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: present within everything, homogeneous, infinite, endless and all-pervading. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
अहेयमनुपादेयमनादेयमनाश्रयम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६७ ॥
verses.roman:
aheyamanupādeyamanādeyamanāśrayam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 467 ||
verses.colloquial:
aheyam anupadeiyam anadeiyam anaashrayam |
ekam eva advayam brahma neha naanaa asti kimchana || 467 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: It cannot be shunned, taken up or accepted, and It rests on no support. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्गुणं निष्कलं सूक्ष्मं निर्विकल्पं निरञ्जनम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६८ ॥
verses.roman:
nirguṇaṃ niṣkalaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nirvikalpaṃ nirañjanam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 468 ||
verses.colloquial:
nirgunam nishkalam suukshmam nirvikalpam niranjanam |
ekam eva advayam brahma neha naanaa asti kimcana || 468 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: beyond attributes, without parts, subtle, absolute and stainless. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
अनिरूप्य स्वरूपं यन्मनोवाचामगोचरम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४६९ ॥
verses.roman:
anirūpya svarūpaṃ yanmanovācāmagocaram |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 469 ||
verses.colloquial:
aniruupya svaruupam yat mano vaachaam agocharam |
ekam eva advayam brahma neha naanaa asti kimchana || 469 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: Its real nature cannot be comprehended, and It lies beyond the reach of mind and speech. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
सत्समृद्धं स्वतःसिद्धं शुद्धं बुद्धमनीदृशम् ।
एकमेवाद्वयं ब्रह्म नेह नानास्ति किंचन ॥ ४७0 ॥
verses.roman:
satsamṛddhaṃ svataḥsiddhaṃ śuddhaṃ buddhamanīdṛśam |
ekamevādvayaṃ brahma neha nānāsti kiṃcana || 470 ||
verses.colloquial:
sat samriddham svatah siddham shuddham buddham aniidrisham |
ekam eva advayam brahma neha naanaa asti kimcana || 470 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Only Brahman exists, the One without a second: the Reality, radiant, self-existent, pure, intelligent and unlike anything finite. In It there is no duality of any kind.

verses.sanskrit:
निरस्तरागा विनिरस्तभोगाः शान्ताः सुदान्ता यतयो महान्तः ।
विज्ञाय तत्त्वं परमेतदन्ते प्राप्ताः परां निर्वृतिमात्मयोगात् ॥ ४७१ ॥
verses.roman:
nirastarāgā vinirastabhogāḥ śāntāḥ sudāntā yatayo mahāntaḥ |
vijñāya tattvaṃ parametadante prāptāḥ parāṃ nirvṛtimātmayogāt || 471 ||
verses.colloquial:
nirasta raagaa vinirasta bhogaah shaantaah sudaantaa yatayo mahaantah |
vijnaaya tattvam param etat ante praaptaah paraam nirvritim aatma yogaat || 471 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Great-souled Sannyasins who have shed all attachment and cast aside all sense-enjoyments, and who are serene and perfectly restrained, realize this Supreme Truth, and in the end reach the Supreme Bliss through their Self-realization.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Experience of Selfhood</vt>
भवानपीदं परतत्त्वमात्मनः स्वरूपमानन्दघनं विचार्य ।
विधूय मोहं स्वमनःप्रकल्पितं मुक्तः कृतार्थो भवतु प्रबुद्धः ॥ ४७२ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Experience of Selfhood</vt>
bhavānapīdaṃ paratattvamātmanaḥ svarūpamānandaghanaṃ vicārya |
vidhūya mohaṃ svamanaḥprakalpitaṃ muktaḥ kṛtārtho bhavatu prabuddhaḥ || 472 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Experience of Selfhood</vt>
bhavaan api idam para tattvam aatmanah svaruupam aananda ghanam vichaarya |
vidhuuya moham sva manah prakalpitam muktah kritaartho bhavatu prabuddhah || 472 ||
verses.translation_reworded: You too must discern this Supreme Truth, the real nature of the Self, which is undiluted Bliss. Shake off the delusion your own mind has created, be free and illumined, and reach the fulfillment of your life.

verses.sanskrit:
समाधिना साधुविनिश्चलात्मना पश्यात्मतत्त्वं स्फुटबोधचक्षुषा ।
निःसंशयं सम्यगवेक्षितश्चेच् छ्रुतः पदार्थो न पुनर्विकल्प्यते ॥ ४७३ ॥
verses.roman:
samādhinā sādhuviniścalātmanā paśyātmatattvaṃ sphuṭabodhacakṣuṣā |
niḥsaṃśayaṃ samyagavekṣitaścec chrutaḥ padārtho na punarvikalpyate || 473 ||
verses.colloquial:
samaadhinaa saadhu vinishcala aatmanaa pashya aatma tattvam sphuta bodha cakshushaa |
nihsamshayam samyag avekshitah cet shrutah padaartho na punar vikalpyate || 473 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through the Samadhi in which the mind has been perfectly stilled, behold the Truth of the Self with the eye of clear realization. If the meaning of the Scriptural words heard from the Guru is discerned perfectly and without question, no further doubt can arise from it.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वस्याविद्याबन्धसंबन्धमोक्षात् सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपात्मलब्धौ ।
शास्त्रं युक्तिर्देशिकोक्तिः प्रमाणं चान्तःसिद्धा स्वानुभूतिः प्रमाणम् ॥ ४७४ ॥
verses.roman:
svasyāvidyābandhasaṃbandhamokṣāt satyajñānānandarūpātmalabdhau |
śāstraṃ yuktirdeśikoktiḥ pramāṇaṃ cāntaḥsiddhā svānubhūtiḥ pramāṇam || 474 ||
verses.colloquial:
svasya avidyaa bandha sambandha mokshaat satya jnaana aananda ruupa aatma labdhau |
shaastram yuktir deshika uktih pramaanam cha antah siddhaa sva anubhuutih pramaanam || 474 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In realizing the Ātman, the Existence-Knowledge-Bliss Absolute, by breaking one's connection with the bondage of Avidya (ignorance), the Scriptures, reasoning and the Guru's words serve as proofs, and one's own experience, gained by concentrating the mind, is a further proof.

verses.sanskrit:
बन्धो मोक्षश्च तृप्तिश्च चिन्तारोग्यक्षुदादयः ।
स्वेनैव वेद्या यज्ज्ञानं परेषामानुमानिकम् ॥ ४७५ ॥
verses.roman:
bandho mokṣaśca tṛptiśca cintārogyakṣudādayaḥ |
svenaiva vedyā yajjñānaṃ pareṣāmānumānikam || 475 ||
verses.colloquial:
bandho mokshas cha triptis cha chintaa rogya kshud aadayah |
svena eva vedyaa yat jnaanam pareshaam aanumanikam || 475 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Bondage, liberation, contentment, anxiety, recovery from illness, hunger and similar things are known only to the person concerned. What others know of them is mere inference.

verses.sanskrit:
तटस्थिता बोधयन्ति गुरवः श्रुतयो यथा ।
प्रज्ञयैव तरेद्विद्वानीश्वरानुगृहीतया ॥ ४७६ ॥
verses.roman:
taṭasthitā bodhayanti guravaḥ śrutayo yathā |
prajñayaiva taredvidvānīśvarānugṛhītayā || 476 ||
verses.colloquial:
tat sthitaa bodhayanti guravah shrutayo yathaa |
prajnayaa eva taret vidvaan iishvara anugriihitayaa || 476 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Gurus and the Śrutis alike instruct the disciple while standing apart. The person of realization crosses over Avidya through Illumination alone, supported by the grace of God.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वानुभूत्या स्वयं ज्ञात्वा स्वमात्मानमखण्डितम् ।
संसिद्धः संमुखं तिष्ठेन्निर्विकल्पात्मनात्मनि ॥ ४७७ ॥
verses.roman:
svānubhūtyā svayaṃ jñātvā svamātmānamakhaṇḍitam |
saṃsiddhaḥ saṃmukhaṃ tiṣṭhennirvikalpātmanātmani || 477 ||
verses.colloquial:
sva anubhuutyaa svayam jnaatvaa svam aatmaanam akhanditam |
samsiddha sammukham tishthennir vikalpa aatmanaa aatmani || 477 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Knowing his indivisible Self through his own realization and so becoming perfect, a person should stand face to face with the Ātman, his mind free from dualistic ideas.

verses.sanskrit:
वेदान्तसिद्धान्तनिरुक्तिरेषा ब्रह्मैव जीवः सकलं जगच्च ।
अखण्डरूपस्थितिरेव मोक्षो ब्रह्माद्वितीये श्रुतयः प्रमाणम् ॥ ४७८ ॥
verses.roman:
vedāntasiddhāntaniruktireṣā brahmaiva jīvaḥ sakalaṃ jagacca |
akhaṇḍarūpasthitireva mokṣo brahmādvitīye śrutayaḥ pramāṇam || 478 ||
verses.colloquial:
vedaanta siddhaanta nirukti resha brahma eva jiivah sakalam jagat cha |
akhanda ruupa sthiti reva moksho brahma advitiye shrutayah pramaanam || 478 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The conclusion of all Vedanta discussions is that the Jīva and the entire universe are nothing but Brahman, and that liberation means abiding in Brahman, the indivisible Entity. The Śrutis themselves are the authority for the statement that Brahman is One without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
इति गुरुवचनाच्छ्रुतिप्रमाणात् परमवगम्य सतत्त्वमात्मयुक्त्या ।
प्रशमितकरणः समाहितात्मा क्वचिदचलाकृतिरात्मनिष्ठतोऽभूत् ॥ ४७९ ॥
verses.roman:
iti guruvacanācchrutipramāṇāt paramavagamya satattvamātmayuktyā |
praśamitakaraṇaḥ samāhitātmā kvacidacalākṛtirātmaniṣṭhato'bhūt || 479 ||
verses.colloquial:
iti guru vachanaat shruti pramaanaat param avagamya sa tattvam aatma yuktyaa |
prashamita karanah samaahita aatmaa kvachid achala aakritir aatma nishthato abhut || 479 ||
verses.translation_reworded: At a blessed moment, through the Guru's teachings above, the authority of the Scriptures and his own reasoning, the disciple realized the Supreme Truth. With his senses quieted and his mind concentrated, he became motionless in form and perfectly established in the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Practice of Knowledge - Disciple</vt>
किंचित्कालं समाधाय परे ब्रह्मणि मानसम् ।
उत्थाय परमानन्दादिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ ४८0 ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Practice of Knowledge - Disciple</vt>
kiṃcitkālaṃ samādhāya pare brahmaṇi mānasam |
utthāya paramānandādidaṃ vacanamabravīt || 480 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Practice of Knowledge - Disciple</vt>
kimchit kaalam samaadhaya pare brahmani maanasam |
utthaaya paramaanandaat idam vachanam abraviit || 480 ||
verses.translation_reworded: After concentrating his mind for a while on the Supreme Brahman, he rose and, out of supreme bliss, spoke these words.

verses.sanskrit:
बुद्धिर्विनष्टा गलिता प्रवृत्तिः ब्रह्मात्मनोरेकतयाधिगत्या ।
इदं न जानेऽप्यनिदं न जाने किं वा कियद्वा सुखमस्त्यपारम् ॥ ४८१ ॥
verses.roman:
buddhirvinaṣṭā galitā pravṛttiḥ brahmātmanorekatayādhigatyā |
idaṃ na jāne'pyanidaṃ na jāne kiṃ vā kiyadvā sukhamastyapāram || 481 ||
verses.colloquial:
buddhir vinashta galitaa pravrittih brahma aatmanor ekatayaa adhigatyaa |
idam na jaane api anidam na jaane kim vaa kiyad vaa sukham asti apaaram || 481 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through realising the identity of the Self and Brahman, my mind has vanished and all its activities have melted away. I do not know this or not-this, nor what the boundless Bliss (of Samadhi) is or how great it is!

verses.sanskrit:
वाचा वक्तुमशक्यमेव मनसा मन्तुं न वा शक्यते स्वानन्दामृतपूरपूरितपरब्रह्माम्बुधेर्वैभवम् ।
अम्भोराशिविशीर्णवार्षिकशिलाभावं भजन्मे मनो यस्यांशांशलवे विलीनमधुनानन्दात्मना निर्वृतम् ॥ ४८२ ॥
verses.roman:
vācā vaktumaśakyameva manasā mantuṃ na vā śakyate svānandāmṛtapūrapūritaparabrahmāmbudhervaibhavam |
ambhorāśiviśīrṇavārṣikaśilābhāvaṃ bhajanme mano yasyāṃśāṃśalave vilīnamadhunānandātmanā nirvṛtam || 482 ||
verses.colloquial:
vaachaa vaktum ashakya eva manasaa mantum na vaa shakyate sva aananda amrita puura puurita para brahma ambudhe vaibhavam |
ambho raashi vishiirna vaarshika shilaa bhaavam bhajan me mano yasya amsha amsha lave viliinam adhunaa aananda aatmanaa nirvritam || 482 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The grandeur of the ocean of Supreme Brahman, brimming with the swell of the Self's nectar-like Bliss, truly cannot be put into words or grasped by the mind. In the tiniest fraction of it my mind melted, like a hailstone dissolving in the sea, and it now rests content in that Essence of Bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
क्व गतं केन वा नीतं कुत्र लीनमिदं जगत् ।
अधुनैव मया दृष्टं नास्ति किं महदद्भुतम् ॥ ४८३ ॥
verses.roman:
kva gataṃ kena vā nītaṃ kutra līnamidaṃ jagat |
adhunaiva mayā dṛṣṭaṃ nāsti kiṃ mahadadbhutam || 483 ||
verses.colloquial:
kva gatam kena vaa niitam kutra liinam idam jagat |
adhunaiva mayaa drishtam naasti kim mahad adbhutam || 483 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Where has the universe gone? Who took it away? Into what has it merged? I saw it only a moment ago, and has it stopped existing? This is very strange!

verses.sanskrit:
किं हेयं किमुपादेयं किमन्यत्किं विलक्षणम् ।
अखण्डानन्दपीयूषपूर्णे ब्रह्ममहार्णवे ॥ ४८४ ॥
verses.roman:
kiṃ heyaṃ kimupādeyaṃ kimanyatkiṃ vilakṣaṇam |
akhaṇḍānandapīyūṣapūrṇe brahmamahārṇave || 484 ||
verses.colloquial:
kim heyam kim upaadeyam kim anyat kim vilakshanam |
akhanda aananda piiyuusha puurne brahma mahaa arnave || 484 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the ocean of Brahman, full of the nectar of Absolute Bliss, what is there to reject or to accept? What is other (than oneself), and what is different?

verses.sanskrit:
न किंचिदत्र पश्यामि न शृणोमि न वेद्म्यहम् ।
स्वात्मनैव सदानन्दरूपेणास्मि विलक्षणः ॥ ४८५ ॥
verses.roman:
na kiṃcidatra paśyāmi na śṛṇomi na vedmyaham |
svātmanaiva sadānandarūpeṇāsmi vilakṣaṇaḥ || 485 ||
verses.colloquial:
na kimcid atra pashyaami na shrinomi na vedmi aham |
sva aatmana eva sadaa aananda ruupena asmi vilakshanah || 485 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In this state I see nothing, hear nothing, and know nothing. I simply exist as the Self, eternal Bliss, distinct from everything else.

verses.sanskrit:
नमो नमस्ते गुरवे महात्मने विमुक्तसङ्गाय सदुत्तमाय ।
नित्याद्वयानन्दरसस्वरूपिणे भूम्ने सदापारदयाम्बुधाम्ने ॥ ४८६ ॥
verses.roman:
namo namaste gurave mahātmane vimuktasaṅgāya saduttamāya |
nityādvayānandarasasvarūpiṇe bhūmne sadāpāradayāmbudhāmne || 486 ||
verses.colloquial:
namo namaste gurave mahaatmane vimukta sangaaya sad uttamaaya |
nitya advaya aananda rasa svaruupine bhuumne sadaa apaara dayaa ambu dhaamne || 486 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Salutations again and again to you, O noble Teacher, free from attachment, best of good souls, embodiment of the essence of Eternal Bliss, the One without a second, infinite and forever a boundless ocean of mercy:

verses.sanskrit:
यत्कटाक्षशशिसान्द्रचन्द्रिका पातधूतभवतापजश्रमः ।
प्राप्तवानहमखण्डवैभवा नन्दमात्मपदमक्षयं क्षणात् ॥ ४८७ ॥
verses.roman:
yatkaṭākṣaśaśisāndracandrikā pātadhūtabhavatāpajaśramaḥ |
prāptavānahamakhaṇḍavaibhavā nandamātmapadamakṣayaṃ kṣaṇāt || 487 ||
verses.colloquial:
yat kataaksha shashi saandra candrikaa paata dhuuta bhava taapa ja shramah |
praapta vaan aham akhanda vaibhavaa nandam aatma padam akshayam kshanaat || 487 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Your glance, like a shower of concentrated moonbeams, has taken away the exhaustion brought on by the world's afflictions, and in a moment has admitted me to the undecaying state of the Ātman, the Bliss of infinite majesty!

verses.sanskrit:
धन्योऽहं कृतकृत्योऽहं विमुक्तोऽहं भवग्रहात् ।
नित्यानन्दस्वरूपोऽहं पूर्णोऽहं त्वदनुग्रहात् ॥ ४८८ ॥
verses.roman:
dhanyo'haṃ kṛtakṛtyo'haṃ vimukto'haṃ bhavagrahāt |
nityānandasvarūpo'haṃ pūrṇo'haṃ tvadanugrahāt || 488 ||
verses.colloquial:
dhanyo aham krita krityo aham vimukto aham bhava grahaat |
nitya aananda svaruupo aham puurno aham tvad anugrahaat || 488 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am blessed. I have reached the fulfilment of my life and am free from the grip of transmigration. I am the Essence of Eternal Bliss, I am infinite, and all of it through your mercy!

verses.sanskrit:
असङ्गोऽहमनङ्गोऽहमलिङ्गोऽहमभङ्गुरः ।
प्रशान्तोऽहमनन्तोऽहममलोऽहं चिरन्तनः ॥ ४८९ ॥
verses.roman:
asaṅgo'hamanaṅgo'hamaliṅgo'hamabhaṅguraḥ |
praśānto'hamananto'hamamalo'haṃ cirantanaḥ || 489 ||
verses.colloquial:
asango aham anango aham alingo aham abhangura |
prashaanto aham ananto aham amalo aham chirantana || 489 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am unattached. I have no body. I am free from the subtle body and undecaying. I am calm, I am infinite, I am stainless and eternal.

verses.sanskrit:
अकर्ताहमभोक्ताहमविकारोऽहमक्रियः ।
शुद्धबोधस्वरूपोऽहं केवलोऽहं सदाशिवः ॥ ४९0 ॥
verses.roman:
akartāhamabhoktāhamavikāro'hamakriyaḥ |
śuddhabodhasvarūpo'haṃ kevalo'haṃ sadāśivaḥ || 490 ||
verses.colloquial:
akartaa aham abhoktaa aham avikaaroham akriyah |
shuddha bodha svaroopoham kevaloham sadaa shivah || 490 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am not the doer and not the experiencer. I am changeless and beyond activity. I am the essence of Pure Knowledge, Absolute, and one with Eternal Good.

verses.sanskrit:
द्रष्टुः श्रोतुर्वक्तुः कर्तुर्भोक्तुर्विभिन्न एवाहम् ।
नित्यनिरन्तरनिष्क्रियनिःसीमासङ्गपूर्णबोधात्मा ॥ ४९१ ॥
verses.roman:
draṣṭuḥ śroturvaktuḥ karturbhokturvibhinna evāham |
nityanirantaraniṣkriyaniḥsīmāsaṅgapūrṇabodhātmā || 491 ||
verses.colloquial:
drashtuh shrotur vaktuh kartur bhoktur vibhinna eva aham |
nitya nirantara nishkriya nihsiima asanga puurna bodha aatmaa || 491 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am truly other than the one who sees, hears, speaks, does, and experiences. I am the essence of Knowledge: eternal, unbroken, beyond activity, limitless, unattached, and infinite.

verses.sanskrit:
नाहमिदं नाहमदोऽप्युभयोरवभासकं परं शुद्धम् ।
बाह्याभ्यन्तरशून्यं पूर्णं ब्रह्माद्वितीयमेवाहम् ॥ ४९२ ॥
verses.roman:
nāhamidaṃ nāhamado'pyubhayoravabhāsakaṃ paraṃ śuddham |
bāhyābhyantaraśūnyaṃ pūrṇaṃ brahmādvitīyamevāham || 492 ||
verses.colloquial:
na aham idam na aham ado api ubhayoh avabhaasakam param shuddham |
baahya abhyantara shuunyam puurnam brahma adviitiiyam eva aham || 492 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am neither this nor that, but the Supreme that lights up both. I am truly Brahman, the One without a second, pure, with no inside or outside, and infinite.

verses.sanskrit:
निरुपममनादितत्त्वं त्वमहमिदमद इति कल्पनादूरम् ।
नित्यानन्दैकरसं सत्यं ब्रह्माद्वितीयमेवाहम् ॥ ४९३ ॥
verses.roman:
nirupamamanāditattvaṃ tvamahamidamada iti kalpanādūram |
nityānandaikarasaṃ satyaṃ brahmādvitīyamevāham || 493 ||
verses.colloquial:
nirupamam anaadi tattvam tvam aham idam ada iti kalpanaa duuram |
nitya aananda eka rasam satyam brahma adviitiiyam eva aham || 493 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am truly Brahman, the One without a second, without equal, the beginningless Reality, beyond such imaginings as you and I, or this and that, the Essence of Eternal Bliss, the Truth.

verses.sanskrit:
नारायणोऽहं नरकान्तकोऽहं पुरान्तकोऽहं पुरुषोऽहमीशः ।
अखण्डबोधोऽहमशेषसाक्षी निरीश्वरोऽहं निरहं च निर्ममः ॥ ४९४ ॥
verses.roman:
nārāyaṇo'haṃ narakāntako'haṃ purāntako'haṃ puruṣo'hamīśaḥ |
akhaṇḍabodho'hamaśeṣasākṣī nirīśvaro'haṃ nirahaṃ ca nirmamaḥ || 494 ||
verses.colloquial:
naaraayano aham naraka antako aham pura antako aham purusho aham iishah |
akhanda bodho aham ashesha saakshii niriishvaro aham niraham cha nirmamah || 494 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am Nārāyaṇa, the slayer of Nāraka. I am the destroyer of Tripura, the Supreme Being, the Ruler. I am Knowledge Absolute, the Witness of everything. I have no Ruler other than myself, and I am without the ideas of "I" and "mine."

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वेषु भूतेष्वहमेव संस्थितो ज्ञानात्मनान्तर्बहिराश्रयः सन् ।
भोक्ता च भोग्यं स्वयमेव सर्वं यद्यत्पृथग्दृष्टमिदन्तया पुरा ॥ ४९५ ॥
verses.roman:
sarveṣu bhūteṣvahameva saṃsthito jñānātmanāntarbahirāśrayaḥ san |
bhoktā ca bhogyaṃ svayameva sarvaṃ yadyatpṛthagdṛṣṭamidantayā purā || 495 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarveshu bhuuteshu aham eva samsthito jnaana aatmanaa antar bahir aashrayah san |
bhoktaa ca bhogyam svayam eva sarvam yad yat prithak drishtam idantayaa puraa || 495 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I alone dwell as knowledge in all beings, their inner and outer support. I myself am the experiencer and everything experienced, all that I earlier regarded as "this," the not-Self.

verses.sanskrit:
मय्यखण्डसुखाम्भोधौ बहुधा विश्ववीचयः ।
उत्पद्यन्ते विलीयन्ते मायामारुतविभ्रमात् ॥ ४९६ ॥
verses.roman:
mayyakhaṇḍasukhāmbhodhau bahudhā viśvavīcayaḥ |
utpadyante vilīyante māyāmārutavibhramāt || 496 ||
verses.colloquial:
mayi akhanda sukha ambhodhau bahudhaa vishva viicayah |
utpadyante viliiyante maayaa maaruta vibhramaat || 496 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In me, the ocean of Infinite Bliss, the waves of the universe rise and fall through the play of the wind of Māyā.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थुलादिभावा मयि कल्पिता भ्रमाद् आरोपितानुस्फुरणेन लोकैः ।
काले यथा कल्पकवत्सराय णर्त्वादयो निष्कलनिर्विकल्पे ॥ ४९७ ॥
verses.roman:
sthulādibhāvā mayi kalpitā bhramād āropitānusphuraṇena lokaiḥ |
kāle yathā kalpakavatsarāya ṇartvādayo niṣkalanirvikalpe || 497 ||
verses.colloquial:
sthuula aadi bhaavaa mayi kalpitaa bhramaat aaropita anusphuranena lokaihi |
kaale yathaa kalpa vatsara ayana ritu aadayo nishkala nirvikalpe || 497 ||
verses.translation_reworded: People mistakenly imagine in me such ideas as gross (or subtle) through the appearance of superimposed things, just as cycles, years, half-years, seasons, and so on are imagined in indivisible, absolute time.

verses.sanskrit:
आरोपितं नाश्रयदूषकं भवेत् कदापि मूढैरतिदोषदूषितैः ।
नार्द्रिकरोत्यूषरभूमिभागं मरीचिकावारि महाप्रवाहः ॥ ४९८ ॥
verses.roman:
āropitaṃ nāśrayadūṣakaṃ bhavet kadāpi mūḍhairatidoṣadūṣitaiḥ |
nārdrikarotyūṣarabhūmibhāgaṃ marīcikāvāri mahāpravāhaḥ || 498 ||
verses.colloquial:
aaropitam na aashraya duushakam bhavet kadaapi muudhair ati dosha duushitaih |
na aardri karoti uushara bhuumi bhaagam mariichikaa vaari mahaa pravaahaḥ || 498 ||
verses.translation_reworded: What grossly ignorant fools superimpose can never stain the substratum. The great flood of water seen in a mirage never dampens the desert.

verses.sanskrit:
आकाशवल्लेपविदूरगोऽहं आदित्यवद्भास्यविलक्षणोऽहम् ।
अहार्यवन्नित्यविनिश्चलोऽहं अम्भोधिवत्पारविवर्जितोऽहम् ॥ ४९९ ॥
verses.roman:
ākāśavallepavidūrago'haṃ ādityavadbhāsyavilakṣaṇo'ham |
ahāryavannityaviniścalo'haṃ ambhodhivatpāravivarjito'ham || 499 ||
verses.colloquial:
aakaasha vat lepa viduura go aham aaditya vat bhaasya vilakshano aham |
ahaarya vat nitya vinishchalo aham ambhodhi vat paara vivarjito aham || 499 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Like the sky, I am beyond contamination. Like the sun, I am separate from the things lit up. Like the mountain, I am forever motionless. Like the ocean, I am without limit.

verses.sanskrit:
न मे देहेन संबन्धो मेघेनेव विहायसः ।
अतः कुतो मे तद्धर्मा जाक्रत्स्वप्नसुषुप्तयः ॥ ५00 ॥
verses.roman:
na me dehena saṃbandho megheneva vihāyasaḥ |
ataḥ kuto me taddharmā jākratsvapnasuṣuptayaḥ || 500 ||
verses.colloquial:
na me dehena sambandho meghena iva vihaayasah |
atah kuto me tad dharmaa jaakrat svapna sushuptayah || 500 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I have no connection with the body, just as the sky has none with the clouds. So how can waking, dream, and deep sleep, which are attributes of the body, affect me?

verses.sanskrit:
उपाधिरायाति स एव गच्छति स एव कर्माणि करोति भुङ्क्ते ।
स एव जीर्यन्म्रियते सदाहं कुलाद्रिवन्निश्चल एव संस्थितः ॥ ५0१ ॥
verses.roman:
upādhirāyāti sa eva gacchati sa eva karmāṇi karoti bhuṅkte |
sa eva jīryanmriyate sadāhaṃ kulādrivanniścala eva saṃsthitaḥ || 501 ||
verses.colloquial:
upaadhi raayaati sa eva gacchati sa eva karmaani karoti bhunkte |
sa eva jiiryan mriyate sadaaham kulaadri van nishcala eva samsthitah || 501 ||
verses.translation_reworded: It is the Upādhi (superimposed attribute) that comes, and that alone goes. It is that which acts and experiences (the results), and that alone which decays and dies. I remain forever firm, like the Kula mountain.

verses.sanskrit:
न मे प्रवृत्तिर्न च मे निवृत्तिः सदैकरूपस्य निरंशकस्य ।
एकात्मको यो निविडो निरन्तरो व्योमेव पूर्णः स कथं नु चेष्टते ॥ ५0२ ॥
verses.roman:
na me pravṛttirna ca me nivṛttiḥ sadaikarūpasya niraṃśakasya |
ekātmako yo niviḍo nirantaro vyomeva pūrṇaḥ sa kathaṃ nu ceṣṭate || 502 ||
verses.colloquial:
na me pravrittir na ca me nivrittih sadaa eka ruupasya niramshakasya |
eka aatmako yo nivido nirantaro vyoma iva puurnah sa katham nu cheshtate || 502 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For me, who am always the same and have no parts, there is neither taking up work nor ceasing from it. How could what is One, concentrated, unbroken, and infinite like the sky ever exert itself?

verses.sanskrit:
पुण्यानि पापानि निरिन्द्रियस्य निश्चेतसो निर्विकृतेर्निराकृतेः ।
कुतो ममाखण्डसुखानुभूतेः ब्रूते ह्यनन्वागतमित्यपि श्रुतिः ॥ ५0३ ॥
verses.roman:
puṇyāni pāpāni nirindriyasya niścetaso nirvikṛternirākṛteḥ |
kuto mamākhaṇḍasukhānubhūteḥ brūte hyananvāgatamityapi śrutiḥ || 503 ||
verses.colloquial:
punyaani paapani nirindriyasya nishchetaso nirvikriter niraakriteh |
kuto mama akhanda sukha anubhuteh bruute hi ananyaagatam iti api shrutih || 503 ||
verses.translation_reworded: How can there be merit or demerit for me, who have no organs, no mind, no change, and no form, and who am the realisation of Bliss Absolute? The Shruti says this too, in the passage "Not touched," and so on.

verses.sanskrit:
छायया स्पृष्टमुष्णं वा शीतं वा सुष्ठु दुःष्ठु वा ।
न स्पृशत्येव यत्किंचित्पुरुषं तद्विलक्षणम् ॥ ५0४ ॥
verses.roman:
chāyayā spṛṣṭamuṣṇaṃ vā śītaṃ vā suṣṭhu duḥṣṭhu vā |
na spṛśatyeva yatkiṃcitpuruṣaṃ tadvilakṣaṇam || 504 ||
verses.colloquial:
chaayayaa sprishtam ushnam vaa shiitam vaa sushtu dushtu vaa |
na sprishaty eva yat kimchit purusham tad vilakshanam || 504 ||
verses.translation_reworded: If heat or cold, good or evil, happens to touch the shadow of a person's body, it does not affect in the least the person himself, who is separate from the shadow.

verses.sanskrit:
न साक्षिणं साक्ष्यधर्माः संस्पृशन्ति विलक्षणम् ।
अविकारमुदासीनं गृहधर्माः प्रदीपवत् ॥ ५0५ ॥
verses.roman:
na sākṣiṇaṃ sākṣyadharmāḥ saṃspṛśanti vilakṣaṇam |
avikāramudāsīnaṃ gṛhadharmāḥ pradīpavat || 505 ||
verses.colloquial:
na saakshinam saakshya dharmaah samsprishanti vilakshanam |
avikaaram udaasinam griha dharmaah pradiipavat || 505 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The properties of things observed do not affect the Witness, which is separate from them, changeless, and indifferent, just as the properties of a room (do not affect) the lamp (that lights it).

verses.sanskrit:
रवेर्यथा कर्मणि साक्षिभावो वन्हेर्यथा दाहनियामकत्वम् ।
रज्जोर्यथारोपितवस्तुसङ्गः तथैव कूटस्थचिदात्मनो मे ॥ ५0६ ॥
verses.roman:
raveryathā karmaṇi sākṣibhāvo vanheryathā dāhaniyāmakatvam |
rajjoryathāropitavastusaṅgaḥ tathaiva kūṭasthacidātmano me || 506 ||
verses.colloquial:
raver yathaa karmani saakshi bhaavo vahner yathaa daaha niyaamakatvam |
rajjor yathaa aaropita vastu sangah tathaa eva kuutastha cid aatmano me || 506 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Just as the sun is only a witness of people's actions, as fire burns everything without distinction, and as the rope is related to what is superimposed on it, so am I, the unchanging Self, Intelligence Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्तापि वा कारयितापि नाहं भोक्तापि वा भोजयितापि नाहम् ।
द्रष्टापि वा दर्शयितापि नाहं सोऽहं स्वयंज्योतिरनीदृगात्मा ॥ ५0७ ॥
verses.roman:
kartāpi vā kārayitāpi nāhaṃ bhoktāpi vā bhojayitāpi nāham |
draṣṭāpi vā darśayitāpi nāhaṃ so'haṃ svayaṃjyotiranīdṛgātmā || 507 ||
verses.colloquial:
kartaa api vaa kaarayitaa api na aham bhoktaa api vaa bhojayitaa api na aham |
drashtaa api vaa darshayitaa api na aham so aham svayam jyotir aniidrig aatmaa || 507 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I do not act or cause others to act. I do not enjoy or cause others to enjoy. I do not see or cause others to see. I am that Self-effulgent, Transcendent Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
चलत्युपाधौ प्रतिबिम्बलौल्यम् अउपाधिकं मूढधियो नयन्ति ।
स्वबिम्बभूतं रविवद्विनिष्क्रियं कर्तास्मि भोक्तास्मि हतोऽस्मि हेति ॥ ५0८ ॥
verses.roman:
calatyupādhau pratibimbalaulyam aupādhikaṃ mūḍhadhiyo nayanti |
svabimbabhūtaṃ ravivadviniṣkriyaṃ kartāsmi bhoktāsmi hato'smi heti || 508 ||
verses.colloquial:
calati upaadhau pratibimba laulyam aupaadhikam muudha dhiyo nayanti |
sva bimba bhuutam ravivat vinishkriyam kartaa asmi bhoktaa asmi hato asmi heti || 508 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the added adjunct (Upādhi) moves, fools attribute the resulting movement of the reflection to the thing reflected, such as the sun, which has no activity. (So they think) "I am the doer," "I am the experiencer," "I am killed, oh, alas!"

verses.sanskrit:
जले वापि स्थले वापि लुठत्वेष जडात्मकः ।
नाहं विलिप्ये तद्धर्मैर्घटधर्मैर्नभो यथा ॥ ५0९ ॥
verses.roman:
jale vāpi sthale vāpi luṭhatveṣa jaḍātmakaḥ |
nāhaṃ vilipye taddharmairghaṭadharmairnabho yathā || 509 ||
verses.colloquial:
jale vaapi sthale vaapi luthatv esha jadaatmakah |
naaham vilipye tad dharmair ghata dharmair nabho yathaa || 509 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Let this inert body fall in water or on land. Its properties do not touch me, just as the properties of a jar do not touch the sky.

verses.sanskrit:
कर्तृत्वभोक्तृत्वखलत्वमत्तता जडत्वबद्धत्वविमुक्ततादयः ।
बुद्धेर्विकल्पा न तु सन्ति वस्तुतः स्वस्मिन् परे ब्रह्मणि केवलेऽद्वये ॥ ५१0 ॥
verses.roman:
kartṛtvabhoktṛtvakhalatvamattatā jaḍatvabaddhatvavimuktatādayaḥ |
buddhervikalpā na tu santi vastutaḥ svasmin pare brahmaṇi kevale'dvaye || 510 ||
verses.colloquial:
kartritva bhoktritva khalatva mattataa jadatva baddhatva vimuktataa aadayah |
buddher vikalpaa na tu santi vastutah svasmin pare brahmani kevale advaye || 510 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Agency, experience, cunning, drunkenness, dullness, bondage, freedom: these are passing states of the Buddhi. They never truly belong to the Self, the Supreme Brahman, the Absolute, the One without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
सन्तु विकाराः प्रकृतेर्दशधा शतधा सहस्रधा वापि ।
किं मेऽसङ्गचितस्तैर्न घनः क्वचिदम्बरं स्पृशति ॥ ५११ ॥
verses.roman:
santu vikārāḥ prakṛterdaśadhā śatadhā sahasradhā vāpi |
kiṃ me'saṅgacitastairna ghanaḥ kvacidambaraṃ spṛśati || 511 ||
verses.colloquial:
santu vikaaraah prakriter dashadhaa shatadhaa sahasradhaa vaapi |
kim me asanga chitas tair na ghanah kvachid ambaram sprishati || 511 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Let the Prakriti change in ten, a hundred, or a thousand ways. What have those changes to do with me, the unattached Knowledge Absolute? The clouds never touch the sky!

verses.sanskrit:
अव्यक्तादिस्थूलपर्यन्तमेतत् विश्व यत्राभासमात्रं प्रतीतम् ।
व्योमप्रख्यं सूक्ष्ममाद्यन्तहीनं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१२ ॥
verses.roman:
avyaktādisthūlaparyantametat viśva yatrābhāsamātraṃ pratītam |
vyomaprakhyaṃ sūkṣmamādyantahīnaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 512 ||
verses.colloquial:
avyakta aadi sthuula paryantam etat vishva yatra aabhaasa maatram pratiitam |
vyoma prakhyam suukshmam aadi anta hiinam brahma advaitam yat tat eva aham asmi || 512 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am truly that Brahman, the One without a second, subtle like the sky, without beginning or end, in which the whole universe, from the Undifferentiated down to the gross body, appears as nothing more than a shadow.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वाधारं सर्ववस्तुप्रकाशं सर्वाकारं सर्वगं सर्वशून्यम् ।
नित्यं शुद्धं निश्चलं निर्विकल्पं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१३ ॥
verses.roman:
sarvādhāraṃ sarvavastuprakāśaṃ sarvākāraṃ sarvagaṃ sarvaśūnyam |
nityaṃ śuddhaṃ niścalaṃ nirvikalpaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 513 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarva aadharam sarva vastu prakaasham sarva aakaaram sarva gam sarva shuunyam |
nityam shuddham nishchalam nirvikalpam brahma advaitam yat tat eva aham asmi || 513 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am truly that Brahman, the One without a second, the support of all, which lights up all things, has infinite forms, is present everywhere, is free of multiplicity, and is eternal, pure, unmoved, and absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्प्रत्यस्ताशेषमायाविशेषं प्रत्यग्रूपं प्रत्ययागम्यमानम् ।
सत्यज्ञानानन्तमानन्दरूपं ब्रह्माद्वैतं यत्तदेवाहमस्मि ॥ ५१४ ॥
verses.roman:
yatpratyastāśeṣamāyāviśeṣaṃ pratyagrūpaṃ pratyayāgamyamānam |
satyajñānānantamānandarūpaṃ brahmādvaitaṃ yattadevāhamasmi || 514 ||
verses.colloquial:
yat pratyasta ashesha maayaa vishesham pratyag ruupam pratyaya agamyamaanam |
satya jnaana anantam aananda ruupam brahma advaitam yat tat eva aham asmi || 514 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am truly that Brahman, the One without a second, which lies beyond the endless differentiations of Māyā, is the innermost essence of all, is out of the reach of consciousness, and is Truth, Knowledge, Infinity, and Bliss Absolute.

verses.sanskrit:
निष्क्रियोऽस्म्यविकारोऽस्मि निष्कलोऽस्मि निराकृतिः ।
निर्विकल्पोऽस्मि नित्योऽस्मि निरालम्बोऽस्मि निर्द्वयः ॥ ५१५ ॥
verses.roman:
niṣkriyo'smyavikāro'smi niṣkalo'smi nirākṛtiḥ |
nirvikalpo'smi nityo'smi nirālambo'smi nirdvayaḥ || 515 ||
verses.colloquial:
nishkriyo asmi avikaaro asmi nishkalo asmi niraakritih |
nirvikalpo asmi nityo asmi niraalambo asmi nirdvayah || 515 ||
verses.translation_reworded: I am without activity, without change, without parts, without form. I am absolute, eternal, in need of no other support, the One without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
सर्वात्मकोऽहं सर्वोऽहं सर्वातीतोऽहमद्वयः ।
केवलाखण्डबोधोऽहमानन्दोऽहं निरन्तरः ॥ ५१६ ॥
verses.roman:
sarvātmako'haṃ sarvo'haṃ sarvātīto'hamadvayaḥ |
kevalākhaṇḍabodho'hamānando'haṃ nirantaraḥ || 516 ||
verses.colloquial:
sarva aatmako aham sarvo aham sarva atiito aham advayah |
kevala akshanda bodho aham aanando aham nirantarah || 516 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Universal and the All am I, transcendent and One without a second. Absolute and Infinite Knowledge is what I am, and indivisible Bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वाराज्यसाम्राज्यविभूतिरेषा भवत्कृपाश्रीमहिमप्रसादात् ।
प्राप्ता मया श्रीगुरवे महात्मने नमो नमस्तेऽस्तु पुनर्नमोऽस्तु ॥ ५१७ ॥
verses.roman:
svārājyasāmrājyavibhūtireṣā bhavatkṛpāśrīmahimaprasādāt |
prāptā mayā śrīgurave mahātmane namo namaste'stu punarnamo'stu || 517 ||
verses.colloquial:
svaaraajya saamraajya vibhuutir eshaa bhavat kripaa shrii mahima prasaadaat |
praaptaa mayaa shrii gurave mahaatmane namo namaste astu punar namo astu || 517 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Through the supreme majesty of your grace I have received this splendour, the sovereignty of Self-effulgence. Salutations to you, O glorious, noble-minded Teacher, salutations again and again!

verses.sanskrit:
महास्वप्ने मायाकृतजनिजरामृत्युगहने भ्रमन्तं क्लिश्यन्तं बहुलतरतापैरनुदिनम् ।
अहंकारव्याघ्रव्यथितमिममत्यन्तकृपया प्रबोध्य प्रस्वापात्परमवितवान्मामसि गुरो ॥ ५१८ ॥
verses.roman:
mahāsvapne māyākṛtajanijarāmṛtyugahane bhramantaṃ kliśyantaṃ bahulataratāpairanudinam |
ahaṃkāravyāghravyathitamimamatyantakṛpayā prabodhya prasvāpātparamavitavānmāmasi guro || 518 ||
verses.colloquial:
mahaa svapne maayaa krita jani jaraa mrityu gahane bhramantam klishyantam bahula tara taapair anudinam |
ahamkaara vyaaghra vyathitam imam atyanta kripayaa prabodhya prasvaapaat param avitavaan maam asi guro || 518 ||
verses.translation_reworded: O Master, out of pure grace you have woken me from sleep and rescued me completely. I was wandering in an endless dream, in a forest of birth, decay, and death created by illusion, tormented day after day by countless afflictions and badly harried by the tiger of egoism.

verses.sanskrit:
नमस्तस्मै सदैकस्मै कस्मैचिन्महसे नमः ।
यदेतद्विश्वरूपेण राजते गुरुराज ते ॥ ५१९ ॥
verses.roman:
namastasmai sadaikasmai kasmaicinmahase namaḥ |
yadetadviśvarūpeṇa rājate gururāja te || 519 ||
verses.colloquial:
namas tasmai sada ekasmai kasmaicin mahase namah |
yad etad vishva ruupena raajate guru raaja te || 519 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Salutations to you, O Prince of Teachers, Greatness beyond naming, who are always the same and who show yourself as this universe. To you I bow.

verses.sanskrit:
इति नतमवलोक्य शिष्यवर्यं समधिगतात्मसुखं प्रबुद्धतत्त्वम् ।
प्रमुदितहृदयं स देशिकेन्द्रः पुनरिदमाह वचः परं महात्मा ॥ ५२0 ॥
verses.roman:
iti natamavalokya śiṣyavaryaṃ samadhigatātmasukhaṃ prabuddhatattvam |
pramuditahṛdayaṃ sa deśikendraḥ punaridamāha vacaḥ paraṃ mahātmā || 520 ||
verses.colloquial:
iti natam avalokya shishya varyam samadhigata aatma sukham prabuddha tattvam |
pramudita hridayam sa deshika indrah punar idam aaha vacah param mahaatmaa || 520 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Seeing the worthy disciple prostrating himself in this way, having reached the Bliss of the Self, realised the Truth, and grown glad at heart, that noble, ideal Teacher spoke again in these excellent words:

verses.sanskrit:
<vt>Final Words of Advice</vt>
ब्रह्मप्रत्ययसन्ततिर्जगदतो ब्रह्मैव तत्सर्वतः पश्याध्यात्मदृशा प्रशान्तमनसा सर्वास्ववस्थास्वपि ।
रूपादन्यदवेक्षितं किमभितश्चक्षुष्मतां दृश्यते तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदः सतः किमपरं बुद्धेर्विहारास्पदम् ॥ ५२१ ॥
verses.roman:
<vt>Final Words of Advice</vt>
brahmapratyayasantatirjagadato brahmaiva tatsarvataḥ paśyādhyātmadṛśā praśāntamanasā sarvāsvavasthāsvapi |
rūpādanyadavekṣitaṃ kimabhitaścakṣuṣmatāṃ dṛśyate tadvadbrahmavidaḥ sataḥ kimaparaṃ buddhervihārāspadam || 521 ||
verses.colloquial:
<vt>Final Words of Advice</vt>
brahma pratyaya santatir jagad ato brahma eva tat sarvatah pashya adhyaatma drishaa prashaanta manasaa sarvaasu avasthasu api |
ruupa aad anyad avekshitam kim abhitah chakshushmataam drishyate tadvad brahma vidah satah kim aparam buddher vihaara aaspadam || 521 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The universe is an unbroken series of perceptions of Brahman, and so it is in every respect nothing but Brahman. See this with the eye of illumination and a calm mind, in all circumstances. Does a person with eyes ever see anything around him except forms? In the same way, what is there apart from Brahman to occupy the intellect of a realised person?

verses.sanskrit:
कस्तां परानन्दरसानुभूति मृत्सृज्य शून्येषु रमेत विद्वान् ।
चन्द्रे महाल्हादिनि दीप्यमाने चित्रेन्दुमालोकयितुं क इच्छेत् ॥ ५२२ ॥
verses.roman:
kastāṃ parānandarasānubhūti mṛtsṛjya śūnyeṣu rameta vidvān |
candre mahālhādini dīpyamāne citrendumālokayituṃ ka icchet || 522 ||
verses.colloquial:
kas taam para aananda rasa anubhuuti mrit srijya shuunyeshu rameta vidvaan |
candre mahaa aahlaadini diipyamaane citra indum aalokayitum ka icchet || 522 ||
verses.translation_reworded: What wise person would throw away that enjoyment of Supreme Bliss and take delight in insubstantial things? When the utterly lovely moon is shining, who would want to look at a painted moon?

verses.sanskrit:
असत्पदार्थानुभवेन किंचिन् न ह्यस्ति तृप्तिर्न च दुःखहानिः ।
तदद्वयानन्दरसानुभूत्या तृप्तः सुखं तिष्ठ सदात्मनिष्ठया ॥ ५२३ ॥
verses.roman:
asatpadārthānubhavena kiṃcin na hyasti tṛptirna ca duḥkhahāniḥ |
tadadvayānandarasānubhūtyā tṛptaḥ sukhaṃ tiṣṭha sadātmaniṣṭhayā || 523 ||
verses.colloquial:
asat padaartha anubhavena kimcin na hi asti triptir na ca duhkha haanih |
tad advaya aananda rasa anubhuutyaa triptah sukham tishtha sadaa aatma nishthayaa || 523 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Perceiving unreal things brings neither satisfaction nor an end to misery. So, content with realising the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, live happily in identity with that Reality.

verses.sanskrit:
स्वमेव सर्वथा पश्यन्मन्यमानः स्वमद्वयम् ।
स्वानन्दमनुभुञ्जानः कालं नय महामते ॥ ५२४ ॥
verses.roman:
svameva sarvathā paśyanmanyamānaḥ svamadvayam |
svānandamanubhuñjānaḥ kālaṃ naya mahāmate || 524 ||
verses.colloquial:
svam eva sarvathaa pashyan manyamaanah svam advayam |
sva aanandam anubhunjaanah kaalam naya mahaamate || 524 ||
verses.translation_reworded: O noble soul, spend your time seeing only the Self in every circumstance, thinking of the Self, the One without a second, and enjoying the Bliss of the Self!

verses.sanskrit:
अखण्डबोधात्मनि निर्विकल्पे विकल्पनं व्योम्नि पुरप्रकल्पनम् ।
तदद्वयानन्दमयात्मना सदा शान्तिं परामेत्य भजस्व मौनम् ॥ ५२५ ॥
verses.roman:
akhaṇḍabodhātmani nirvikalpe vikalpanaṃ vyomni puraprakalpanam |
tadadvayānandamayātmanā sadā śāntiṃ parāmetya bhajasva maunam || 525 ||
verses.colloquial:
akhanda bodha aatmani nirvikalpe vikalpanam vyomni pura prakalpanam |
tad advaya aananda maya aatmanaa sadaa shaantim paraam etya bhajasva maunam || 525 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Ideas of duality in the Ātman, the Infinite Knowledge, the Absolute, are like castles imagined in the air. So, always identifying yourself with the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second, and reaching Supreme Peace in that way, remain quiet.

verses.sanskrit:
तूष्णीमवस्था परमोपशान्तिः बुद्धेरसत्कल्पविकल्पहेतोः ।
ब्रह्मात्मन ब्रह्मविदो महात्मनो यत्राद्वयानन्दसुखं निरन्तरम् ॥ ५२६ ॥
verses.roman:
tūṣṇīmavasthā paramopaśāntiḥ buddherasatkalpavikalpahetoḥ |
brahmātmana brahmavido mahātmano yatrādvayānandasukhaṃ nirantaram || 526 ||
verses.colloquial:
tuushniim avasthaa parama upashaantih buddher asat kalpa vikalpa hetoh |
brahma aatmana brahma vido mahaatmano yatra advaya aananda sukham nirantaram || 526 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For the sage who has realised Brahman, the mind, the source of unreal fancies, becomes fully tranquil. This truly is his state of quietude, in which, one with Brahman, he constantly enjoys the Bliss Absolute, the One without a second.

verses.sanskrit:
नास्ति निर्वासनान्मौनात्परं सुखकृदुत्तमम् ।
विज्ञातात्मस्वरूपस्य स्वानन्दरसपायिनः ॥ ५२७ ॥
verses.roman:
nāsti nirvāsanānmaunātparaṃ sukhakṛduttamam |
vijñātātmasvarūpasya svānandarasapāyinaḥ || 527 ||
verses.colloquial:
naasti nirvaasanaan maunaat param sukha krit uttamam |
vijnaata aatma svaruupasya sva aananda rasa paayinah || 527 ||
verses.translation_reworded: For the person who has realised his own nature and drinks the undiluted Bliss of the Self, nothing is more exhilarating than the quietude that comes from being free of desire.

verses.sanskrit:
गच्छंस्तिष्ठन्नुपविशञ्छयानो वान्यथापि वा ।
यथेच्छया वेसेद्विद्वानात्नारामः सदा मुनिः ॥ ५२८ ॥
verses.roman:
gacchaṃstiṣṭhannupaviśañchayāno vānyathāpi vā |
yathecchayā vesedvidvānātnārāmaḥ sadā muniḥ || 528 ||
verses.colloquial:
gacchan tishthan upavishan shayaano vaa anyathaa api vaa |
yathaa icchayaa vased vidvaan aatma aaraamah sadaa munih || 528 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The illumined sage, whose only pleasure is in the Self, always lives at ease, whether walking or standing still, sitting or lying down, or in any other condition.

verses.sanskrit:
न देशकालासनदिग्यमादि लक्ष्याद्यपेक्षाप्रतिबद्धवृत्तेः ।
संसिद्धतत्त्वस्य महात्मनोऽस्ति स्ववेदने का नियमाद्यवस्था ॥ ५२९ ॥
verses.roman:
na deśakālāsanadigyamādi lakṣyādyapekṣāpratibaddhavṛtteḥ |
saṃsiddhatattvasya mahātmano'sti svavedane kā niyamādyavasthā || 529 ||
verses.colloquial:
na desha kaala aasana dik yama aadi lakshya aadi apekshaa pratibaddha vritteh |
samsiddha tattvasya mahaatmano asti sva vedane kaa niyama aadi avasthaa || 529 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The noble soul who has fully realised the Truth, and whose mind-functions meet no obstruction, no longer depends on conditions of place, time, posture, direction, moral disciplines, objects of meditation, and so on. What rules can apply to knowing one's own Self?

verses.sanskrit:
घटोऽयमिति विज्ञातुं नियमः कोऽन्ववेक्षते ।
विना प्रमाणसुष्ठुत्वं यस्मिन् सति पदार्थधीः ॥ ५३0 ॥
verses.roman:
ghaṭo'yamiti vijñātuṃ niyamaḥ ko'nvavekṣate |
vinā pramāṇasuṣṭhutvaṃ yasmin sati padārthadhīḥ || 530 ||
verses.colloquial:
ghato ayam iti vijnaatum niyamah ko anvavekshate |
vinaa pramaana sushthuttvam yasmin sati padaartha dhiih || 530 ||
verses.translation_reworded: To know that this is a jar, what condition is needed other than that the means of knowledge be free of defect, which alone ensures knowledge of the object?

verses.sanskrit:
अयमात्मा नित्यसिद्धः प्रमाणे सति भासते ।
न देशं नापि कालं न शुद्धिं वाप्यपेक्षते ॥ ५३१ ॥
verses.roman:
ayamātmā nityasiddhaḥ pramāṇe sati bhāsate |
na deśaṃ nāpi kālaṃ na śuddhiṃ vāpyapekṣate || 531 ||
verses.colloquial:
ayam aatmaa nitya siddha pramane sati bhaasate |
na desham na api kaalam na shuddhim va api apekshate || 531 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way this Ātman, an eternal truth, reveals Itself as soon as the right means of knowledge is present, and does not depend on place, time, or (inner) purity.

verses.sanskrit:
देवदत्तोऽहमित्येतद्विज्ञानं निरपेक्षकम् ।
तद्वद्ब्रह्मविदोऽप्यस्य ब्रह्माहमिति वेदनम् ॥ ५३२ ॥
verses.roman:
devadatto'hamityetadvijñānaṃ nirapekṣakam |
tadvadbrahmavido'pyasya brahmāhamiti vedanam || 532 ||
verses.colloquial:
devadatto aham iti etad vijnyaanam nirapekshakam |
tadvad brahmavido api asya brahma aham iti vedanam || 532 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The awareness "I am Devadatta" does not depend on circumstances. The same holds for the knower of Brahman's realisation that he is Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
भानुनेव जगत्सर्वं भासते यस्य तेजसा ।
अनात्मकमसत्तुच्छं किं नु तस्यावभासकम् ॥ ५३३ ॥
verses.roman:
bhānuneva jagatsarvaṃ bhāsate yasya tejasā |
anātmakamasattucchaṃ kiṃ nu tasyāvabhāsakam || 533 ||
verses.colloquial:
bhaanun eva jagat sarvam bhaasate yasya tejasaa |
anaatmakam asat tuccham kim nu tasya avabhaasakam || 533 ||
verses.translation_reworded: What could possibly reveal That whose radiance, like the sun's, makes the whole universe, insubstantial, unreal, and insignificant, appear at all?

verses.sanskrit:
वेदशास्त्रपुराणानि भूतानि सकलान्यपि ।
येनार्थवन्ति तं किन्नु विज्ञातारं प्रकाशयेत् ॥ ५३४ ॥
verses.roman:
vedaśāstrapurāṇāni bhūtāni sakalānyapi |
yenārthavanti taṃ kinnu vijñātāraṃ prakāśayet || 534 ||
verses.colloquial:
veda shaastra puraanaani bhuutaani sakalaani api |
yena arthavanti tam kinnu vijnaataaram prakaashayet || 534 ||
verses.translation_reworded: What could possibly light up that Eternal Subject through which the Vedas, the Puranas, the other Scriptures, and all beings are given meaning?

verses.sanskrit:
एष स्वयंज्योतिरनन्तशक्तिः आत्माप्रमेयः सकलानुभूतिः ।
यमेव विज्ञाय विमुक्तबन्धो जयत्ययं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमोत्तमः ॥ ५३५ ॥
verses.roman:
eṣa svayaṃjyotiranantaśaktiḥ ātmāprameyaḥ sakalānubhūtiḥ |
yameva vijñāya vimuktabandho jayatyayaṃ brahmaviduttamottamaḥ || 535 ||
verses.colloquial:
esha svayam jyotir ananta shaktih aatmaa prameyah sakala anubhuutih |
yam eva vijnaaya vimukta bandho jayaty ayam brahma vid uttama uttamah || 535 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Here is the Self-effulgent Ātman, of infinite power, beyond the reach of conditioned knowledge and yet the common experience of all. By realising this alone, this incomparable knower of Brahman lives his glorious life, free from bondage.

verses.sanskrit:
न खिद्यते नो विषयैः प्रमोदते न सज्जते नापि विरज्यते च ।
स्वस्मिन्सदा क्रीडति नन्दति स्वयं निरन्तरानन्दरसेन तृप्तः ॥ ५३६ ॥
verses.roman:
na khidyate no viṣayaiḥ pramodate na sajjate nāpi virajyate ca |
svasminsadā krīḍati nandati svayaṃ nirantarānandarasena tṛptaḥ || 536 ||
verses.colloquial:
na khidyate no vishayaih pramodate na sajjate naapi virajyate ca |
svasmin sadaa kriidati nandati svayam nirantara aananda rasena triptah || 536 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Content with undiluted, unending Bliss, he is neither saddened nor elated by sense-objects, neither attached to them nor averse to them, but always sports with the Self and takes pleasure in it.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षुधां देहव्यथां त्यक्त्वा बालः क्रीडति वस्तुनिः ।
तथैव विद्वान् रमते निर्ममो निरहं सुखी ॥ ५३७ ॥
verses.roman:
kṣudhāṃ dehavyathāṃ tyaktvā bālaḥ krīḍati vastuniḥ |
tathaiva vidvān ramate nirmamo nirahaṃ sukhī || 537 ||
verses.colloquial:
kshudhaam deha vyathaam tyaktvaa baalah kriidati vastunih |
tathaiva vidvaan ramate nirmamo niraham sukhii || 537 ||
verses.translation_reworded: A child plays with its toys, forgetting hunger and bodily pain. In exactly that way, the realised person takes pleasure in the Reality, without ideas of "I" or "mine," and is happy.

verses.sanskrit:
चिन्ताशून्यमदैन्यभैक्षमशनं पानं सरिद्वारिषु स्वातन्त्र्येण निरङ्कुशा स्थितिरभीर्निद्रा श्मशाने वने ।
वस्त्रं क्षालनशोषणादिरहितं दिग्वास्तु शय्या मही संचारो निगमान्तवीथिषु विदां क्रीडा परे ब्रह्मणि ॥ ५३८ ॥
verses.roman:
cintāśūnyamadainyabhaikṣamaśanaṃ pānaṃ saridvāriṣu svātantryeṇa niraṅkuśā sthitirabhīrnidrā śmaśāne vane |
vastraṃ kṣālanaśoṣaṇādirahitaṃ digvāstu śayyā mahī saṃcāro nigamāntavīthiṣu vidāṃ krīḍā pare brahmaṇi || 538 ||
verses.colloquial:
cintaa shuunyam adainya bhaiksham ashanam paanam sarid vaariṣu svaatantryena nirankushaa sthitir abhiir nidraa shmashaane vane |
vastram kshaalana shoshana aadi rahitam dig vaastu shayyaa mahii sancaaro nigamaanta viithishu vidaam kriidaa pare brahmani || 538 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Realised people get their food by begging, without anxiety or humiliation, and drink from rivers. They live freely and independently, and sleep without fear in cremation grounds or forests. Their clothing may be the directions themselves, which need no washing or drying, or some bark or the like. The earth is their bed. They roam along the avenue of Vedanta, and their pastime is in the Supreme Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
विमानमालम्ब्य शरीरमेतद् भुनक्त्यशेषान्विषयानुपस्थितान् ।
परेच्छया बालवदात्मवेत्ता योऽव्यक्तलिङ्गोऽननुषक्तबाह्यः ॥ ५३९ ॥
verses.roman:
vimānamālambya śarīrametad bhunaktyaśeṣānviṣayānupasthitān |
parecchayā bālavadātmavettā yo'vyaktaliṅgo'nanuṣaktabāhyaḥ || 539 ||
verses.colloquial:
vimaanam aalambya shariiram etad bhunakti asheshaan vishayaan upasthitaan |
parecchayaa baala vad aatma vettaa yo avyakta lingo ananuṣakta baahyah || 539 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The knower of the Ātman, who wears no outward sign and is unattached to external things, rests on this body without identifying with it, and, like a child, experiences all kinds of sense-objects as they come through the wishes of others.

verses.sanskrit:
दिगम्बरो वापि च साम्बरो वा त्वगम्बरो वापि चिदम्बरस्थः ।
उन्मत्तवद्वापि च बालवद्वा पिशाचवद्वापि चरत्यवन्याम् ॥ ५४0 ॥
verses.roman:
digambaro vāpi ca sāmbaro vā tvagambaro vāpi cidambarasthaḥ |
unmattavadvāpi ca bālavadvā piśācavadvāpi caratyavanyām || 540 ||
verses.colloquial:
digambaro vaapi ca saambaro vaa tvag ambaro vaapi cid ambara sthaah |
unmatta vad vaapi ca baala vad vaa pishaaca vad vaapi charati avanyaam || 540 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Established in the ethereal plane of Absolute Knowledge, he wanders through the world, sometimes like a madman, sometimes like a child, and at other times like a ghoul, wearing nothing but the directions, or sometimes clothes, or at other times perhaps skins.

verses.sanskrit:
कामान्निष्कामरूपी संश्चरत्येकचारो मुनिः ।
स्वात्मनैव सदा तुष्टः स्वयं सर्वात्मना स्थितः ॥ ५४१ ॥
verses.roman:
kāmānniṣkāmarūpī saṃścaratyekacāro muniḥ |
svātmanaiva sadā tuṣṭaḥ svayaṃ sarvātmanā sthitaḥ || 541 ||
verses.colloquial:
kaamaan nishkaama ruupii samshcarati eka caaro munih |
sva aatmanaa eva sadaa tushtah svayam sarva aatmanaa sthitah || 541 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Living alone, the sage partakes of sense-objects as the very embodiment of desirelessness. He is always satisfied with his own Self, and he himself is present in the All.

verses.sanskrit:
क्वचिन्मूढो विद्वान् क्वचिदपि महाराजविभवः क्वचिद्भ्रान्तः सौम्यः क्वचिदजगराचारकलितः ।
क्वचित्पात्रीभूतः क्वचिदवमतः क्वाप्यविदितः चरत्येवं प्राज्ञः सततपरमानन्दसुखितः ॥ ५४२ ॥
verses.roman:
kvacinmūḍho vidvān kvacidapi mahārājavibhavaḥ kvacidbhrāntaḥ saumyaḥ kvacidajagarācārakalitaḥ |
kvacitpātrībhūtaḥ kvacidavamataḥ kvāpyaviditaḥ caratyevaṃ prājñaḥ satataparamānandasukhitaḥ || 542 ||
verses.colloquial:
kvacit muudho vidvaan kvacit api mahaa raaja vibhavah kvacit bhraantah saumyah kvacit ajagara aacaara kalitah |
kvacit paatrii bhuutah kvacit avamatah kva api aviditah carati evam praajnah satata parama aananda sukhitah || 542 ||
verses.translation_reworded: At times he seems a fool, at times a sage, at times he has the splendour of a king. At times he wanders, at times he acts like a motionless python, at times his face is kindly. Sometimes honoured, sometimes insulted, sometimes unknown: so lives the man of realization, always happy in Supreme Bliss.

verses.sanskrit:
निर्धनोऽपि सदा तुष्टोऽप्यसहायो महाबलः ।
नित्यतृप्तोऽप्यभुञ्जानोऽप्यसमः समदर्शनः ॥ ५४३ ॥
verses.roman:
nirdhano'pi sadā tuṣṭo'pyasahāyo mahābalaḥ |
nityatṛpto'pyabhuñjāno'pyasamaḥ samadarśanaḥ || 543 ||
verses.colloquial:
nirdhanopi sadaa tushto api asahaayo mahaabalah |
nitya tripto api abhunjaano api asamah sama darshanah || 543 ||
verses.translation_reworded: He has no wealth, yet he is always content. He has no one to help him, yet he has great power. He does not enjoy sense-objects, yet he is eternally satisfied. He has no exemplar, yet he looks on everyone with an equal eye.

verses.sanskrit:
अपि कुर्वन्नकुर्वाणश्चाभोक्ता फलभोग्यपि ।
शरीर्यप्यशरीर्येष परिच्छिन्नोऽपि सर्वगः ॥ ५४४ ॥
verses.roman:
api kurvannakurvāṇaścābhoktā phalabhogyapi |
śarīryapyaśarīryeṣa paricchinno'pi sarvagaḥ || 544 ||
verses.colloquial:
api kurvan akurvaanash cha abhoktaa phala bhogya api |
shariiry apy ashariiry esha paricchinno api sarvagah || 544 ||
verses.translation_reworded: He acts, yet he is inactive. He experiences the fruits of past actions, yet they do not touch him. He has a body, yet does not identify with it. He seems limited, yet he is omnipresent.

verses.sanskrit:
अशरीरं सदा सन्तमिमं ब्रह्मविदं क्वचित् ।
प्रियाप्रिये न स्पृशतस्तथैव च शुभाशुभे ॥ ५४५ ॥
verses.roman:
aśarīraṃ sadā santamimaṃ brahmavidaṃ kvacit |
priyāpriye na spṛśatastathaiva ca śubhāśubhe || 545 ||
verses.colloquial:
ashariram sadaa santam imam brahma vidam kvacit |
priya apriye na sprishatas tathaa eva ca shubha ashubhe || 545 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Neither pleasure nor pain, neither good nor evil, ever touches this knower of Brahman, who lives constantly without the idea of being a body.

verses.sanskrit:
स्थूलादिसंबन्धवतोऽभिमानिनः सुखं च दुःखं च शुभाशुभे च ।
विध्वस्तबन्धस्य सदात्मनो मुनेः कुतः शुभं वाप्यशुभं फलं वा ॥ ५४६ ॥
verses.roman:
sthūlādisaṃbandhavato'bhimāninaḥ sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca śubhāśubhe ca |
vidhvastabandhasya sadātmano muneḥ kutaḥ śubhaṃ vāpyaśubhaṃ phalaṃ vā || 546 ||
verses.colloquial:
sthuula aadi sambandha vato abhimaaninah sukham ca duhkham ca shubha ashubhe ca |
vidhvasta bandhasya sada aatmano muneh kutah shubham vaa api ashubham phalam vaa || 546 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Pleasure and pain, good and evil, affect only the one who is connected with the gross body and the like and who identifies with them. How can good or evil, or what they bring, touch the sage who has identified with the Reality and so has shattered his bondage?

verses.sanskrit:
तमसा ग्रस्तवद्भानादग्रस्तोऽपि रविर्जनैः ।
ग्रस्त इत्युच्यते भ्रान्त्यां ह्यज्ञात्वा वस्तुलक्षणम् ॥ ५४७ ॥
verses.roman:
tamasā grastavadbhānādagrasto'pi ravirjanaiḥ |
grasta ityucyate bhrāntyāṃ hyajñātvā vastulakṣaṇam || 547 ||
verses.colloquial:
tamasaa grasta vad bhaanaad agrasto api ravir janaihi |
grasta iti ucyate bhraantyaam hi ajnaatvaa vastu lakshanam || 547 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Rāhu appears to swallow the sun but does not actually do so. People who do not know the sun's real nature say, out of delusion, that it has been swallowed.

verses.sanskrit:
तद्वद्देहादिबन्धेभ्यो विमुक्तं ब्रह्मवित्तमम् ।
पश्यन्ति देहिवन्मूढाः शरीराभासदर्शनात् ॥ ५४८ ॥
verses.roman:
tadvaddehādibandhebhyo vimuktaṃ brahmavittamam |
paśyanti dehivanmūḍhāḥ śarīrābhāsadarśanāt || 548 ||
verses.colloquial:
tadvat deha aadi bandhebhyo vimuktam brahma vittamam |
pashyanti dehivat muudhaah shariira aabhaasa darshanaat || 548 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In the same way, ignorant people regard the perfect knower of Brahman, who is wholly rid of the bonds of the body and the like, as having a body, because they see only an appearance of one.

verses.sanskrit:
अहिर्निर्ल्वयनीं वायं मुक्त्वा देहं तु तिष्ठति ।
इतस्ततश्चाल्यमानो यत्किंचित्प्राणवायुना ॥ ५४९ ॥
verses.roman:
ahirnirlvayanīṃ vāyaṃ muktvā dehaṃ tu tiṣṭhati |
itastataścālyamāno yatkiṃcitprāṇavāyunā || 549 ||
verses.colloquial:
ahir nirlvayanim vaayam muktvaa deham tu tishthati |
itas tatash chaalyamaano yat kimchit praana vaayunaa || 549 ||
verses.translation_reworded: In truth he rests, having cast off the body as a snake casts off its slough, and the force of the Prāṇa moves the body about wherever it will.

verses.sanskrit:
स्त्रोतसा नीयते दारु यथा निम्नोन्नतस्थलम् ।
दैवेन नीयते देहो यथाकालोपभुक्तिषु ॥ ५५0 ॥
verses.roman:
strotasā nīyate dāru yathā nimnonnatasthalam |
daivena nīyate deho yathākālopabhuktiṣu || 550 ||
verses.colloquial:
strotasaa niiyate daaru yathaa nimna unnata sthalam |
daivena niiyate deho yathaa kaala upabhuktishu || 550 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As a current carries a piece of wood now to high ground and now to low, so the momentum of past actions carries his body along to the varied experience of their fruits, as these arrive in due course.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रारब्धकर्मपरिकल्पितवासनाभिः संसारिवच्चरति भुक्तिषु मुक्तदेहः ।
सिद्धः स्वयं वसति साक्षिवदत्र तूष्णीं चक्रस्य मूलमिव कल्पविकल्पशून्यः ॥ ५५१ ॥
verses.roman:
prārabdhakarmaparikalpitavāsanābhiḥ saṃsārivaccarati bhuktiṣu muktadehaḥ |
siddhaḥ svayaṃ vasati sākṣivadatra tūṣṇīṃ cakrasya mūlamiva kalpavikalpaśūnyaḥ || 551 ||
verses.colloquial:
praarabdha karma parikalpita vaasanaabhih samsaari vat charati bhuktishu mukta dehah |
siddhah svayam vasati saakshi vat atra tuushniim chakrasya muulam iva kalpa vikalpa shuunyah || 551 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The man of realization, having lost the idea of being a body, moves among sense-enjoyments like someone subject to transmigration, through desires produced by Prārabdha work. But he himself stays unmoved in the body, like a witness, free of mental wavering, like the pivot of a potter's wheel.

verses.sanskrit:
नैवेन्द्रियाणि विषयेषु नियुङ्क्त एष नैवापयुङ्क्त उप्दर्शनलक्षणस्थः ।
नैव क्रियाफलमपीषदवेक्षते स स्वानन्दसान्द्ररसपानसुमत्तचित्तः ॥ ५५२ ॥
verses.roman:
naivendriyāṇi viṣayeṣu niyuṅkta eṣa naivāpayuṅkta updarśanalakṣaṇasthaḥ |
naiva kriyāphalamapīṣadavekṣate sa svānandasāndrarasapānasumattacittaḥ || 552 ||
verses.colloquial:
na eva indriyaani vishayeshu niyunkta esha na eva apayunkta upadarshana lakshana sthah |
na eva kriyaa phalam api iishat avekshate sa sva aananda saandra rasa paana sumatta chittah || 552 ||
verses.translation_reworded: He neither sends his sense-organs toward their objects nor pulls them back, but remains like an unconcerned spectator. He has no regard whatever for the fruits of actions, for his mind is thoroughly intoxicated from drinking the pure elixir of the Bliss of Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
लक्ष्यालक्ष्यगतिं त्यक्त्वा यस्तिष्ठेत्केवलात्मना ।
शिव एव स्वयं साक्षादयं ब्रह्मविदुत्तमः ॥ ५५३ ॥
verses.roman:
lakṣyālakṣyagatiṃ tyaktvā yastiṣṭhetkevalātmanā |
śiva eva svayaṃ sākṣādayaṃ brahmaviduttamaḥ || 553 ||
verses.colloquial:
lakshya alakshya gatim tyaktvaa yas tishthet kevala aatmanaa |
shiva eva svayam saakshaat ayam brahma vit uttamah || 553 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One who gives up all such thoughts as "this is fit for meditation and this is not" and lives as the absolute Ātman is truly Śiva himself, and he is the finest of the Knowers of Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
जीवन्नेव सदा मुक्तः कृतार्थो ब्रह्मवित्तमः ।
उपाधिनाशाद्ब्रह्मैव सन् ब्रह्माप्येति निर्द्वयम् ॥ ५५४ ॥
verses.roman:
jīvanneva sadā muktaḥ kṛtārtho brahmavittamaḥ |
upādhināśādbrahmaiva san brahmāpyeti nirdvayam || 554 ||
verses.colloquial:
jiivan eva sadaa muktah kritaartho brahma vit tamah |
upaadhi naashaat brahma eva san brahma apyeti nirdvayam || 554 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When the adjuncts that had come upon him are destroyed, the perfect knower of Brahman merges into the One Brahman without a second, which he has been all along. He becomes wholly free while still living and reaches the fulfilment of his life.

verses.sanskrit:
शैलूषो वेषसद्भावा भावयोश्च यथा पुमान् ।
तथैव ब्रह्मविच्छ्रेष्ठः सदा ब्रह्मैव नापरः ॥ ५५५ ॥
verses.roman:
śailūṣo veṣasadbhāvā bhāvayośca yathā pumān |
tathaiva brahmavicchreṣṭhaḥ sadā brahmaiva nāparaḥ || 555 ||
verses.colloquial:
shailuusho vesha sadbhaavaa bhaavayoshca yathaa pumaan |
tathaiva brahma vic chreshtah sadaa brahma eva na aparah || 555 ||
verses.translation_reworded: An actor remains a man whether or not he is wearing his costume. In the same way, the perfect knower of Brahman is always Brahman and nothing else.

verses.sanskrit:
यत्र क्वापि विशीर्णं सत्पर्णमिव तरोर्वपुः पततात् ।
ब्रह्मीभूतस्य यतेः प्रागेव तच्चिदग्निना दग्धम् ॥ ५५६ ॥
verses.roman:
yatra kvāpi viśīrṇaṃ satparṇamiva tarorvapuḥ patatāt |
brahmībhūtasya yateḥ prāgeva taccidagninā dagdham || 556 ||
verses.colloquial:
yatra kva api vishiirnam sat parnam iva taror vapuh patataat |
brahmii bhuutasya yateh praag eva tat cid agninaa dagdham || 556 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Let the body of the Sannyasin who has realized his identity with Brahman wither and drop anywhere, like a leaf from a tree. It matters little to him, for the fire of knowledge has already burnt it.

verses.sanskrit:
सदात्मनि ब्रह्मणि तिष्ठतो मुनेः पूर्णाद्वयानन्दमयात्मना सदा ।
न देशकालाद्युचितप्रतीक्षा त्वङ्मांसविट्पिण्डविसर्जनाय ॥ ५५७ ॥
verses.roman:
sadātmani brahmaṇi tiṣṭhato muneḥ pūrṇādvayānandamayātmanā sadā |
na deśakālādyucitapratīkṣā tvaṅmāṃsaviṭpiṇḍavisarjanāya || 557 ||
verses.colloquial:
sadaa aatmani brahmani tishthato muneh puurnaa advaya aananda maya aatmanaa sadaa |
na desha kaala aadi ucita pratiikshaa tvak maamsa vit pinda visarjanaaya || 557 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The sage who lives always in the Reality, Brahman, as Infinite Bliss, the One without a second, does not rely on the usual considerations of place, time, and so on when giving up this heap of skin, flesh, and filth.

verses.sanskrit:
देहस्य मोक्षो नो मोक्षो न दण्डस्य कमण्डलोः ।
अविद्याहृदयग्रन्थिमोक्षो मोक्षो यतस्ततः ॥ ५५८ ॥
verses.roman:
dehasya mokṣo no mokṣo na daṇḍasya kamaṇḍaloḥ |
avidyāhṛdayagranthimokṣo mokṣo yatastataḥ || 558 ||
verses.colloquial:
dehasya moksho no moksho na dandasya kamandaloh |
avidyaa hridaya granthi moksho moksho yatas tatah || 558 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Liberation is not giving up the body, nor giving up the staff and water-bowl. Liberation is the destruction of the heart's knot, which is Nescience.

verses.sanskrit:
कुल्यायामथ नद्यां वा शिवक्षेत्रेऽपि चत्वरे ।
पर्णं पतति चेत्तेन तरोः किं नु शुभाशुभम् ॥ ५५९ ॥
verses.roman:
kulyāyāmatha nadyāṃ vā śivakṣetre'pi catvare |
parṇaṃ patati cettena taroḥ kiṃ nu śubhāśubham || 559 ||
verses.colloquial:
kulyaayaam atha nadyaam vaa shiva kshetre api catvare |
parnam patati cet tena taroh kim nu shubha ashubham || 559 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Whether a leaf falls into a small stream, a river, a place consecrated by Shiva, or a crossroads, what good or harm does that do the tree?

verses.sanskrit:
पत्रस्य पुष्पस्य फलस्य नाशवद् देहेन्द्रियप्राणधियां विनाशः ।
नैवात्मनः स्वस्य सदात्मकस्या नन्दाकृतेर्वृक्षवदस्ति चैषः ॥ ५६0 ॥
verses.roman:
patrasya puṣpasya phalasya nāśavad dehendriyaprāṇadhiyāṃ vināśaḥ |
naivātmanaḥ svasya sadātmakasyā nandākṛtervṛkṣavadasti caiṣaḥ || 560 ||
verses.colloquial:
patrasya pushpasya phalasya naashavad deha indriya praana dhiyaam vinaashaha |
na eva aatmanaha svasya sadaatmakasyaa nanda aakriter vrikshavad asti ca eshaha || 560 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The destruction of the body, organs, Prāṇas, and Buddhi is like the loss of a leaf, flower, or fruit to a tree. It does not affect the Ātman, the Reality, the Embodiment of Bliss, which is one's true nature. That lives on, as the tree does.

verses.sanskrit:
प्रज्ञानघन इत्यात्मलक्षणं सत्यसूचकम् ।
अनूद्यौपाधिकस्यैव कथयन्ति विनाशनम् ॥ ५६१ ॥
verses.roman:
prajñānaghana ityātmalakṣaṇaṃ satyasūcakam |
anūdyaupādhikasyaiva kathayanti vināśanam || 561 ||
verses.colloquial:
prajnaana ghana iti aatma lakshanam satya suuchakam |
anuudya aupaadhikasya eva kathayanti vinaashanam || 561 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Śrutis set out the real nature of the Ātman in words such as "The Embodiment of Knowledge," which point to Its Reality, and they speak of the destruction of the apparent limitations only.

verses.sanskrit:
अविनाशी वा अरेऽयमात्मेति श्रुतिरात्मनः ।
प्रब्रवीत्यविनाशित्वं विनश्यत्सु विकारिषु ॥ ५६२ ॥
verses.roman:
avināśī vā are'yamātmeti śrutirātmanaḥ |
prabravītyavināśitvaṃ vinaśyatsu vikāriṣu || 562 ||
verses.colloquial:
avinaashii vaa are ayam aatmaa iti shrutir aatmanah |
prabraviiiti avinaashitvam vinashyatsu vikarishu || 562 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The Śruti passage "Truly this Ātman is immortal, my dear" states the immortality of the Ātman among things that perish and undergo change.

verses.sanskrit:
पाषाणवृक्षतृणधान्यकडङ्कराद्या दग्धा भवन्ति हि मृदेव यथा तथैव ।
देहेन्द्रियासुमन आदि समस्तदृश्यं ज्ञानाग्निदग्धमुपयाति परात्मभावम् ॥ ५६३ ॥
verses.roman:
pāṣāṇavṛkṣatṛṇadhānyakaḍaṅkarādyā dagdhā bhavanti hi mṛdeva yathā tathaiva |
dehendriyāsumana ādi samastadṛśyaṃ jñānāgnidagdhamupayāti parātmabhāvam || 563 ||
verses.colloquial:
paashaana vriksha trina dhaanya kadangara aadyaa dagdhaa bhavanti hi mrid eva yathaa tathaiva |
deha indriya asu manah aadi samasta drishyam jnaana agni dagdham upayaati para aatma bhaavam || 563 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When stone, tree, grass, paddy, husk, and so on are burnt, they become nothing but earth (ashes). In the same way, the entire objective universe, including the body, organs, Prāṇas, Manas, and the rest, is reduced to the Supreme Self when burnt by the fire of realization.

verses.sanskrit:
विलक्षणं यथा ध्वान्तं लीयते भानुतेजसि ।
तथैव सकलं दृश्यं ब्रह्मणि प्रविलीयते ॥ ५६४ ॥
verses.roman:
vilakṣaṇaṃ yathā dhvāntaṃ līyate bhānutejasi |
tathaiva sakalaṃ dṛśyaṃ brahmaṇi pravilīyate || 564 ||
verses.colloquial:
vilakshanam yathaa dhvaantam liiyate bhaanu tejasi |
tathaa eva sakalam drishyam brahmani praviliiyate || 564 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Just as darkness, which is distinct from sunshine, vanishes in the sun's radiance, so the entire objective universe dissolves in Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
घटे नष्टे यथा व्योम व्योमैव भवति स्फुटम् ।
तथैवोपाधिविलये ब्रह्मैव ब्रह्मवित्स्वयम् ॥ ५६५ ॥
verses.roman:
ghaṭe naṣṭe yathā vyoma vyomaiva bhavati sphuṭam |
tathaivopādhivilaye brahmaiva brahmavitsvayam || 565 ||
verses.colloquial:
ghate nashte yathaa vyoma vyoma eva bhavati sphutam |
tathaiva upaadhi vilaye brahma eva brahma vit svayam || 565 ||
verses.translation_reworded: When a jar breaks, the space it enclosed is plainly the limitless space. In the same way, when the apparent limitations are destroyed, the knower of Brahman truly becomes Brahman Itself.

verses.sanskrit:
क्षीरं क्षीरे यथा क्षिप्तं तैलं तैले जलं जले ।
संयुक्तमेकतां याति तथात्मन्यात्मविन्मुनिः ॥ ५६६ ॥
verses.roman:
kṣīraṃ kṣīre yathā kṣiptaṃ tailaṃ taile jalaṃ jale |
saṃyuktamekatāṃ yāti tathātmanyātmavinmuniḥ || 566 ||
verses.colloquial:
kshiiram kshiire yathaa kshiptam tailam taile jalam jale |
samyuktam ekataam yaati tathaa aatmani aatmavit munih || 566 ||
verses.translation_reworded: As milk poured into milk, oil into oil, or water into water blends and becomes one with it, so the sage who has realized the Ātman becomes one in the Ātman.

verses.sanskrit:
एवं विदेहकैवल्यं सन्मात्रत्वमखण्डितम् ।
ब्रह्मभावं प्रपद्यैष यतिर्नावर्तते पुनः ॥ ५६७ ॥
verses.roman:
evaṃ videhakaivalyaṃ sanmātratvamakhaṇḍitam |
brahmabhāvaṃ prapadyaiṣa yatirnāvartate punaḥ || 567 ||
verses.colloquial:
evam videha kaivalyam san maatra tvam akhanditam |
brahma bhaavam prapadya esha yatir na aavartate punah || 567 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Having thus realized the utter isolation that comes from being without a body, and having become forever identified with the Absolute Reality, Brahman, the sage suffers transmigration no more.

verses.sanskrit:
सदात्मैकत्वविज्ञानदग्धाविद्यादिवर्ष्मणः ।
अमुष्य ब्रह्मभूतत्वाद्ब्रह्मणः कुत उद्भवः ॥ ५६८ ॥
verses.roman:
sadātmaikatvavijñānadagdhāvidyādivarṣmaṇaḥ |
amuṣya brahmabhūtatvādbrahmaṇaḥ kuta udbhavaḥ || 568 ||
verses.colloquial:
sadaa atma ekatva vijnaana dagdha avidya aadi varshmana |
amusya brahma bhuutatvaat brahmana kuta udbhava || 568 ||
verses.translation_reworded: His bodies, made of Nescience and the rest, have been burnt by the realization that the Jīva and Brahman are one, so he becomes Brahman Itself. And how could Brahman ever be reborn?

verses.sanskrit:
मायाकॢप्तौ बन्धमोक्षौ न स्तः स्वात्मनि वस्तुतः ।
यथा रज्जौ निष्क्रियायां सर्पाभासविनिर्गमौ ॥ ५६९ ॥
verses.roman:
māyākḷptau bandhamokṣau na staḥ svātmani vastutaḥ |
yathā rajjau niṣkriyāyāṃ sarpābhāsavinirgamau || 569 ||
verses.colloquial:
maayaa kliptau bandha mokshau na stah svaatmani vastutah |
yathaa rajjau nishkriyaayaam sarpa aabhaasa vinirgamau || 569 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Bondage and Liberation are conjured up by Māyā and do not truly exist in the Ātman, one's Reality. The snake's appearing and departing likewise do not belong to the rope, which never changes.

verses.sanskrit:
आवृतेः सदसत्त्वाभ्यां वक्तव्ये बन्धमोक्षणे ।
नावृतिर्ब्रह्मणः काचिदन्याभावादनावृतम् यद्यस्त्यद्वैतहानिः स्याद्द्वैतं नो सहते श्रुतिः ॥ ५७0 ॥
verses.roman:
āvṛteḥ sadasattvābhyāṃ vaktavye bandhamokṣaṇe |
nāvṛtirbrahmaṇaḥ kācidanyābhāvādanāvṛtam yadyastyadvaitahāniḥ syāddvaitaṃ no sahate śrutiḥ || 570 ||
verses.colloquial:
aavriteh sad asattvabhyaam vaktavye bandha moksane |
na aavritir brahmanah kaachid anya abhaavaat anaavritam yadi asti advaita haanih syaat dvaitam no sahate shrutih || 570 ||
verses.translation_reworded: One might speak of bondage and Liberation where a covering veil is present or absent. But Brahman can have no covering veil, since It is always uncovered, there being no second thing besides Itself. If there were a veil, the non-duality of Brahman would be contradicted, and the Śrutis can never tolerate duality.

verses.sanskrit:
बन्धञ्च मोक्षञ्च मृषैव मूढा बुद्धेर्गुणं वस्तुनि कल्पयन्ति ।
दृगावृतिं मेघकृतां यथा रवौ यतोऽद्वयासङ्गचिदेतदक्षरम् ॥ ५७१ ॥
verses.roman:
bandhañca mokṣañca mṛṣaiva mūḍhā buddherguṇaṃ vastuni kalpayanti |
dṛgāvṛtiṃ meghakṛtāṃ yathā ravau yato'dvayāsaṅgacidetadakṣaram || 571 ||
verses.colloquial:
bandham cha moksham cha mrisha eva muudhaa buddher gunam vastuni kalpayanti |
drig aavritim megha kritaam yathaa ravau yato advaya asanga chit etat aksharam || 571 ||
verses.translation_reworded: Bondage and Liberation are attributes of the Buddhi, which ignorant people falsely superimpose on the Reality, just as a cloud's covering of the eyes is attributed to the sun. For this Immutable Brahman is Knowledge Absolute, the One without a second, and unattached.

verses.sanskrit:
अस्तीति प्रत्ययो यश्च यश्च नास्तीति वस्तुनि ।
बुद्धेरेव गुणावेतौ न तु नित्यस्य वस्तुनः ॥ ५७२ ॥
verses.roman:
astīti pratyayo yaśca yaśca nāstīti vastuni |
buddhereva guṇāvetau na tu nityasya vastunaḥ || 572 ||
verses.colloquial:
asti iti pratyayo yashca yashca na asti iti vastuni |
buddher eva gunaa etau na tu nityasya vastunah || 572 ||
verses.translation_reworded: The idea that bondage exists and the idea that it does not are, with regard to the Reality, both merely attributes of the Buddhi. They never belong to the Eternal Reality, Brahman.

verses.sanskrit:
